def validate_segment_levels(axis: AxisMeta, node_id: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Refuse a segment axis whose levels are not the known tiers.

    Strict on purpose: every number in a segmentation sheet is labeled with one
    of these names, and a reader has no way to tell a mislabeled column from a
    correct one. A run whose segments are ``S1..S4`` produces a sheet that
    looks authoritative and says nothing.
    """
    if set(axis.levels) != set(SEGMENT_TIERS):
        raise ValueError(
            f"segment axis {axis.name!r}"
            + (f" on node {node_id!r}" if node_id else "")
            + f" has levels {list(axis.levels)!r}, which are not the readiness "
            f"tiers {list(SEGMENT_TIERS)!r}. A highlight sheet labels every "
            "number with a tier name, so it cannot be written from levels it "
            "cannot name."
        )
rationale: Checks that readiness tier labels are known before writing labeled numbers.

def sheet_frame(array: StructuredArray, seg_axis: AxisMeta) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """``array`` collapsed to the sheet's columns, tiers across the top.

    Collapses by ``per_capita``: the shares are the ``rate`` family, so this is
    ``sum(share * pop) / sum(pop)`` -- the share of the *people* in each tier,
    which is the number the sheet claims. Population comes from the array (the
    result attaches it from the population special), and broadcasts across the
    segment axis it does not have.

    An array whose axes are already the sheet's columns is written as it stands.
    Weighting is how you collapse an axis, so a fit with no axis to collapse
    needs no weights, and asking for them would refuse a genderless
    segmentation over a pointer it has no use for.
    """
    keep = tuple(
        name
        for name in (*SHEET_AXES, seg_axis.name)
        if name in array.axis_names
    )
    reduced = (
        array
        if set(keep) == set(array.axis_names)
        else array.per_capita(keep_disaggregated=keep)
    )
    long = _long_frame(reduced)
    return _tiers_across(long, seg_axis.name, tuple(seg_axis.levels))
rationale: Reduces to display axes with population weights and pivots tiers into sheet columns.

def latest_year(levels: Iterable[Any], *, now: datetime | None = None) -> Any:
    """The greatest year level not later than ``now``'s year.

    A fit's year axis usually runs past the present (the panel is projected
    forward), and a "this year" sheet showing a projection would be read as a
    measurement. Raises rather than falling back to the maximum level, because
    the fallback is the failure mode.
    """
    this_year = (now or datetime.now()).year
    candidates = [level for level in levels if int(level) <= this_year]
    if not candidates:
        raise ValueError(
            f"no year level at or before {this_year}; the year axis holds "
            f"{sorted(levels)!r}, so there is no single year to report as the "
            "present one"
        )
    return max(candidates, key=int)
rationale: Chooses the latest observed year no later than the current year and rejects an empty eligible set.

def latest_tracker(directory: Path | str | None = None) -> Path:
    """The most recent dated tracker workbook in ``directory``.

    Newest by filename, which works because the date is written ``YYYYMMDD``
    and sorts lexically. Raises when there is none: a tracker highlight with no
    tracker has nothing to say, and an empty sheet would not admit that.
    """
    directory = Path(directory) if directory is not None else TRACKER_DIR
    found = sorted(directory.glob(TRACKER_GLOB))
    if not found:
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"no tracker matching {TRACKER_GLOB!r} in {directory}; the tracker "
            "highlights read the availability workbook and cannot be written "
            "without it"
        )
    return found[-1]
rationale: Finds the latest matching tracker workbook and reports missing input.

def read_tracker(path: Path | str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The tracker's national sheet, cut to :data:`TRACKER_COLUMNS`.

    Rows with no indicator code are dropped: the sheet interleaves category
    banner rows among the indicator rows, and they carry a category and nothing
    else.
    """
    path = Path(path) if path is not None else latest_tracker()
    frame = pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name=TRACKER_SHEET, header=TRACKER_HEADER_ROW)
    missing = [name for name in TRACKER_COLUMNS if name not in frame.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(
            f"tracker {path.name!r} sheet {TRACKER_SHEET!r} has no column(s) "
            f"{missing!r}; the highlight indexes on them, so a renamed column "
            "is a silently empty sheet"
        )
    frame = frame[list(TRACKER_COLUMNS)].rename(columns=TRACKER_COLUMNS)
    return frame[frame["indicator"].notna()].reset_index(drop=True)
rationale: Selects the workbook schema, validates columns, renames fields, and drops empty indicators.
Extracts data-feed metadata from graph nodes and rejects graphs without observations.

def indicator_table(graph: Any, tracker: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The model's (indicator, source) pairs, described by the tracker.

    A left join, so a pair the tracker does not list still appears -- with the
    tracker columns blank and ``in_tracker`` false. That is a fact worth
    reporting rather than a row worth dropping: it says the model reads
    something the tracker does not know about.

    Refuses only when an ambiguity reaches this join. The tracker does list some
    pairs twice, but a duplicate among rows the model never reads is the
    tracker's business, not this sheet's.
    """
    observations = model_observations(graph)
    wanted = set(zip(observations["indicator"], observations["source"]))
    described = tracker[
        [pair in wanted for pair in zip(tracker["indicator"], tracker["source"])]
    ]
    duplicated = described[described.duplicated(subset=["indicator", "source"])]
    if len(duplicated):
        pairs = sorted(set(zip(duplicated["indicator"], duplicated["source"])))
        raise ValueError(
            f"the tracker lists {pairs!r} more than once, and the model reads "
            "them; the join has no one description to attach, and would pick a "
            "row arbitrarily"
        )
    table = observations.merge(described, on=["indicator", "source"], how="left")
    table["in_tracker"] = table["category"].notna()
    return table
rationale: Joins graph observations to tracker feeds and rejects ambiguous duplicate descriptions.

def cluster_coverage(graph: Any, tracker: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per (category, cluster): how many of the tracker's indicators the model uses.

    Counted over distinct indicator *codes*, not rows, because the tracker lists
    one row per (indicator, source) and two sources for one indicator is one
    indicator. Every tracker group appears, including those the model draws
    nothing from -- a zero is the answer to "how representative is this?".
    """
    used = set(model_observations(graph)["indicator"])
    frame = tracker.assign(in_model=tracker["indicator"].isin(used))
    grouped = frame.groupby(["category", "cluster"], dropna=False).agg(
        indicators_in_tracker=("indicator", "nunique"),
        indicators_in_model=("indicator", lambda s: s[frame.loc[s.index, "in_model"]].nunique()),
    )
    return grouped.reset_index().sort_values(
        ["indicators_in_model", "category", "cluster"],
        ascending=[False, True, True],
        ignore_index=True,
    )
rationale: Aggregates tracker and model coverage by category and cluster.
Flattens tensor values alongside the named coordinate product.

source:
def _tiers_across(long: pd.DataFrame, seg_name: str, tiers: tuple[str, ...]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Pivot the segment axis to columns in ladder order, and add the total.

    Reindexing to ``tiers`` rather than taking pandas' sort keeps the ladder
    order the axis declared; a sheet whose columns read
    ``full_ai_ready, small_ai_ready, ...`` inverts the thing being shown.
    """
    index = [c for c in long.columns if c not in (seg_name, "value")]
    wide = long.pivot(index=index, columns=seg_name, values="value")
    wide = wide.reindex(columns=list(tiers))
    wide.columns.name = None
    if len(tiers) == 4:
        wide[TOTAL_AI_READY] = wide[tiers[-2]] + wide[tiers[-1]]
    return wide.reset_index()
rationale: Pivots ordered tiers and derives the total-ready field.

def level_set_suffix(levels: Sequence[Any]) -> str:
    """A short digest of an *ordered* level list, stable across processes.

    Same suffix if and only if same coordinate list -- so the two orderings of
    one pair differ, since they are two different coord lists and putting them
    on one dim name would recreate the collision the suffix removes.

    Cross-process stability is the requirement, which rules out ``hash()``
    (Python salts string hashes per run). It matters because the suffix reaches
    places the wrapper does not front: saved netCDF files compared across runs,
    arviz's plotting functions, and the ``.posterior`` escape hatch.
    """
    canon = _LEVEL_SEP.join(_tagged(level) for level in levels)
    return hashlib.blake2s(canon.encode("utf-8"), digest_size=3).hexdigest()
rationale: Creates a stable short digest from typed level encodings.
Preserves level type distinctions during canonical serialization.

source:
def level_text(level: Any) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """One level as ``(type tag, text)``, invertible by ``parse_level``.

    The tag vocabulary is the digest's, because the distinction a written level
    has to preserve is exactly the one that makes two level sets different --
    a second vocabulary would let a file and a dim name disagree about whether
    ``2019`` and ``"2019"`` are the same level. It comes back *separated* from
    the text so a caller can hoist it: a file that declares its axis's type once
    can then hold plain ``KE``, not ``s:KE``.
    """
    tagged = _tagged(level)
    tag, _, body = tagged.partition(":")
    if tag not in _UNTAG:
        raise TypeError(
            f"level {level!r} of type {type(level).__name__} has no written "
            "form that reads back as itself; give the axis levels of a type "
            f"the writer knows ({', '.join(sorted(_UNTAG))})"
        )
    return tag, body
rationale: Checks round-trip support and splits encoded levels into a tag and value.
Validates the stored type tag before dispatching its parser.

def to_inference_data(sampled: Mapping[str, StructuredArray]) -> object:
    """Assemble a single-draw posterior ``DataTree`` from a node->array map.

    Parameters
    ----------
    sampled
        The compiled model's return value: ``node_id -> StructuredArray`` for
        every node (latent and deterministic), with values already substituted
        at the MAP point.

    Returns
    -------
    The ArviZ container (an xarray ``DataTree`` under ArviZ 1.x). Each node
    becomes a posterior variable named by its ``node_id``, with the node's
    ``AxisMeta`` axes as named dims/coords and leading ``(chain, draw)`` dims
    of length 1.

    An axis name carrying two different level lists is split into one suffixed
    dim per level set; a name that is unambiguous across the whole map keeps its
    bare form, which is what every existing ``.sel(country=...)`` addresses.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Defensively, if any node's array shape disagrees with its declared axis
        lengths.
    """
    # First pass: validate, and learn which axis names carry more than one
    # level list. Ambiguity is a property of the whole map, but the *suffix* is
    # a function of the level set alone -- so a dim name does not change when an
    # unrelated node joins the graph, and yesterday's saved output still lines
    # up with today's.
    prepared: list[tuple[str, np.ndarray, list[str], dict[str, list]]] = []
    for node_id, sa in sampled.items():
        array = np.asarray(sa.array)
        dim_names, node_coords = _dims_and_coords(array, sa.axes, name=node_id)
        # Single-draw MAP posterior: prepend (chain=1, draw=1). ArviZ treats
        # the first two unlisted dims as the sample dims, so `dims` lists only
        # the domain axes.
        prepared.append(
            (node_id, array[np.newaxis, np.newaxis, ...], dim_names, node_coords)
        )
    return assemble_posterior(prepared)
rationale: Validates structured dimensions and adds MAP chain and draw dimensions.
Disambiguates dimension names when nodes use distinct level sets before assembling ArviZ data.

def read_posterior(
    idata: Any,
) -> list[tuple[str, np.ndarray, list[str], dict[str, list]]]:
    """Recover ``assemble_posterior``'s input from a container it built.

    The inverse of the suffixing, so a reader never has to carry a digest of its
    own: a trailing ``__xxxxxx`` is stripped only when it is *verified* to be the
    digest of that dim's own coordinate list. An axis genuinely named with a
    double underscore therefore survives, and so does one whose levels happen to
    end in six hex characters -- the check is on the digest, not on the shape of
    the text.
    """
    posterior = idata["posterior"] if "posterior" in idata else idata.posterior
    dataset = getattr(posterior, "dataset", posterior)
    out: list[tuple[str, np.ndarray, list[str], dict[str, list]]] = []
    for node_id in dataset.data_vars:
        variable = dataset[node_id]
        names: list[str] = []
        node_coords: dict[str, list] = {}
        # The first two dims are (chain, draw); the rest are the domain axes.
        for dim in variable.dims[2:]:
            levels = [_native(level) for level in variable.coords[dim].values]
            bare = _bare_dim(str(dim), levels)
            names.append(bare)
            node_coords[bare] = levels
        out.append((node_id, np.asarray(variable.values), names, node_coords))
    return out
rationale: Extracts node arrays and restores native levels and bare dimension names.
Removes a suffix only when it matches the actual coordinate-level digest.
Converts NumPy scalars while leaving ordinary Python values unchanged.
Adds a level-set suffix only for ambiguous dimension names.

source:
def _dims_and_coords(
    array: np.ndarray,
    axes: Sequence[AxisMeta],
    *,
    name: str,
) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, list]]:
    """Validate one array against its axes and extract dim names + coords.

    Kept separate from ``to_inference_data`` so the shape/axis contract is
    independently exercisable on a bare ``(array, axes)`` pair -- a
    ``StructuredArray`` enforces this at construction, but the converter
    re-checks defensively so a future bare-array path can't silently mislabel
    dims.
    """
    if array.ndim != len(axes):
        raise ValueError(
            f"node {name!r}: array has {array.ndim} dims but {len(axes)} "
            "axes were declared"
        )
    dim_names: list[str] = []
    coords: dict[str, list] = {}
    for i, axis in enumerate(axes):
        if array.shape[i] != len(axis.levels):
            raise ValueError(
                f"node {name!r}: axis {axis.name!r} declares "
                f"{len(axis.levels)} levels but array dimension {i} has "
                f"length {array.shape[i]}"
            )
        dim_names.append(axis.name)
        coords[axis.name] = list(axis.levels)
    return dim_names, coords
rationale: Validates axis rank and lengths and builds labeled dimension coordinates.

def run_map(
    model: Any,
    graph: BayesGraph,
    observations: Observations | None = None,
    *,
    steps: int = DEFAULT_STEPS,
    lr: float = DEFAULT_LR,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> InferenceResult:
    """Fit a MAP point estimate and wrap it as a labeled ``InferenceResult``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model
        A compiled model from ``compile_model(graph)``. Drives both the fit and
        the post-fit replay.
    graph
        The graph the model was compiled from. Not retained on the result, save
        for each node's ``specials`` (see ``InferenceResult``).
    observations
        Optional evidence container. When omitted, fits the prior-only model
        (the v0 walking skeleton, before any observation node exists).
    steps, lr
        SVI step count and Adam learning rate.
    seed
        PRNG seed; the same seed reproduces the same MAP estimate.

    Returns
    -------
    InferenceResult
        A single-draw posterior carrying every latent and deterministic site,
        labeled by the graph's axis metadata.
    """
    guide = AutoDelta(model)
    svi = infer.SVI(
        model, guide, numpyro.optim.Adam(lr), loss=infer.Trace_ELBO()
    )
    key = jax.random.PRNGKey(seed)
    svi_result = svi.run(
        key, steps, progress_bar=False, observations=observations
    )

    # MAP point: the AutoDelta guide's median is its single learned location,
    # returned in the model's original (constrained) space -- ready to
    # substitute directly back into the model's sample sites.
    map_point = guide.median(svi_result.params)

    # Replay at the MAP point to (a) surface deterministic sites the fit never
    # optimized and (b) read back each site's axis metadata. `substitute`
    # pins the latent sites; `seed` defensively supplies an RNG for any site
    # not covered by the MAP point (observed sites take their evidence value).
    replay = handlers.seed(handlers.substitute(model, map_point), key)
    sampled = replay(observations=observations)

    # The map is the result: it is what the replay above went to the trouble of
    # recovering, and the ArviZ container is one view of it (built on demand).
    # The graph's specials come along -- the one part of it a result keeps, and
    # the part a downstream reader cannot rebuild (see `InferenceResult`).
    specials = {
        meta.node_id: meta.specials
        for meta in graph.nodes()
        if meta.specials and meta.node_id in sampled
    }
    return InferenceResult(
        sampled, specials=specials, losses=np.asarray(svi_result.losses)
    )
rationale: Fits an AutoDelta guide, replays the fitted graph, and packages labeled results.

def run_nuts(
    model: Callable[..., Any],
    observations: Observations | None = None,
    *,
    num_warmup: int = 1000,
    num_samples: int = 1000,
    num_chains: int = 4,
    seed: int = DEFAULT_SEED,
    target_accept_prob: float = 0.9,
    max_tree_depth: int = 10,
    chain_method: str = "sequential",
    progress_bar: bool = True,
) -> MCMC:
    """Sample all continuous latent sites, preserving the supplied evidence.

    Sequential chains work on a single device. Use vectorized chains to trade
    memory for concurrency, or parallel chains when enough JAX devices exist.
    A diagonal mass matrix is used; no MAP initialization or fitting is done.
    """
    if num_warmup < 0 or num_samples < 1 or num_chains < 1:
        raise ValueError(
            "warmup must be nonnegative; samples and chains must be positive"
        )
    if not 0.0 < target_accept_prob < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("target_accept_prob must be strictly between 0 and 1")
    if max_tree_depth < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_tree_depth must be positive")
    if chain_method not in {"sequential", "parallel", "vectorized"}:
        raise ValueError("chain_method must be sequential, parallel, or vectorized")
    if not 0 <= seed < 2**32:
        raise ValueError("seed must be an unsigned 32-bit integer")
    if chain_method == "parallel" and num_chains > jax.local_device_count():
        raise ValueError(
            f"parallel chains require {num_chains} JAX devices, but only "
            f"{jax.local_device_count()} are available; use sequential or vectorized"
        )

    key = jax.random.PRNGKey(seed)
    trace_key, sampling_key = jax.random.split(key)
    trace = handlers.trace(handlers.seed(model, trace_key)).get_trace(
        observations=observations
    )
    discrete = [
        name
        for name, site in trace.items()
        if site["type"] == "sample"
        and not site["is_observed"]
        and site["fn"].support.is_discrete
    ]
    if discrete:
        raise ValueError(
            "NUTS cannot sample unobserved discrete sites: "
            + ", ".join(discrete)
            + ". Supply fitting evidence, including constraint-zero observations."
        )

    kernel = NUTS(
        model,
        init_strategy=init_to_median(num_samples=15),
        dense_mass=False,
        target_accept_prob=target_accept_prob,
        max_tree_depth=max_tree_depth,
    )
    mcmc = MCMC(
        kernel,
        num_warmup=num_warmup,
        num_samples=num_samples,
        num_chains=num_chains,
        chain_method=chain_method,
        progress_bar=progress_bar,
    )
    mcmc.run(sampling_key, observations=observations, extra_fields=EXTRA_FIELDS)
    return mcmc
rationale: Validates chain settings and discrete sites before constructing and running NUTS.
Normalizes numerical diagnostics to finite floats or JSON-safe absence.

def save_nuts_result(
    mcmc: MCMC,
    directory: str | Path,
    *,
    max_tree_depth: int,
    metadata: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Save draws, post-warmup sampler statistics, and a diagnostic summary.

    Both NPZ archives have leading ``(chain, draw)`` axes and load without pickle.
    ``summary.csv`` uses NumPyro's ESS and split R-hat, not rank-normalized ArviZ
    diagnostics. Nonfinite summaries are blank/null rather than JSON NaN.
    Short runs with fewer than four retained draws omit summary rows entirely.
    An existing directory is refused to avoid overwriting another run.
    Supply the same tree-depth limit used for sampling.
    """
    if max_tree_depth < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_tree_depth must be positive")
    samples = {
        name: np.asarray(value)
        for name, value in mcmc.get_samples(group_by_chain=True).items()
    }
    extra = {
        name: np.asarray(value)
        for name, value in mcmc.get_extra_fields(group_by_chain=True).items()
    }
    directory = Path(directory)
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    np.savez_compressed(directory / "posterior.npz", **samples)
    np.savez_compressed(directory / "sample_stats.npz", **extra)

    with (directory / "summary.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(
            f,
            fieldnames=(
                "site",
                "index",
                "mean",
                "std",
                "median",
                "q05",
                "q95",
                "n_eff",
                "r_hat",
            ),
        )
        writer.writeheader()
        if mcmc.num_samples >= 4:
            with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
                statistics = summary(samples, prob=0.9, group_by_chain=True)
            for name, stats in statistics.items():
                for index in np.ndindex(np.shape(stats["mean"])):
                    row = {"site": name, "index": json.dumps(index)}
                    for field, key in (
                        ("mean", "mean"),
                        ("std", "std"),
                        ("median", "median"),
                        ("q05", "5.0%"),
                        ("q95", "95.0%"),
                        ("n_eff", "n_eff"),
                        ("r_hat", "r_hat"),
                    ):
                        row[field] = _finite_number(np.asarray(stats[key])[index])
                    writer.writerow(row)

    energy = extra["energy"]
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        bfmi = (
            np.mean(np.diff(energy, axis=1) ** 2, axis=1) / np.var(energy, axis=1)
            if energy.shape[1] > 1
            else np.full(energy.shape[0], np.nan)
        )
    diagnostics = {
        "divergences_by_chain": extra["diverging"].sum(axis=1).tolist(),
        "mean_accept_prob_by_chain": [
            _finite_number(value) for value in extra["accept_prob"].mean(axis=1)
        ],
        "ebfmi_by_chain": [_finite_number(value) for value in bfmi],
        "nonfinite_potential_energy_by_chain": (~np.isfinite(extra["potential_energy"]))
        .sum(axis=1)
        .tolist(),
        "tree_step_limit_hits_by_chain": (extra["num_steps"] >= 2**max_tree_depth - 1)
        .sum(axis=1)
        .tolist(),
        "tree_step_limit_note": "Step-budget hits are a proxy for tree-depth saturation.",
        "summary_note": (
            "NumPyro ESS and split R-hat; single-chain split R-hat does not assess "
            "agreement between independently initialized chains."
            if mcmc.num_samples >= 4
            else "Fewer than four draws: ESS/R-hat summary omitted."
        ),
    }
    info = {
        "metadata": dict(metadata or {}),
        "sampler": {
            "num_warmup": mcmc.num_warmup,
            "num_samples": mcmc.num_samples,
            "num_chains": mcmc.num_chains,
            "chain_method": mcmc.chain_method,
            "max_tree_depth": max_tree_depth,
        },
        "versions": {"numpyro": numpyro.__version__, "jax": jax.__version__},
        "sample_axes": ["chain", "draw"],
        "site_shapes": {name: list(value.shape) for name, value in samples.items()},
        "diagnostics": diagnostics,
    }
    with (directory / "run_info.json").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(info, f, indent=2, allow_nan=False, default=_json_scalar)
        f.write("\n")
    return directory
rationale: Saves posterior draws, sampler fields, summaries, and chain diagnostics.
Implements the json.dump default callback for NumPy scalars and rejects unsupported objects.
Implements explicit, special-tag, and legacy fallback precedence for segmentation output.
Implements explicit, special-tag, and legacy fallback precedence for population output.

def result_tables(
    result: InferenceResult,
    *,
    shares_node: str | None = None,
    population_node: str | None = None,
    segment_dim: str = "segment",
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Tidy tables from a fitted result: the reusable, D7-aligned layer.

    Returns ``{SHEET_SEGMENT_SHARES, SHEET_NATIONAL_SUMMARY, SHEET_RUN_INFO}``:

    - **segment_shares** (long): one row per cell x segment, with ``share`` and
      -- when a population node is present -- ``people = share * population``.
    - **national_summary** (wide): one row per cell, with ``population`` (if
      present), ``expected_segment`` (the population-free 1-based segment index
      weighted by share, ``sum_k k * share_k``), and one share column per
      segment level.
    - **run_info** (key/value): axis sizes, ``final_elbo_loss`` when the fit
      recorded a loss curve, and any caller-supplied ``metadata`` (e.g.
      ``generated_at``, ``seed``, ``steps``).

    Driven entirely by the result's coords -- segment / cell labels and their
    order come from the posterior, not from positional assumptions. Depends only
    on the ``InferenceResult`` (no ``BayesGraph``). When ``shares_node`` /
    ``population_node`` are omitted, each is resolved from the result's retained
    ``specials`` (``segmentation`` / ``population``), then from the demo-lineage
    ids ``segment_shares`` / ``population`` if those variables are present.
    ``people`` / ``population`` are omitted (not errored) when no population
    node resolves.
    """
    shares_node = _resolve_shares_node(result, shares_node)
    if shares_node is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "this result has no segmentation node to tabulate: none carries "
            f"the {SEGMENTATION_SPECIAL!r} special and "
            f"{_DEMO_SHARES_NODE!r} is not in the posterior "
            f"({list(result.posterior.data_vars)!r})"
        )
    population_node = _resolve_population_node(result, population_node)

    posterior = result.posterior

    # MAP point estimate: the single fitted draw. reset_coords drops the now
    # scalar chain/draw coords so they don't leak into the tidy frames.
    shares = posterior[shares_node].isel(chain=0, draw=0).reset_coords(drop=True)
    cell_dims = [d for d in shares.dims if d != segment_dim]
    seg_levels = list(shares[segment_dim].values)

    has_population = (
        population_node is not None and population_node in posterior
    )
    if has_population:
        pop = (
            posterior[population_node].isel(chain=0, draw=0).reset_coords(drop=True)
        )

    # -- segment_shares (long) --------------------------------------------------
    long_parts = [shares.rename("share")]
    if has_population:
        # xarray aligns by dim name -> people broadcasts share over segment by
        # the matching population cell; positions never enter into it.
        long_parts.append((shares * pop).rename("people"))
    long = xr.merge(long_parts).to_dataframe().reset_index()
    long_cols = [*cell_dims, segment_dim, "share"]
    if has_population:
        long_cols.append("people")
    segment_shares = long[long_cols]

    # -- national_summary (wide) ------------------------------------------------
    wide = (
        long.pivot_table(index=cell_dims, columns=segment_dim, values="share")
        .reindex(columns=seg_levels)  # keep the posterior's segment order
        .reset_index()
    )
    # Population-free headline: expected 1-based segment index (S1->1 .. SK->K).
    k_index = xr.DataArray(
        np.arange(1, len(seg_levels) + 1),
        dims=segment_dim,
        coords={segment_dim: shares[segment_dim]},
    )
    expected = (shares * k_index).sum(segment_dim).rename("expected_segment")
    summary = wide.merge(expected.to_dataframe().reset_index(), on=cell_dims)
    lead_cols = list(cell_dims)
    if has_population:
        summary = summary.merge(
            pop.rename("population").to_dataframe().reset_index(), on=cell_dims
        )
        lead_cols.append("population")
    lead_cols.append("expected_segment")
    national_summary = summary[lead_cols + seg_levels]

    # -- run_info (key/value) ---------------------------------------------------
    info_items: list[tuple[str, Any]] = [
        (f"n_{d}", int(shares.sizes[d])) for d in shares.dims
    ]
    info_items.append(("n_draws", int(posterior.sizes.get("draw", 1))))
    if result.losses is not None:
        info_items.append(("final_elbo_loss", float(np.asarray(result.losses)[-1])))
    for key, value in (metadata or {}).items():
        info_items.append((key, value))
    run_info = pd.DataFrame(info_items, columns=["key", "value"])

    return {
        SHEET_SEGMENT_SHARES: segment_shares,
        SHEET_NATIONAL_SUMMARY: national_summary,
        SHEET_RUN_INFO: run_info,
    }
rationale: Derives segmentation summary, population totals, and run information tables.
Collects observed geography-year coverage while skipping incomplete records.
Recognizes plain and disambiguated country columns.

def mask_unobserved_latent_tables(
    tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
    result: InferenceResult,
    observed: dict[str, set[tuple[Any, Any]]],
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Blank ``value`` where a latent indicator has no observation for that cell.

    Observation nodes (``*__obs`` in the graph) are left unchanged. Latent nodes
    whose indicator has partial panel coverage (e.g. ``hh_inet`` on 14/27
    countries) export ``NaN`` instead of a model-filled number that reads like a
    measurement.
    """
    masked: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
    for node_id, frame in tables.items():
        if node_id not in result.sampled():
            masked[node_id] = frame
            continue
        indicator = result.structured(node_id).indicator.indicator
        obs_cells = observed.get(indicator)
        if not obs_cells:
            masked[node_id] = frame
            continue
        if "value" in frame.columns:
            country_col = _country_column(frame)
            if country_col is None or "year" not in frame.columns:
                masked[node_id] = frame
                continue
            out = frame.copy()
            keys = list(zip(out[country_col], out["year"]))
            out.loc[[k not in obs_cells for k in keys], "value"] = np.nan
            masked[node_id] = out
            continue
        country_col = _country_column(frame)
        if country_col is None:
            masked[node_id] = frame
            continue
        year_cols = [c for c in frame.columns if c != country_col and str(c).isdigit()]
        if not year_cols:
            masked[node_id] = frame
            continue
        out = frame.copy()
        for idx, row in out.iterrows():
            country = row[country_col]
            for year_col in year_cols:
                key = (country, int(year_col))
                if key not in obs_cells:
                    out.at[idx, year_col] = np.nan
        masked[node_id] = out
    return masked
rationale: Masks inferred cells absent from indicator observations across long and wide layouts.

def parameter_tables(result: InferenceResult) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """One tidy frame per inferred node -- the "all the numbers" dump.

    Returns ``{node_name: DataFrame}`` covering *every* variable in the posterior
    -- latents and deterministics alike (e.g. ``theta_weight``, ``seg_logits``,
    ``income``, ``cov_3g``, ``population``) -- so a v0 workbook can expose
    everything the model inferred, not just the segmentation headline that
    :func:`result_tables` curates.

    The shaping rule is uniform and rank-agnostic, so it copes with whatever axes
    a node happens to carry: the node's **last axis spreads across columns**
    (named by level) and any **earlier axes become leading index columns**. A
    ``(country, year)`` node thus reads as a grid, a ``(transition, driver)`` node
    as a transition x driver grid, and a scalar node as a single ``value`` cell.
    Like :func:`result_tables`, it takes the MAP point (the single
    ``(chain=0, draw=0)`` draw) and is driven by the result's coords, not by
    positions; it needs only an ``InferenceResult`` (no ``BayesGraph``).

    This is the v0-only window into the model internals: the three curated sheets
    are the layer meant to survive into D7 reporting, while this per-node dump is
    not expected to outlive v0.
    """
    posterior = result.posterior
    return {
        name: _node_frame(
            posterior[name].isel(chain=0, draw=0).reset_coords(drop=True)
        )
        for name in posterior.data_vars
    }
rationale: Converts each posterior node to its first-draw presentation table.

def _node_frame(da: xr.DataArray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shape a single node's MAP draw into a tidy frame (see ``parameter_tables``)."""
    dims = list(da.dims)
    if not dims:  # scalar node -> a single labeled cell
        return pd.DataFrame({"value": [float(da.values)]})
    if len(dims) == 1:  # 1-D node -> (<axis>, value) long
        return da.rename("value").to_dataframe().reset_index()[[dims[0], "value"]]
    # >=2-D node: last axis -> columns (in coord order), earlier axes -> row index.
    col_dim = dims[-1]
    wide = (
        da.to_series()
        .unstack(col_dim)
        .reindex(columns=list(da[col_dim].values))  # keep the coord's level order
    )
    wide.columns = [str(c) for c in wide.columns]  # Excel headers must be strings
    return wide.reset_index()
rationale: Chooses scalar, vector, or wide table layout while preserving coordinate order.

def _safe_sheet_name(raw: str, used: set[str]) -> str:
    """An Excel-legal, unique sheet name for ``raw`` given the names already taken.

    Replaces forbidden characters, truncates to 31 chars, and appends ``~N`` if
    truncation made two distinct nodes collide. Short, already-legal names (the
    curated sheets) pass through unchanged.
    """
    name = _INVALID_SHEET_CHARS.sub("_", raw)[:_MAX_SHEET_NAME] or "sheet"
    if name not in used:
        used.add(name)
        return name
    i = 1
    while True:
        suffix = f"~{i}"
        candidate = name[: _MAX_SHEET_NAME - len(suffix)] + suffix
        if candidate not in used:
            used.add(candidate)
            return candidate
        i += 1
rationale: Sanitizes, truncates, and deduplicates workbook sheet names.

def write_workbook(
    tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
    out_dir: str | Path,
    *,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Write tidy ``tables`` to a timestamped ``.xlsx``: the thin, swappable layer.

    One sheet per ``(name, frame)`` entry, named for its key. The filename is
    ``YYYYMMDD_hhmmss_model_outputs.xlsx`` from ``now`` (defaulting to the
    current time; injected in tests for a deterministic name). Creates
    ``out_dir`` (and parents) if missing and returns the written path.

    The only layer that knows about Excel -- swap it for another sink without
    touching :func:`result_tables`.
    """
    now = now or datetime.now()
    out_dir = Path(out_dir)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = out_dir / _FILENAME_TEMPLATE.format(stamp=now.strftime(_STAMP_FORMAT))

    used: set[str] = set()
    with pd.ExcelWriter(path, engine="openpyxl") as writer:
        for name, frame in tables.items():
            frame.to_excel(writer, sheet_name=_safe_sheet_name(name, used), index=False)
    return path
rationale: Creates the destination and manages the Excel writer with valid unique sheet names.

def write_outputs(
    result: InferenceResult,
    out_dir: str | Path,
    *,
    now: datetime | None = None,
    shares_node: str | None = None,
    population_node: str | None = None,
    loaded: Any | None = None,
    **metadata: Any,
) -> Path:
    """Tabulate ``result`` and write the workbook -- the one-call convenience.

    A single ``now`` stamps both the ``run_info`` ``generated_at`` field and the
    filename, so the table's provenance and the file's name agree. Extra keyword
    metadata (e.g. ``seed=0``, ``steps=3000``) is recorded in ``run_info``.

    Segmentation and population nodes default to the result's ``specials`` (see
    :func:`result_tables`); pass ``shares_node`` / ``population_node`` to
    override.

    When ``loaded`` is supplied, latent indicator sheets blank cells with no
    observation in the panel (partial-coverage indicators such as ``hh_inet``).

    The workbook carries the three curated sheets *and* one sheet per inferred
    node from :func:`parameter_tables`, so it's a full window into the fit. A node
    whose name collides with a curated sheet (e.g. ``segment_shares``) is not
    duplicated -- the curated long sheet wins, so the headline view is never
    shadowed by the node's raw grid.
    """
    now = now or datetime.now()
    meta = {"generated_at": now.isoformat(timespec="seconds"), **metadata}
    tables = result_tables(
        result,
        shares_node=shares_node,
        population_node=population_node,
        metadata=meta,
    )
    for node, frame in parameter_tables(result).items():
        tables.setdefault(node, frame)  # curated sheets keep their name on collision
    if loaded is not None:
        observed = observed_country_years_by_indicator(loaded)
        tables = mask_unobserved_latent_tables(tables, result, observed)
    return write_workbook(tables, out_dir, now=now)
rationale: Assembles result and parameter sheets, applies coverage masks, and writes a dated workbook.

def __init__(
    self,
    sampled: Mapping[str, StructuredArray],
    *,
    specials: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    scenario: Any = None,
    losses: Any = None,
) -> None:
    if scenario is not None:
        # Narrowed to NoneType until scenario analysis is fleshed out (Max,
        # 2026-08-24). Refusing at construction rather than at save time
        # keeps every result that exists a result the writer can write.
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "scenario-carrying results are not implemented: nothing sets a "
            f"scenario yet, and there is no agreed form for one ({scenario!r})"
        )
    stored = {
        node_id: _prepare(node_id, array) for node_id, array in sampled.items()
    }
    object.__setattr__(self, "_sampled", stored)
    object.__setattr__(self, "_specials", _prepare_specials(specials, stored))
    object.__setattr__(self, "_scenario", scenario)
    object.__setattr__(
        self, "_losses", None if losses is None else np.asarray(losses)
    )
    object.__setattr__(self, "_idata", None)

def structured(self, node_id: str) -> StructuredArray:
    """One node's fitted array, with its axes, indicator and population.

    The whole point of holding the map: a caller that wants to aggregate
    needs ``indicator.family`` to know whether to sum or population-weight,
    and needs the axes to know what it is summing over. Reaching for
    ``posterior[node_id]`` gets the numbers without either.

    The population comes from the node carrying the ``population`` special,
    not from a pointer baked in at build time. The v4 graph wires the
    population as a *parent* of each observation grid, which is what the
    grid needs to collapse an axis while it is being built, and it leaves
    the emitted array's pointer ``None``. A consumer holding a finished
    result is asking a different question, and the special is what answers
    it: which node the people are. Attached verbatim -- projecting it onto
    this node's axes is the reduction's business, not this method's (see
    ``core.structured_array``).
    """
    try:
        array = self._sampled[node_id]
    except KeyError:
        raise KeyError(
            f"no node {node_id!r} in this result; it holds "
            f"{list(self._sampled)!r}"
        ) from None
    if array.population is not None:
        return array
    population_id = self.node_for_special(POPULATION_SPECIAL)
    if population_id is None or population_id == node_id:
        return array
    return replace(array, population=self._sampled[population_id])
rationale: Resolves missing population pointers through declared special nodes and reports unknown nodes.
Exposes a read-only view of stored samples.

def specials(self) -> Mapping[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
    """The structural properties each node carries, as a read-only view.

    Only nodes with at least one special appear. This is the one piece of
    the graph a result keeps, and it is kept because it is the piece a
    reader cannot rebuild: which node *is* the population, or the
    segmentation, is the config author's choice of node id and role name
    (see ``core.graph``), so a downstream consumer that lost it would be
    back to matching id conventions.
    """
    return MappingProxyType(self._specials)
rationale: Exposes a read-only view of special-node metadata.

def node_for_special(self, special: str) -> str | None:
    """The node carrying ``special``, or ``None`` if no node does.

    Singular because construction refuses a special on two nodes: "the
    population" and "the segmentation" are definite descriptions, and a
    reader asking for one wants an answer or nothing, not a list to choose
    from.
    """
    for node_id, specials in self._specials.items():
        if special in specials:
            return node_id
    return None
rationale: Resolves a special role across stored node metadata.

def as_inference_data(self) -> Any:
    """The map as an ArviZ container (a ``DataTree`` under ArviZ 1.x).

    Built on first call and kept: ``to_inference_data`` recomputes coords,
    dims and the level-set suffix rule over the whole node set, which is
    not worth repeating per access. It is a view, so it is derived rather
    than stored -- the container drops metadata the map keeps, and only one
    of the two can be the thing a result *is*.
    """
    if self._idata is None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "_idata", to_inference_data(self._sampled))
    return self._idata

def samples(self, node_id: str, **sel: Any):
    """Posterior array for ``node_id``, optionally sliced by named dims.

    Generic core accessor (D7): ``result.samples("segment_shares",
    country="KE")``. Shortcut methods like ``segment_shares`` are just
    named wrappers over this.

    Axis names are given bare: if the labeler suffixed a dim by its level
    set (see ``labeling.level_set_suffix``), the translation happens here.
    It is unambiguous because selection is per-node -- one variable can
    carry at most one dim per base name.
    """
    array = self.posterior[node_id]
    if not sel:
        return array
    return array.sel(**{_dim_for(array, name): v for name, v in sel.items()})
rationale: Resolves dimension aliases before selecting per-node posterior data.

def sel(self, **sel: Any):
    """Reserved: selecting one level across nodes with differing level sets.

    Not implemented rather than guessed at (Max, 2026-08-20: the use case
    isn't clear yet). It exists as a refusal because the thing a caller
    would otherwise reach for -- ``result.posterior.sel(country="KE")`` --
    applies *silently* to only the variables whose dim is literally named
    ``country``, leaving suffixed ones untouched. A partial answer with no
    error is worse than none.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError(
        "cross-node selection is not implemented: nodes may carry the same "
        f"axis over different level sets ({sorted(sel)!r}). Select per node "
        "with samples(node_id, ...)."
    )
rationale: Rejects unsupported cross-node selection with a concrete remedy.
Only fixes the segment_shares node name in samples and forwards country and year; callers can use the existing samples API directly.

def highlights(
    self,
    out: str | Path,
    include: Sequence[str],
    graph: Any = None,
    skipped: MutableMapping[str, str] | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> dict[str, Path]:
    """Write one highlight file per ``include`` name into directory ``out``.

    Each name has its own producer method, so the set of highlights grows by
    adding a method and an entry rather than by branching inside one writer.
    ``graph`` is accepted for producers that describe the *model* rather than
    the fit (the indicator list needs the graph the result deliberately does
    not keep); the segmentation sheets ignore it.

    Returns ``{name: path}``. An unknown name raises rather than being
    skipped -- a caller asking for a highlight that does not exist wants to
    hear about it, not to get a short dict back.

    Options in ``kwargs`` go to the producers that name them and no others,
    so ``now=`` reaching the tracker sheets is not a ``TypeError``. An option
    no requested producer names still raises: that is a typo, and silently
    dropping it would write the sheet the caller did not ask for.

    A producer can refuse because *this fit* cannot answer its question (a
    config with no segmentation). Pass ``skipped`` to collect those as
    ``{name: reason}`` instead of raising: a highlight is an extract allowed
    to lose things, so a caller who did not name the sheet itself wants the
    run to finish and to hear which sheets it lost. Without ``skipped`` the
    refusal propagates, which is what a caller naming the sheet wants.
    """
    unknown = [name for name in include if name not in HIGHLIGHTS]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unknown highlight(s) {unknown!r}; available: "
            f"{sorted(HIGHLIGHTS)!r}"
        )
    producers = {name: getattr(self, HIGHLIGHTS[name]) for name in include}
    accepted = {
        name: set(inspect.signature(producer).parameters)
        for name, producer in producers.items()
    }
    stray = set(kwargs) - set().union(*accepted.values(), set())
    if stray:
        raise TypeError(
            f"option(s) {sorted(stray)!r} are not taken by any of the "
            f"requested highlight(s) {list(include)!r}"
        )
    out = Path(out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    written: dict[str, Path] = {}
    for name, producer in producers.items():
        options = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if k in accepted[name]}
        try:
            written[name] = producer(out, graph=graph, **options)
        except ValueError as exc:
            if skipped is None:
                raise
            skipped[name] = str(exc)
    return written
rationale: Validates highlight requests and options, dispatches producers, and handles skippable outputs.

def _segmentation_sheet(self) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    """The validated segmentation frame, and the name of its year axis.

    The one place the segmentation is found and its tiers are checked, so
    both sheets agree about what counts as a real segmentation. Not cached
    (Max, 2026-08-28): the result is immutable by design, and a walk over a
    handful of axis names is not worth a mutable slot.
    """
    node_id = self.node_for_special(SEGMENTATION_SPECIAL)
    if node_id is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "this result has no node carrying the "
            f"{SEGMENTATION_SPECIAL!r} special, so there are no "
            f"segmentation numbers to report; it holds {list(self._sampled)!r}"
        )
    array = self.structured(node_id)
    seg_axis = _highlights.segmentation_axis(array)
    _highlights.validate_segment_levels(seg_axis, node_id)
    return _highlights.sheet_frame(array, seg_axis), array
rationale: Resolves segmentation by role and validates segment metadata before tabulation.

def _dim_for(array, name: str) -> str:
    """The dim of ``array`` a caller means by the bare axis name ``name``.

    Falls through to ``name`` when nothing matches, so xarray raises its own
    error about the dim the caller actually asked for.
    """
    if name in array.dims:
        return name
    prefix = name + SUFFIX_SEP
    matches = [str(dim) for dim in array.dims if str(dim).startswith(prefix)]
    return matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else name
rationale: Resolves an unsuffixed dimension name only when its disambiguated match is unique.

def save_result(result: InferenceResult, directory: Path | str) -> Path:
    """Write ``result`` into ``directory``, creating it if need be.

    Returns the directory. Existing files of the same names are overwritten;
    unrelated files are left alone, so a caller can keep a graph or a README
    beside the data.
    """
    out = Path(directory)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    specials = result.specials()
    nodes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for index, (node_id, sa) in enumerate(result.sampled().items()):
        _refuse_unwritable(node_id, sa)
        array = np.asarray(sa.array)
        filename = f"{index:03d}_{_UNSAFE.sub('_', node_id)}.csv"
        axes = [_axis_entry(axis) for axis in sa.axes]
        _write_node(out / filename, array, axes)
        nodes.append(
            {
                "node_id": node_id,
                "file": filename,
                "dtype": str(array.dtype),
                "indicator": {
                    "indicator": sa.indicator.indicator,
                    "family": sa.indicator.family,
                    "unit": sa.indicator.unit,
                },
                "specials": list(specials.get(node_id, ())),
                "axes": axes,
            }
        )

    manifest: dict[str, Any] = {
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "scenario": None,
        "losses": None,
        "nodes": nodes,
    }
    if result.losses is not None:
        losses = np.asarray(result.losses)
        _write_losses(out / LOSSES_NAME, losses)
        manifest["losses"] = {"file": LOSSES_NAME, "dtype": str(losses.dtype)}

    (out / MANIFEST_NAME).write_text(
        yaml.safe_dump(manifest, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    return out
rationale: Writes round-trip node arrays and metadata using the persisted schema.

def load_result(directory: Path | str) -> InferenceResult:
    """Read back what ``save_result`` wrote."""
    src = Path(directory)
    manifest = yaml.safe_load((src / MANIFEST_NAME).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    version = manifest.get("schema_version")
    if version != SCHEMA_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{src / MANIFEST_NAME} declares schema version {version!r}, but this "
            f"reader understands only {SCHEMA_VERSION}"
        )
    if manifest.get("scenario") is not None:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "this file carries a scenario, which is not implemented"
        )

    sampled: dict[str, StructuredArray] = {}
    specials: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    for node in manifest["nodes"]:
        axes = node["axes"]
        shape = tuple(len(axis["levels"]) for axis in axes)
        array = _read_node(src / node["file"], axes, shape, np.dtype(node["dtype"]))
        node_id = node["node_id"]
        # A required key rather than a ``.get``, which would read a missing one
        # as "no specials" -- the reading the version bump exists to prevent.
        specials[node_id] = tuple(node["specials"])
        sampled[node_id] = StructuredArray(
            array=array,
            # The axis type is declared once, so the level column stays plain
            # text; this is where that declaration is spent.
            axes=tuple(
                AxisMeta(
                    name=axis["name"],
                    levels=tuple(
                        parse_level(axis["type"], text) for text in axis["levels"]
                    ),
                    kind=axis["kind"],
                    axis_role=axis["axis_role"],
                )
                for axis in axes
            ),
            indicator=IndicatorMeta(**node["indicator"]),
            population=None,
            node_id=node_id,
        )

    losses = None
    if manifest.get("losses") is not None:
        spec = manifest["losses"]
        losses = _read_losses(src / spec["file"], np.dtype(spec["dtype"]))

    return InferenceResult(sampled, specials=specials, losses=losses)
rationale: Validates the schema and reconstructs named structured arrays and specials.
Rejects metadata with no supported persisted representation.

def _axis_entry(axis: AxisMeta) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """One axis for the manifest: name, level *type*, kind, role, levels as text.

    The type is hoisted out of the levels so both the manifest and the table can
    hold plain ``KE`` and ``2019``. One type per axis, because levels of an axis
    stand for the same kind of thing; a mixed axis is refused rather than
    written in a form that would read back with a type it did not have.
    """
    tagged = [level_text(level) for level in axis.levels]
    tags = {tag for tag, _ in tagged}
    if len(tags) > 1:
        raise TypeError(
            f"axis {axis.name!r} mixes level types {sorted(tags)!r}; a written "
            "axis declares one type for all its levels"
        )
    return {
        "name": axis.name,
        # An empty axis has no level to read a type from; str is the harmless
        # choice, since there is nothing to parse back either way.
        "type": next(iter(tags), "s"),
        "kind": axis.kind,
        "axis_role": axis.axis_role,
        "levels": [text for _, text in tagged],
    }
rationale: Encodes typed coordinate levels and rejects mixed level types.

def _labels(axes: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[tuple[str, ...]]:
    """The odometer over the axes' level texts: one tuple per cell, array order."""
    level_lists = [axis["levels"] for axis in axes]
    return list(itertools.product(*level_lists)) if level_lists else [()]
rationale: Enumerates axis coordinates in persisted cell order, including the scalar case.

def _write_node(path: Path, array: np.ndarray, axes: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
    """One long-form row per cell of ``array``."""
    names = [axis["name"] for axis in axes]
    flat = array.reshape(-1)
    cells = _labels(axes)
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.writer(handle)
        writer.writerow([*names, "value"])
        for column, cell in enumerate(cells):
            writer.writerow([*cell, _number(flat[column])])
rationale: Writes ordered labeled cells with dtype-aware numeric text.

def _read_node(
    path: Path,
    axes: list[dict[str, Any]],
    shape: tuple[int, ...],
    dtype: np.dtype,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Invert ``_write_node``, checking the labels rather than trusting order.

    The values could be read by position alone -- the manifest fixes the order.
    Reading the label columns back and comparing is what turns a hand-edited or
    reordered file into an error instead of a silently transposed array. The
    comparison is on the text, before any parsing, so it also catches a file
    whose labels were rewritten into some other spelling of the same level.
    """
    expected_cells = _labels(axes)
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        rows = list(csv.reader(handle))
    header, body = rows[0], rows[1:]
    n_cells = int(np.prod(shape)) if shape else 1
    if len(body) != n_cells:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{path}: has {len(body)} rows but the manifest describes "
            f"{n_cells} cells"
        )
    names = [axis["name"] for axis in axes]
    if header[:-1] != names:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{path}: axis columns {header[:-1]} do not match the "
            f"manifest's {names}"
        )
    values = np.empty(len(body), dtype=dtype)
    for index, row in enumerate(body):
        cell = tuple(row[:-1])
        if cell != expected_cells[index]:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{path}, row {index + 2}: labels {cell!r} where the manifest's "
                f"level order gives {expected_cells[index]!r}"
            )
        values[index] = dtype.type(row[-1])
    return values.reshape(shape)
rationale: Validates cell counts, headers, and coordinate order before reconstructing the tensor.

def _number(value: Any) -> str:
    """A scalar as text that reads back as the same scalar.

    ``repr`` of a Python float is the shortest string that round-trips, which is
    the property this needs; the manifest's dtype then puts it back in the width
    it came from, so a float32 fit does not silently reload as float64.
    """
    scalar = value.item() if isinstance(value, np.generic) else value
    return repr(scalar) if isinstance(scalar, float) else str(scalar)
rationale: Preserves round-trip float representation while normalizing NumPy scalars.

def build_graph(
    config: GraphConfig,
    observations: LoadedObservations | None = None,
    *,
    data_resolver: DataResolver | None = None,
) -> BayesGraph:
    """Assemble a :class:`BayesGraph` from a config and (optionally) loaded data.

    Declared nodes are added first, then declared edges (so every edge endpoint
    resolves). When ``observations`` is given, one family-bundled Type-III obs
    node is assembled per loader bundle and wired to the declared latents whose
    indicators it observes; cells for undeclared indicators are gated out and
    warned about. At ``version: 4`` that assembly happens in ``desugar``, which is
    handed the same bundles; step 5 below serves ≤v3 only.
    ``data_resolver`` materializes any :class:`DataRef`-bearing
    hyperparameters/axes; omit it for panel-independent configs.
    """
    from digital_readiness.core.cpd import CpdSpec  # local: avoid import cycle risk

    # Lower any v2 sugar to the flat Tier-1 form first: everything below this
    # line only ever sees a flat config.
    config = desugar(config, observations)

    axis_registry = config.resolve_axes(data_resolver=data_resolver)

    # 0. Structural-axis inference. When a segmentation anchor is present, the
    #    segment/output/driver axes are inferred into the registry (if not
    #    declared) BEFORE node conversion, so node `axes: [transition]`
    #    references resolve unchanged via `_resolve_axis`. Declared axes win.
    anchor_pair = _find_segmentation_anchor(config)
    anchor, anchor_entry = anchor_pair if anchor_pair is not None else (None, None)
    if anchor is not None:
        _infer_structural_axes(config, axis_registry, anchor, anchor_entry)

    graph = BayesGraph()

    # 1. Declared nodes first. The role specs come along so each node's role
    #    resolves to its `specials`; without them a graph-side consumer looking
    #    for a named structural property (the population node) would be back to
    #    matching a role name the config is free to choose.
    role_specs = config.resolved_node_roles()
    declared_ids: set[str] = set()
    for node in config.nodes:
        graph.add_node(
            node.to_node_meta(
                axis_registry, data_resolver=data_resolver, role_specs=role_specs
            )
        )
        declared_ids.add(node.id)

    # 1b. Pre-synthesize downstream mixture-means so declared edges that wire
    #     obs/constraints off the mean can resolve before step 2. Only the
    #     segment_shares/profile parent edges are synthesized here; child edges
    #     (mean -> obs, mean -> constraint) stay declared.
    #
    #     Gated off at ``version: 4`` (plan J1) for the same reason as step 3
    #     below: a v4 config is supposed to look like its graph, and this helper
    #     keys on ``extra.manifestation_role`` to add a node the config never
    #     names. A v4 config declares its means outright -- the spelling is not
    #     new, ``demo_v0_bundled.yaml`` has declared exactly these two by hand
    #     since v0. Ungated, the mismatch was not merely cosmetic: an
    #     ``observation_v0`` node inheriting its ``indicator`` from one of these
    #     means found no parent *node* and fell back to its own id, which is the
    #     silent ``inherit`` -> ``own`` demotion B3 turns into an error.
    #
    #     The tag itself stays: ``model/cpds/manifestation.py`` reads
    #     ``manifestation_role`` at runtime to sort the mean's parents into
    #     ``shares`` vs ``profile``, so it is a parent-role declaration as well as
    #     a trigger. This gate retires only the trigger.
    shares_anchor = _find_continuation_ratio_anchor(config)
    if shares_anchor is not None and config.version < 4:
        _attach_downstream_manifestation_pairs(graph, config, shares_anchor, CpdSpec)

    # 2. Declared edges. Endpoints may be declared or pre-synthesized above.
    for edge in config.edges:
        for endpoint, role in ((edge.parent, "parent"), (edge.child, "child")):
            if endpoint not in declared_ids and endpoint not in graph:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"edge ({edge.parent!r} -> {edge.child!r}) names an "
                    f"undeclared {role} node {endpoint!r}; declare it in the "
                    "config's `nodes` section before referencing it in `edges`"
                )
        graph.add_edge(edge.parent, edge.child)

    # 3. Synthesize upstream driver standardizers (root -> _z -> anchor) for
    #    any ``indicator_role: upstream`` root that left the standardizer chain
    #    unfilled. Run before logit-bridge synthesis so the anchor's parent set
    #    is complete.
    #
    #    BRIDGE-B (throwaway): ungated for ``version: 2`` and ``3`` (see the v4
    #    gate below, which is the start of its removal).
    #    Desugar-v2 emits the segmentation priors but not the
    #    ``_z`` standardizers, so build backfills them here to keep the v1/v2
    #    twins synthesizing the same graph. Slated for removal once desugar
    #    synthesizes ``standardization`` prerequisites on demand (the consumer
    #    declares ``parents: [{normalizer: z_score}, ...]``); at that point no
    #    synthesis should key on ``extra.indicator_role`` at all.
    #
    #    Gated off at ``version: 4``: a v4 config is supposed to look like its
    #    graph, so the standardizer chain is *declared* there
    #    (``parents: [{id: root, normalize: {}}]``, which desugar's
    #    ``expand_parents`` lowers into a real ``_z`` node). Backfilling from a
    #    tag would let a v4 graph acquire a node the config never names.
    if anchor is not None and config.version < 4:
        _attach_upstream_driver_pairs(
            graph, config, anchor, CpdSpec, data_resolver=data_resolver
        )

    # 4. v1-only: generic segmentation priors (theta_bias/theta_weight) for any
    #    role the anchor's declared parents leave unfilled. For ``version: 2+``,
    #    desugar owns the equivalent structure (autoconstruct); this helper must
    #    not fire (plan M4 / design doc architecture glance). Run after declared
    #    nodes+edges so the role classification sees them.
    if config.version == 1 and anchor is not None:
        _attach_segmentation_priors(
            graph, config, axis_registry, anchor, anchor_entry, CpdSpec
        )

    # 5. Data-driven observation auto-attach: one family-bundled Type-III obs
    #    node per loader bundle, gated to declared indicators, wired to their
    #    latents. Deliberately *ungated* across versions (like BRIDGE-B above):
    #    desugar's ``_expand_obs`` only lowers explicit ``obs:`` blocks, so
    #    data-driven attach has no desugar equivalent yet and build backfills it
    #    for every version. Temporary, and a breach rather than a design: Max,
    #    2026-08-13, "desugar is just a way for a config author to be able to write
    #    by shorthand what they'd otherwise have to write by hand" -- and these
    #    nodes are written by *build* from loaded data, so no hand-authored config
    #    corresponds to them. Phase J is where the construction moves into the
    #    lowering; D1 is where autoconstruction gains the data it needs to do it.
    #    Dormant unless the caller passes ``observations`` --
    #    the pipeline passes them only when the config declares no obs nodes
    #    (``build_graph_from_config``), so declared-obs configs never double-attach.
    #
    #    Gated off at ``version: 4``: desugar's ``synthesize_observations`` now
    #    emits these nodes from the same bundles, so at v4 they are already in
    #    ``config.nodes`` by the time step 1 runs. The ≤v3 path stays as-is.
    if observations is not None and config.version < 4:
        _attach_observations(graph, config, observations, CpdSpec)

    return graph
rationale: Assembles nodes and edges, resolves axes, and performs version-dependent synthesis.

def _find_segmentation_anchor(config: GraphConfig):
    """The single segmentation-anchor node and its entry, or ``None`` if absent.

    Detection is by the per-family ``SegmentationAnchor`` descriptor
    (``entry.segmentation_anchor is not None``), never by family string or node
    id -- the anchor's *declared property* (not its name or paradigm) is what
    triggers structural inference and prior synthesis. Returns ``(node, entry)``
    so callers read the descriptor and parameter schema without re-looking-up.
    """
    for node in config.nodes:
        if node.cpd is None:
            continue
        entry = registry_entry_for(node.cpd)
        if entry is not None and entry.segmentation_anchor is not None:
            return node, entry
    return None
rationale: Searches configured nodes using registry capabilities and returns the node plus its descriptor.

def _infer_structural_axes(
    config: GraphConfig, axis_registry: dict, anchor, entry
) -> None:
    """Inject the segment/output/driver axes the config omitted.

    Mutates ``axis_registry`` in place. A declared axis is never overwritten
    (override preserved). Which axes there are, what their levels and ``kind``
    are, and in what order they resolve all come from
    :func:`desugar.structural_axis_rules` -- shared with desugar's ``loc``-grid
    sizing, which needs the same lengths and used to derive them separately. So
    the paradigm owns the segmentation shape, and build owns only the two things
    that are build's: that a declared axis wins, and that an unknown K is an
    error here (desugar merely gives up).
    """
    for rule in structural_axis_rules(config, anchor, entry, entry.segmentation_anchor.role_tag):
        if rule.name in axis_registry:
            continue
        # Resolved lazily and only when needed: a config with no K at all is
        # fine as long as no K-derived axis is actually missing.
        k = _resolve_segment_count(config, axis_registry) if rule.needs_segment_count else None
        axis_registry[rule.name] = AxisMeta(
            name=rule.name,
            levels=rule.levels(k),
            kind=rule.kind,
            axis_role=rule.axis_role,
        )
rationale: Applies shared axis rules while preserving declared axes and validating missing segment counts.

def _resolve_segment_count(config: GraphConfig, axis_registry: dict) -> int:
    """K, the number of latent segments.

    Precedence: a declared ``segment`` axis's length, else ``config.segment_count``.
    If both are present they must agree. If neither is, raise a named error (the
    structural axes cannot be inferred without K).
    """
    declared = axis_registry.get("segment")
    declared_k = len(declared.levels) if declared is not None else None
    if declared_k is not None and config.segment_count is not None:
        if declared_k != config.segment_count:
            raise ValueError(
                f"segment_count={config.segment_count} disagrees with the "
                f"declared `segment` axis length {declared_k}; drop one or make "
                "them consistent"
            )
        return declared_k
    if declared_k is not None:
        return declared_k
    if config.segment_count is not None:
        return config.segment_count
    raise ValueError(
        "cannot infer the structural axes: the segment count K is unknown. "
        "Set the top-level `segment_count` scalar, or declare the `segment` axis "
        "explicitly in `axes`."
    )
rationale: Encodes precedence and consistency checks between a declared axis and segment_count.

def _attach_segmentation_priors(
    graph: BayesGraph,
    config: GraphConfig,
    axis_registry: dict,
    anchor,
    entry,
    cpd_spec_cls: Any,
) -> None:
    """Synthesize the segmentation anchor's omitted parameter priors.

    Reads *what to synthesize* off the anchor family's registry entry rather than
    a build-side table: the auto-buildable roles are those whose ``ParamDecl``
    carries a ``default_prior`` (its presence is the capability), the synthesized
    distribution is that ``default_prior``'s family + hyperparameters, and the
    shape is ``(*B, *ParamDecl.axes)`` -- the disaggregation axes B (config-derived,
    see ``desugar.infer_disaggregation_axes``) prepended to the role's own
    resolved axes.
    Build no longer re-states any of these CPD facts (T2 §4).

    Precedence, mirroring the obs auto-attach precedent:

    - A declared parent in the role (by the paradigm's ``role_tag``) suppresses
      synthesis entirely ("config wins").
    - ``parents.<role>.autoconstruct: false`` also suppresses it (author owns it).
    - ``parents.<role>.axes`` overrides the inferred shape verbatim.
    - ``parents.<role>.distribution`` overrides the synthesized *distribution*
      (family + hyperparameters); the shape is unaffected (independent knobs).

    The driver ``sign``/``sign_loc`` tags steer the ``weights`` role's ``loc`` and
    are normal-only; a non-normal ``distribution`` override wins wholesale and the
    tags are rejected under it (§5b). Synthesis is direct ``NodeMeta``/``CpdSpec``
    construction (past the schema boundary, like ``_obs_node_meta``); the node id
    is the general ``{anchor_id}_{role}`` unless the paradigm opts into the legacy
    ``BRIDGE_NODE_IDS`` map via ``SegmentationAnchor.legacy_theta_prior_ids``
    (transition, for demo/ELBO equivalence). The role each synthesized node fills
    is recorded under the paradigm's ``role_tag`` extra key.
    """
    from digital_readiness.core.graph import NodeMeta

    # TODO(auto-construct walk): role_tag and legacy_theta_prior_ids are
    # placeholders pending the proper node-synthesis logic -- tagging role on the
    # node may not survive bundling (where it belongs is not yet explored), and
    # naming is not settled (testlist Open-1).
    descriptor = entry.segmentation_anchor
    role_tag = descriptor.role_tag

    declared_roles = {
        (node.extra or {}).get(role_tag)
        for node in config.nodes
        if node.id in graph and anchor.id in graph.children(node.id)
    }

    parents_block = (anchor.cpd.parents if anchor.cpd is not None else {}) or {}
    parameter_schema = entry.parameter_schema
    # Auto-buildable roles: those the family declares with a default_prior. A role
    # with axes but no default_prior must be supplied; a data input (neither) is
    # never synthesized. `is_auto_buildable_param` is the shared predicate (see
    # core.cpd) -- kept in one place so build and the desugar boundary agree.
    buildable_roles = [
        role for role, decl in parameter_schema.items() if is_auto_buildable_param(decl)
    ]

    # A `distribution` override tunes synthesis; it cannot enable it. Overriding a
    # role that is not auto-buildable is a config error (not a silent no-op).
    for role, parent_spec in parents_block.items():
        if getattr(parent_spec, "distribution", None) is None:
            continue
        if role not in buildable_roles:
            raise ValueError(
                f"`parents.{role}.distribution` on {anchor.id!r} overrides the "
                f"synthesized distribution, but role {role!r} has no `default_prior` "
                "(it is not auto-buildable); remove the override or declare the "
                "parent node explicitly"
            )

    inferred_B: tuple[str, ...] | None = None  # computed lazily, at most once

    for role in buildable_roles:
        if role in declared_roles:
            continue  # a node in this role is declared -> do not synthesize
        parent_spec = parents_block.get(role)
        if parent_spec is not None and not parent_spec.autoconstruct:
            continue  # author owns this parent -> hands off ("config wins")

        decl = parameter_schema[role]
        if parent_spec is not None and parent_spec.axes is not None:
            axis_names = tuple(parent_spec.axes)  # declaration wins, verbatim
        else:
            if inferred_B is None:
                inferred_B = infer_disaggregation_axes(config, anchor, role_tag)
            structural = resolve_axis_refs(anchor.cpd, entry, decl.axes or ())
            axis_names = (*inferred_B, *structural)

        try:
            axes = tuple(axis_registry[name] for name in axis_names)
        except KeyError as exc:
            raise ValueError(
                f"`parents` block for role {role!r} on {anchor.id!r} names axis "
                f"{exc.args[0]!r}, which is not in the axis registry"
            ) from None

        # Distribution: config override wins over the CPD's default_prior. Shape
        # (axes) is independent of family and already resolved above.
        override = parent_spec.distribution if parent_spec is not None else None
        if override is not None:
            family = override.family
            hyperparameters = {**dict(override.hyperparameters), "axes": axes}
        else:
            prior = decl.default_prior
            family = prior.family
            hyperparameters = {**dict(prior.hyperparameters), "axes": axes}

        # Normal-only sign/sign_loc loc steering (weights role). A non-normal
        # override wins wholesale; sign tags are rejected under it (no silent mix).
        if role == "weights":
            if family == "normal":
                hyperparameters["loc"] = _synthesized_theta_weight_loc(config, axes)
            elif any_driver_signed(config, anchor, role_tag):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"`parents.weights.distribution` on {anchor.id!r} uses "
                    f"non-normal family {family!r}, but a driver carries "
                    "`sign`/`sign_loc` (normal-only loc steering); remove one"
                )

        # General id is `{anchor_id}_{role}`; the transition paradigm opts into
        # the legacy theta_bias/theta_weight map for demo/ELBO equivalence.
        if descriptor.legacy_theta_prior_ids:
            node_id = BRIDGE_NODE_IDS.get(role, f"{anchor.id}_{role}")
        else:
            node_id = f"{anchor.id}_{role}"
        graph.add_node(
            NodeMeta(
                node_id=node_id,
                kind="prior_v0",
                cpd_spec=cpd_spec_cls(
                    family=family,
                    constructor=None,
                    hyperparameters=hyperparameters,
                ),
                extra={role_tag: role},
            )
        )
        graph.add_edge(node_id, anchor.id)
rationale: Resolves role-specific priors, shape overrides, distribution policy, and graph wiring.
