def register() -> None:
    """Install this module's CPD entries in the global registry."""
    register_cpd(
        "transition_logits",
        "linear",
        transition_logits_linear,
        kind="deterministic",
        default_role="structural_prereq",
        parameter_schema={
            # biases/weights carry `axes` (as hyperparameter-name references) and
            # a `default_prior` -- the two make them auto-buildable by build's T2
            # synthesis path. `drivers` carries neither: it is a data input, never
            # synthesized. See docs/sketches/t2_segmentation_seam.md, Piece A.
            "biases": ParamDecl(
                description="Bias vector a over the transition axis; one.",
                min_count=1,
                max_count=1,
                axes=("transition_axis",),
                default_prior=DefaultPrior("normal", {"loc": 0.0, "scale": 1.0}),
            ),
            "weights": ParamDecl(
                description=(
                    "Slope matrix g over (transition, driver); one. Driver "
                    "axis levels are driver names."
                ),
                min_count=1,
                max_count=1,
                axes=("transition_axis", "driver_axis"),
                default_prior=DefaultPrior("normal", {"loc": 0.0, "scale": 1.0}),
            ),
            "drivers": ParamDecl(
                description=(
                    "Standardized driver fields, one per indicator; matched "
                    "to weight columns by indicator name."
                ),
                min_count=1,
                max_count=None,
            ),
        },
        hyperparameter_schema={
            "transition_axis": HyperDecl(
                description="Name of the transition axis on biases/weights.",
                default="transition",
            ),
            "driver_axis": HyperDecl(
                description="Name of the weights' driver axis.",
                default="driver",
            ),
            "disaggregation_axes": HyperDecl(
                description=(
                    "Optional list of axis names the coefficients disaggregate "
                    "along (e.g. ['gender', 'urban_rural']). Unset -> inferred "
                    "from the weights' non-role axes. When set, each declared "
                    "axis is sourced from whichever parent carries it and other "
                    "parents broadcast over it; a declared axis no parent carries, "
                    "or an undeclared coefficient axis, is an error."
                ),
                default=None,
            ),
        },
        resolve_bindings=_resolve_transition_logits_bindings,
        # This family IS the (default) segmentation anchor. Its output axis is
        # named by the `transition_axis` hyperparameter, and the continuation-
        # ratio paradigm emits K-1 logits for K segments.
        segmentation_anchor=SegmentationAnchor(
            output_axis_hyperparameter="transition_axis",
            output_length_from_k=lambda k: k - 1,
            # TODO(auto-construct walk): this legacy opt-in preserves the demo's
            # theta_bias/theta_weight ids (ELBO equivalence). The general default
            # is `{anchor_id}_{role}`; both go away once the walk owns naming.
            legacy_theta_prior_ids=True,
        ),
    )

def tex_text(value: Any) -> str:
    """Escape literal YAML text; never interpret it as user-supplied TeX."""
    replacements = {
        "\\": r"\backslash{}",
        "{": r"\{",
        "}": r"\}",
        "_": r"\_",
        "%": r"\%",
        "&": r"\&",
        "#": r"\#",
        "$": r"\$",
        "^": r"\hat{}",
        "~": r"\sim{}",
    }
    return r"\text{" + "".join(replacements.get(c, c) for c in str(value)) + "}"

def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--config", "-c", required=True, help="YAML path or example name"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--data", "-d", type=Path, required=True, help="panel workbook")
    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", "-o", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--warmup", "--num-warmup", dest="num_warmup", type=_nonnegative, default=1000
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--samples", "--num-samples", dest="num_samples", type=_positive, default=1000
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--chains", "--num-chains", dest="num_chains", type=_positive, default=4
    )
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=DEFAULT_SEED)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--target-accept", dest="target_accept_prob", type=_probability, default=0.9
    )
    parser.add_argument("--max-tree-depth", type=_positive, default=10)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--chain-method",
        choices=("sequential", "parallel", "vectorized"),
        default="sequential",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--x64", action="store_true", help="enable JAX float64 before loading"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--no-progress", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--year-min", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--year-max", type=int)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--obs-status",
        default="A",
        help="comma-separated statuses; explicitly use A,CF,U for the labeled AI trial",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--countries", help="optional comma-separated country ISO3 codes"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if not 0 <= args.seed < 2**32:
        parser.error("--seed must be an unsigned 32-bit integer")
    if (
        args.year_min is not None
        and args.year_max is not None
        and args.year_min > args.year_max
    ):
        parser.error("--year-min must not exceed --year-max")
    statuses = tuple(
        value.strip() for value in args.obs_status.split(",") if value.strip()
    )
    if not statuses:
        parser.error("--obs-status must contain at least one status")
    countries = (
        tuple(value.strip() for value in args.countries.split(",") if value.strip())
        if args.countries is not None
        else None
    )
    if countries == ():
        parser.error("--countries must contain at least one country")
    try:
        config_path = _resolve_config(args.config)
    except FileNotFoundError as error:
        parser.error(str(error))
    data_path = args.data.resolve()
    if not data_path.is_file():
        parser.error(f"data file not found: {data_path}")
    if args.out_dir.exists() and not args.out_dir.is_dir():
        parser.error("--out-dir must be a directory")
    if args.x64:
        jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)

    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    clock = perf_counter()
    register_pipeline_cpds()
    config = load_graph_config(config_path)
    flt = ObservationLoadFilter(
        obs_status=statuses,
        country_iso3=countries,
        year_min=args.year_min,
        year_max=args.year_max,
    )
    loaded = load_observations_for_config(config, data_path, flt=flt)
    graph = build_graph_from_config(config, loaded)
    evidence = fit_observations(config, loaded, graph=graph, data_path=data_path)
    model = compile_model(graph)
    print(
        f"NUTS config={config_path.name} rows={loaded.n_rows_kept} "
        f"chains={args.num_chains} warmup={args.num_warmup} samples={args.num_samples} "
        f"seed={args.seed} chain_method={args.chain_method}",
        flush=True,
    )
    mcmc = run_nuts(
        model,
        evidence,
        num_warmup=args.num_warmup,
        num_samples=args.num_samples,
        num_chains=args.num_chains,
        seed=args.seed,
        target_accept_prob=args.target_accept_prob,
        max_tree_depth=args.max_tree_depth,
        chain_method=args.chain_method,
        progress_bar=not args.no_progress,
    )
    point = {
        name: values[0, 0]
        for name, values in mcmc.get_samples(group_by_chain=True).items()
    }
    replay = handlers.seed(
        handlers.substitute(model, data=point), jax.random.PRNGKey(args.seed)
    )(observations=evidence)
    node_axes = {
        name: [{"name": axis.name, "levels": list(axis.levels)} for axis in value.axes]
        for name, value in replay.items()
    }
    run_dir = args.out_dir / started.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S_%f_nuts")
    save_nuts_result(
        mcmc,
        run_dir,
        max_tree_depth=args.max_tree_depth,
        metadata={
            "started_at": started.isoformat(),
            "elapsed_seconds": perf_counter() - clock,
            "config": str(config_path),
            "data": str(data_path),
            "rows_kept": loaded.n_rows_kept,
            "seed": args.seed,
            "target_accept_prob": args.target_accept_prob,
            "jax_enable_x64": bool(jax.config.jax_enable_x64),
            "obs_status": statuses,
            "countries": countries,
            "year_min": args.year_min,
            "year_max": args.year_max,
            "observed_sites": sorted(evidence.observed_sites()),
            "node_axes": node_axes,
            "site_axes": _site_axes(graph, replay, point),
        },
    )
    shutil.copyfile(config_path, run_dir / "config.yaml")
    print(f"NUTS artifacts={run_dir}", flush=True)

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _isolate_registry():
    """Clear the global CPD registry around every test in this module.

    The registry is a module-global ``dict``; without this fixture, a test
    that registers ``"beta.observation"`` would leak that entry into the next
    test and corrupt independence.
    """
    _clear_registry()
    yield
    _clear_registry()

def _noop_fn(**_kwargs: Any) -> None:
    return None

def _noop_resolver(**_kwargs: Any) -> dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
    return {}

def test_register_rejects_duplicate() -> None:
    register_cpd("beta", "observation", _noop_fn, kind="stochastic")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="already registered"):
        register_cpd("beta", "observation", _noop_fn, kind="stochastic")

def test_register_rejects_param_schema_without_resolver() -> None:
    # Per D17, a non-empty parameter_schema is incoherent without a
    # resolve_bindings callable; the compile step would have no way to fill in
    # resolved_bindings. Caught at registration time.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="resolve_bindings"):
        register_cpd(
            "lognormal", "latent", _noop_fn,
            kind="stochastic",
            parameter_schema={"mu": ParamDecl()},
        )

def test_register_accepts_empty_param_schema_without_resolver() -> None:
    # A root-style CPD (no parents) has nothing to resolve; resolve_bindings
    # legitimately stays None.
    register_cpd("beta", "observation", _noop_fn, kind="stochastic")
    entry = lookup(CpdSpec(family="beta", constructor="observation"), "unused")
    assert entry.resolve_bindings is None

def test_lookup_falls_back_to_default_constructor() -> None:
    register_cpd("beta", "observation", _noop_fn, kind="stochastic")
    entry = lookup(CpdSpec(family="beta"), default_constructor="observation")
    assert entry.fn is _noop_fn

def test_lookup_unknown_constructor_lists_registered_names() -> None:
    register_cpd("beta", "observation", _noop_fn, kind="stochastic")
    with pytest.raises(KeyError) as exc:
        lookup(
            CpdSpec(family="beta", constructor="not_there"),
            default_constructor="observation",
        )
    # The error message should help a user discover what *is* available, not
    # just say "missing"; otherwise debugging typo'd constructor names is hard.
    assert "not_there" in str(exc.value)
    assert "observation" in str(exc.value)

def test_cpdspec_is_frozen() -> None:
    spec = CpdSpec(family="beta")
    with pytest.raises(dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError):
        spec.family = "lognormal"  # type: ignore[misc]

def _register_two_role_constructor(
    *,
    components: ParamDecl,
    anchor: ParamDecl = ParamDecl(),
) -> ConstructorEntry:
    """Register a two-role constructor and return its entry.

    Most validation tests need an entry whose ``parameter_schema`` has one
    role of interest plus a stable arity-1 ``anchor`` role; this helper
    keeps each test focused on the one varied dimension.
    """
    register_cpd(
        "agg", "default", _noop_fn,
        kind="stochastic",
        parameter_schema={"components": components, "anchor": anchor},
        resolve_bindings=_noop_resolver,
    )
    return lookup(CpdSpec(family="agg", constructor="default"), "default")

def test_validate_resolution_happy_arity1() -> None:
    entry = _register_two_role_constructor(components=ParamDecl())
    validate_resolution(
        entry=entry,
        resolved={"components": ("a",), "anchor": ("b",)},
        parent_node_ids=frozenset({"a", "b"}),
    )

def test_validate_resolution_happy_variable_arity() -> None:
    # Variable-arity role: 3 parents bind to one role, plus an unrelated
    # arity-1 anchor.
    entry = _register_two_role_constructor(
        components=ParamDecl(min_count=1, max_count=None),
    )
    validate_resolution(
        entry=entry,
        resolved={"components": ("a", "b", "c"), "anchor": ("d",)},
        parent_node_ids=frozenset({"a", "b", "c", "d"}),
    )

def test_validate_resolution_empty_schema_and_resolution() -> None:
    # A root-style CPD: empty schema, empty resolution, no parents. Should
    # validate trivially.
    register_cpd("beta", "observation", _noop_fn, kind="stochastic")
    entry = lookup(CpdSpec(family="beta", constructor="observation"), "unused")
    validate_resolution(
        entry=entry, resolved={}, parent_node_ids=frozenset()
    )

def test_validate_resolution_missing_role() -> None:
    entry = _register_two_role_constructor(components=ParamDecl())
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="missing"):
        validate_resolution(
            entry=entry,
            resolved={"components": ("a",)},  # anchor absent

def test_unbundle_all_recovers_coalesced_effect_group() -> None:
    """One (consumer, role) with two per-axis atoms -> two recovered arrays.

    A coalesced effect group holds one entry per demographic axis under the
    same key. ``unbundle`` would raise ('mixed entry_axes'); ``unbundle_all``
    returns each atom separately, in first-appearance order.
    """
    gender = AxisMeta(name="gender", levels=("F", "M"), kind="categorical")
    country = AxisMeta(
        name="country", levels=("A", "B", "C"), kind="categorical"
    )
    g_vals = jnp.array([1.0, 2.0])
    c_vals = jnp.array([10.0, 20.0, 30.0])
    bundle = _bundle_from_entries(
        [
            ("c1", "effects", (gender,), g_vals),
            ("c1", "effects", (country,), c_vals),
        ]
    )
    # unbundle chokes on the coalesced key; unbundle_all is the way in.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="mixed entry_axes"):
        bundle.unbundle(consumer_id="c1", role="effects")

    atoms = bundle.unbundle_all(consumer_id="c1", role="effects")
    assert len(atoms) == 2
    assert atoms[0].axes == (gender,)
    assert atoms[1].axes == (country,)
    assert jnp.allclose(atoms[0].array, g_vals)
    assert jnp.allclose(atoms[1].array, c_vals)

def test_round_trip_preserves_axis_kind() -> None:
    """A declared ``ordinal`` axis must come back ordinal.

    The label carries the axis whole, so there is nothing to re-derive on the
    way out. Before that, the gather rebuilt the axis from ``(name, levels)``
    alone and had to supply ``kind="categorical"``, which silently turned every
    bundled axis categorical however it was declared -- and downstream rejected
    it with an error whose two axis lists printed identically.
    """
    year = AxisMeta(name="year", levels=(2020, 2021, 2022), kind="ordinal")
    bundle = _bundle_from_entries([("mob", "weights", (year,), jnp.arange(3.0))])
    got = bundle.unbundle(consumer_id="mob", role="weights")
    assert got.axes == (year,)
    assert got.axes[0].kind == "ordinal"

def test_round_trip_preserves_axis_basis() -> None:
    """``basis`` is the same casualty as ``kind``, and the same fix closes it.

    A basis axis that came back without its ``BasisSpec`` would silently skip
    ``_densify_touched_basis`` on any reduction touching it.
    """
    basis = BasisSpec(
        name="age",
        family="piecewise_linear_hat",
        knots=(0.0, 10.0, 20.0),
        grid=(0, 10, 20),
    )
    ax = AxisMeta(name="age_bs", levels=(0, 1, 2), kind="ordinal", basis=basis)
    bundle = _bundle_from_entries([("n", "coeffs", (ax,), jnp.arange(3.0))])
    got = bundle.unbundle(consumer_id="n", role="coeffs")
    assert got.axes[0].basis == basis

def test_entries_differing_only_in_kind_are_separate_entries() -> None:
    """Two axes alike but for ``kind`` must not coalesce into one entry.

    This pins the cause rather than the symptom: under the old ``(name,
    levels)`` label these two were indistinguishable, so they grouped together
    and ``unbundle`` saw one entry of six cells instead of two of three.

def test_projected_blocks_carry_no_node_id() -> None:
    """A projected block is a ``(consumer, role)`` cell, not a node's output.

    The bundle itself is attributed (it *is* one node's realization), but a block
    cut out of it stands for a consumer/role slot; ``BundleCellLabel`` records no

def test_fill_rule_takes_its_shape_from_the_site() -> None:
    """The property A2 exists to establish, stated as plainly as possible.

    The rule is built knowing only a site name and a constant. It is *asked*
    for a shape it was never told about, and answers at exactly that shape.
    Nothing here consults a graph, and nothing could: there is no graph.
    """
    rule = obs_mod.fill({"constraint_income"}, 0.0)
    value = rule.value_for("constraint_income", (27, 1, 2))
    assert value.shape == (27, 1, 2)
    assert (value == 0.0).all()

def test_fill_rule_enumerates_every_site_it_claims() -> None:
    """``sites()`` is load-bearing, not a convenience -- see the module docstring."""
    rule = obs_mod.fill({"constraint_a", "constraint_b"}, 0.0)
    assert rule.sites() == frozenset({"constraint_a", "constraint_b"})

def test_fill_rule_without_a_shape_is_an_error() -> None:
    """A fill cannot guess. Asked for a value with no shape, it says so.

    Callers that only ever hold literals keep the one-argument ``value_for``;
    this is the case where that shortcut is genuinely not answerable, and a
    loud failure beats a scalar that silently broadcasts to anything.
    """
    rules = Observations(rules=(obs_mod.fill({"y"}, 0.0),))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="shape"):
        rules.value_for("y")

def test_literal_rule_returns_its_array_unreshaped() -> None:
    """A literal's array is authoritative about its own contents.

    The shape argument never changes what comes back -- a literal came from
    somewhere real, and quietly reshaping it would be second-guessing data. A3
    added the one thing the shape *is* used for here: agreeing with it. This test
    was written for A2 as ``test_literal_rule_ignores_the_shape_it_is_given``,
    asserting a scalar answered a ``(99, 99)`` site; that is now the rejected
    case, and its own test below.
    """
    values = jnp.asarray([0.4, 0.5, 0.6])
    rule = obs_mod.literal("obs_beta", values)
    assert rule.sites() == frozenset({"obs_beta"})
    assert rule.value_for("obs_beta", (3,)) is values

def test_first_matching_rule_wins() -> None:
    """Resolution is first-match-wins over the list -- the one precedence rule.

    Two mechanisms (``by_site`` beating ``by_family``) collapse into one
    ordering, so a reader can see precedence by reading the list rather than by
    knowing which of two maps is consulted first.
    """
    obs = Observations(
        rules=(obs_mod.literal("y", jnp.full((3,), 7.0)), obs_mod.fill({"y"}, 0.0)),
    )
    assert (obs.value_for("y", (3,)) == 7.0).all()

def test_by_site_still_precedes_by_family() -> None:
    """The compatibility kwargs preserve today's precedence exactly.

    ``by_site``/``by_family`` are both keyed by site id today, so the split is
    documentary rather than functional -- but a ~29-call-site form that predates
    A2 must keep behaving as it did (the additivity constraint that B2 also
    landed under). Both build literal rules; ``by_site`` goes first.
    """
    obs = Observations(by_site={"y": 1.0}, by_family={"y": 2.0})
    assert obs.value_for("y") == 1.0
    assert obs.observed_sites() == frozenset({"y"})

def test_scalar_literal_on_a_multi_cell_site_is_rejected() -> None:
    """The hazard, named: one number cannot be evidence about six cells."""
    rule = obs_mod.literal("obs_beta", 0.4)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="obs_beta"):
        rule.value_for("obs_beta", (2, 3))

def test_partially_broadcasting_literal_is_rejected() -> None:
    """Replication of a *row* is as wrong as replication of a scalar.

    ``(3,)`` against a ``(4, 3)`` site broadcasts cleanly, and each of the three
    numbers would then stand in for four cells. Nothing in the array says which
    of those two readings was meant, which is the point: the caller has to say.
    """
    rule = obs_mod.literal("obs_beta", jnp.asarray([0.1, 0.2, 0.3]))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="obs_beta"):
        rule.value_for("obs_beta", (4, 3))

def test_rejection_names_the_site_and_both_shapes() -> None:
    """The message has to carry the comparison that failed.

    A shape complaint that does not say *which* shapes sends the reader back to
    the graph to work out what the site was; both numbers are in hand here.
    """
    rule = obs_mod.literal("obs_beta", 0.4)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"\(2, 3\)"):
        rule.value_for("obs_beta", (2, 3))

def test_literal_differing_only_by_a_length_one_axis_is_accepted() -> None:
    """The real-data path, preserved deliberately rather than by omission.

    A single-cell observation bundle carries a length-1 array; the site it
    conditions has batch shape ``()``. One number, one cell, no replication --
    so A3 has no complaint, even though the ranks differ. Four production tests
    depend on this (the probe file lists them), and tightening A3 to exact
    equality would break them for no gain in what gets caught.
    """
    rule = obs_mod.literal("obs_beta", jnp.asarray([0.4]))
    assert rule.value_for("obs_beta", ()).shape == (1,)

def test_literal_of_the_right_size_at_a_different_rank_is_accepted() -> None:
    """Stated separately from the case above, because it is the general claim.

    A3's question is "does any element serve more than one cell", not "do the
    shapes match". ``(1, 3)`` into a ``(3,)`` site carries exactly three numbers
    for exactly three cells, so it passes -- and saying so here keeps a later
    reader from tightening the check into rank equality.
    """
    rule = obs_mod.literal("obs_beta", jnp.asarray([[0.1, 0.2, 0.3]]))
    assert rule.value_for("obs_beta", (3,)).shape == (1, 3)

def test_literal_that_does_not_broadcast_at_all_is_rejected() -> None:
    """Size agreement alone is not enough; it must still reach the site.

    ``(3,)`` into a ``(4,)`` site fails today at the NumPyro call, some distance
    from the caller that built it. A3 does not change *whether* this is an
    error, only that the rule itself is where it is noticed.
    """
    rule = obs_mod.literal("obs_beta", jnp.asarray([0.1, 0.2, 0.3]))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        rule.value_for("obs_beta", (4,))

def test_literal_asked_without_a_shape_is_unchecked() -> None:
    """No shape, no check -- and no guess either.

    Callers holding only literals keep the one-argument ``value_for``, and it
    cannot verify anything because nobody has told it what the site is. That is
    a real gap, not a safe default; it is closed by the conditioning point
    always passing the shape, which is what ``inference/compile.py`` does.
    """
    rule = obs_mod.literal("obs_beta", 0.4)
    assert rule.value_for("obs_beta") == 0.4

def test_identity_at_knot_rows(self) -> None:
    # At a grid age coinciding with knot k, the densified value is exactly
    # coefficient k: c_k = f(knot_k).
    B = _hat_basis_matrix(_KNOTS, _GRID)
    # Knots 0, 2, 4 sit at grid indices 0, 2, 4.
    assert jnp.allclose(B[0], jnp.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0]))
    assert jnp.allclose(B[2], jnp.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]))
    assert jnp.allclose(B[4], jnp.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]))

    # Below first knot (ages 0, 1) -> first knot weight 1.
    assert jnp.allclose(B[0], jnp.array([1.0, 0.0]))
    # Above last knot (age 4) -> last knot weight 1.
    assert jnp.allclose(B[4], jnp.array([0.0, 1.0]))

        ),

    out = count_basis.cumulative(keep_disaggregated=("age_basis",))
    assert out.axis_names == ("age_basis",)
    assert out.axes[0].basis is not None
    assert jnp.allclose(out.array, jnp.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]))

    pop = _build_dense_age_pop([20.0, 20.0, 20.0, 20.0, 20.0])
    c1 = [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]
    c2 = [0.4, 0.1, 0.2]

    out2 = _build_basis_rate(c2, pop).cumulative(keep_disaggregated=())
    out_sum = _build_basis_rate(
        [a + b for a, b in zip(c1, c2)], pop
    ).cumulative(keep_disaggregated=())
    assert jnp.allclose(out_sum.array, out1.array + out2.array)

def _build_count_with_pop_2d() -> StructuredArray:
    """A count indicator (not population itself) carrying a population pointer.

    Indicator values (year=2, gender=2) = 10/20/30/40; population = 100/100/
    200/200. Lets us check that a count.cumulative result carries the
    sum-reduced *population*, not a copy of the indicator.
    """
    pop = StructuredArray(
        array=jnp.array([[100.0, 100.0], [200.0, 200.0]]),
        axes=(
            AxisMeta(name="year", levels=(2020, 2025), kind="ordinal"),
            AxisMeta(name="gender", levels=("m", "f"), kind="categorical"),
        ),
        indicator=_pop_meta(),
        population=None,
    )
    return StructuredArray(
        array=jnp.array([[10.0, 20.0], [30.0, 40.0]]),
        axes=pop.axes,
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="internet_users", family="count", unit="people"),
        population=pop,
    )

def test_chained_per_capita_matches_single_full_reduction(self) -> None:
    # The self-consistency commitment: per_capita keeping year, then
    # per_capita to a scalar on the result, must equal a single full-

    pop = _build_pop_2d()

    # sum over age, keep year. Axes (year=2, age_basis=3); population
    # (year=2, age=5).

        array=jnp.array(

def _ttt(d: pd.DataFrame, code: str, source: str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The one total-total-total row per country for an indicator in the demo year.

    The panel carries gender / urban-rural / age-group breakdowns; the genderless
    quantities (income, coverage) use only the ``T`` / ``T`` / ``T`` national
    totals. ``source`` disambiguates indicators that appear under more than one
    source (population; coverage at 2024).
    """
    sub = d[
        (d.indicator_code == code)
        & (d.gender == "T")
        & (d.urban_rural == "T")
        & (d.age_group == "T")
    ]
    if source is not None:
        sub = sub[sub.source_code == source]
    return sub.sort_values("country_iso3")

def gendered_col(
    d: pd.DataFrame,
    code: str,
    countries: tuple[str, ...],
    *,
    source: str | None = None,
    scale: float = 1.0,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """A ``(country, gender)`` array from the F/M rows of a gendered indicator.

    Sparsity is **explicit, never silent**: a (country, gender) cell with no
    matching row is left as ``NaN`` rather than collapsed to zero, so a missing
    gender surfaces as a fitting-time signal (a later observation node can skip
    absent genders) instead of a fabricated value. The urban-rural / age-group
    totals are still required; only the gender axis is split.
    """
    sub = d[
        (d.indicator_code == code)
        & (d.urban_rural == "T")
        & (d.age_group == "T")
        & (d.gender.isin(GENDERS))
    ]
    if source is not None:
        sub = sub[sub.source_code == source]
    out = np.full((len(countries), len(GENDERS)), np.nan)
    country_pos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(countries)}
    for row in sub.itertuples(index=False):
        ci = country_pos.get(row.country_iso3)
        if ci is not None:
            out[ci, GENDERS.index(row.gender)] = float(row.value) * scale
    return out

def load_panel(path: str | Path = DATA_PATH) -> Panel:
    """Load the 2024 national cross-section and freeze the standardization constants.

    Coverage is stored as percentages and divided by 100 here so it lives on
    [0, 1]; the gendered DGG manifestation series (``inet_combined`` /
    ``ownmbl_combined``) are already fractions and load at scale 1.0. The
    genderless quantities (income, coverage) come from the T/T/T rows; the
    gendered quantities (population, the two manifestations) come from their F/M
    rows via :func:`gendered_col`. The standardization ``center`` / ``scale`` are
    computed from this very (genderless) sample -- properties of the observed
    cross-section, not learned quantities.
    """
    df = pd.read_excel(path)
    d = df[df.year == YEAR]

    countries = tuple(sorted(d.country_iso3.unique()))

    def col(code: str, source: str | None = None, scale: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        rows = _ttt(d, code, source)
        if tuple(rows.country_iso3) != countries:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{code}: expected one T/T/T row per country in {countries}; "
                f"got {tuple(rows.country_iso3)}"
            )
        return rows.value.to_numpy(dtype=float) * scale

    income = col(_INCOME_CODE)
    cov_3g = col(_COV_3G_CODE, source=_COV_SOURCE, scale=1.0 / 100.0)
    cov_4g = col(_COV_4G_CODE, source=_COV_SOURCE, scale=1.0 / 100.0)
    mobinet = gendered_col(d, _MOBINET_CODE, countries)  # fraction already
    smartphone = gendered_col(d, _SMARTPHONE_CODE, countries)  # fraction already
    population = gendered_col(d, _POP_CODE, countries, source=_POP_SOURCE)

    log_income = np.log(income)
    return Panel(
        countries=countries,
        genders=GENDERS,
        income=income,
        cov_3g=cov_3g,
        cov_4g=cov_4g,
        mobinet=mobinet,
        smartphone=smartphone,
        population=population,
        income_center=float(log_income.mean()),
        income_scale=float(log_income.std()),
        cov_3g_center=float(cov_3g.mean()),
        cov_3g_scale=float(cov_3g.std()),
        cov_4g_center=float(cov_4g.mean()),
        cov_4g_scale=float(cov_4g.std()),
    )

def _year_axis() -> AxisMeta:
    return AxisMeta(name="year", levels=(YEAR,), kind="ordinal")

def _transition_axis() -> AxisMeta:
    return AxisMeta(name="transition", levels=TRANSITIONS, kind="ordinal")

def _segment_axis() -> AxisMeta:
    return AxisMeta(name="segment", levels=SEGMENTS, kind="ordinal")

def _beta_ab_from_means(means: tuple[float, ...], kappa: float):
    """Mean/concentration -> (a, b) per-segment beta shape params.

    ``a = mean * kappa``, ``b = (1 - mean) * kappa`` so ``Beta(a, b).mean ==
    mean`` and larger ``kappa`` -> tighter. Used to build the monotone-increasing
    manifestation profile priors.
    """
    m = np.asarray(means, dtype=float)
    return m * kappa, (1.0 - m) * kappa

def demo_graph(
    panel: Panel, *, constraint_tightness: float = _CONSTRAINT_TIGHTNESS
) -> BayesGraph:
    """Build the full step-7 segmentation graph for ``panel``.

    ``constraint_tightness`` overrides the shared lambda on the three soft
    constraints. Passing ``0.0`` makes every penalty a constant ``log(0.5)``
    (zero gradient): the same graph behaves as an *unconstrained* fit, which
    is how the behavioral tests build their comparison baseline.
    """
    country = panel.country_axis
    year = _year_axis()
    gender = panel.gender_axis
    transition = _transition_axis()
    driver = _driver_axis()
    segment = _segment_axis()
    cell = (country, year)  # genderless cells (coverage)
    cell_g = (country, year, gender)  # gendered cells (income, population)

    g = BayesGraph()

    # -- split prior nodes (the resolved theta bridge) --------------------------
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="theta_bias",
            kind="prior_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="normal",
                hyperparameters={
                    "loc": 0.0,
                    "scale": _BIAS_SCALE,
                    "axes": (gender, transition),
                },
            ),
            extra={"logit_role": "biases"},
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="theta_weight",
            kind="prior_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="normal",
                hyperparameters={
                    "loc": 0.0,
                    "scale": _WEIGHT_SCALE,
                    "axes": (gender, transition, driver),
                },
            ),
            extra={"logit_role": "weights"},
        )
    )
    mob_a, mob_b = _beta_ab_from_means(_PROFILE_MOBINET_MEAN, _PROFILE_KAPPA)
    sp_a, sp_b = _beta_ab_from_means(_PROFILE_SMARTPHONE_MEAN, _PROFILE_KAPPA)
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="profile_mobinet",
            kind="prior_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="beta",
                hyperparameters={
                    "a": jnp.asarray(mob_a),
                    "b": jnp.asarray(mob_b),
                    "axes": (segment,),
                },
            ),
            extra={"manifestation_role": "profile"},
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="profile_smartphone",
            kind="prior_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="beta",
                hyperparameters={
                    "a": jnp.asarray(sp_a),
                    "b": jnp.asarray(sp_b),
                    "axes": (segment,),
                },
            ),
            extra={"manifestation_role": "profile"},
        )
    )

    # -- driver + population roots ----------------------------------------------
    # Fixed gendered population weights for the income latent's `per_capita`
    # aggregation: same axes, same order as the latent (the `_weight_subset`
    # contract), wrapping the observed F/M head counts from the panel.
    # These weights are frozen to observed census -- NOT the learned `population`
    # latent below. `income_obs` therefore pins the genderless T value against
    # a population-weighted mean at the observed mix; `pop_obs` separately
    # anchors the latent head counts.
    # TODO: In v1 and beyond, the latent population should be the array used
    # for population weighting.
    pop_weights = StructuredArray(
        array=jnp.asarray(
            panel.population.reshape(panel.n_countries, 1, panel.n_genders)
        ),
        axes=cell_g,
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="pop", family="count", unit="people"),
        population=None,
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="income",
            kind="prior_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="lognormal",
                hyperparameters={
                    "loc": panel.income_center,
                    "scale": 1.0,
                    "axes": cell_g,
                    # Per-capita income is intensive: aggregating over gender is
                    # a population-weighted mean, not a sum.
                    "family": "rate",
                    "population": pop_weights,
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="population",
            kind="prior_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="lognormal",
                hyperparameters={
                    "loc": float(np.log(panel.population).mean()),
                    "scale": 3.0,  # population spans ~3 orders of magnitude
                    "axes": cell_g,
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    for cov_id in ("cov_3g", "cov_4g"):
        g.add_node(
            NodeMeta(
                node_id=cov_id,
                kind="prior",
                cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                    family="beta",
                    hyperparameters={"alpha": 1.0, "beta": 1.0, "axes": cell},
                ),
            )
        )

    # -- standardization (frozen center/scale) ----------------------------------
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="income_z",
            kind="zscore",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="standardize",
                hyperparameters={
                    "center": panel.income_center,
                    "scale": panel.income_scale,
                    "transform": "log",
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="cov_3g_z",
            kind="zscore",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="standardize",
                hyperparameters={
                    "center": panel.cov_3g_center,
                    "scale": panel.cov_3g_scale,
                    "transform": "identity",
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="cov_4g_z",
            kind="zscore",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="standardize",
                hyperparameters={
                    "center": panel.cov_4g_center,
                    "scale": panel.cov_4g_scale,
                    "transform": "identity",
                },
            ),
        )
    )

    # -- logits -> simplex -------------------------------------------------------
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="seg_logits",
            kind="linear",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(family="transition_logits"),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="segment_shares",
            kind="segment",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="continuation_ratio",
                hyperparameters={"segment_levels": SEGMENTS},
            ),
        )
    )

    # -- manifestations ----------------------------------------------------------
    for mean_id in ("mobinet_mean", "smartphone_mean"):
        g.add_node(
            NodeMeta(
                node_id=mean_id,
                kind="mixture_mean",
                cpd_spec=CpdSpec(family="manifestation"),
            )
        )

    # -- observations ------------------------------------------------------------
    # income_obs observes the genderless T value against the gendered latent's
    # population-weighted mean over gender (the rate-family per_capita); pop_obs
    # observes the gendered latent elementwise against the F/M data.
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="income_obs",
            kind="observation_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="lognormal",
                hyperparameters={
                    "scale": _OBS_LOGNORMAL_SCALE,
                    "aggregate_over": ("gender",),
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="pop_obs",
            kind="observation_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="lognormal",
                hyperparameters={"scale": _OBS_LOGNORMAL_SCALE},
            ),
        )
    )
    for obs_id in ("cov_3g_obs", "cov_4g_obs", "mobinet_obs", "smartphone_obs"):
        g.add_node(
            NodeMeta(
                node_id=obs_id,
                kind="observation_v0",
                cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                    family="beta",
                    hyperparameters={"concentration": _OBS_BETA_CONCENTRATION},
                ),
            )
        )

    # -- constraints (synthetic Bernoulli children observed at 0) -----------------
    # Roles are assigned via explicit parameter_bindings on every constraint
    # node (uniform with constraint_income, which MUST use them: it binds the
    # one `income` parent to BOTH roles, sliced F vs M -- a cross-role
    # duplicate the validator explicitly allows).
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="constraint_3g",
            kind="constraint_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="bernoulli",
                hyperparameters={
                    "lower_spec": {"axis": "segment", "levels": ("S3", "S4")},
                    "transform": "absolute",
                    "tightness": constraint_tightness,
                },
                parameter_bindings={
                    "lower": ("segment_shares",),
                    "upper": ("cov_3g",),
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="constraint_4g",
            kind="constraint_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="bernoulli",
                hyperparameters={
                    "lower_spec": {"axis": "segment", "levels": ("S4",)},
                    "transform": "absolute",
                    "tightness": constraint_tightness,
                },
                parameter_bindings={
                    "lower": ("segment_shares",),
                    "upper": ("cov_4g",),
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="constraint_income",
            kind="constraint_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="bernoulli",
                hyperparameters={
                    "lower_spec": {"axis": "gender", "levels": ("F",)},
                    "upper_spec": {"axis": "gender", "levels": ("M",)},
                    # Income is positive; the log-difference is the scale-free
                    # footing (vs percentage points for the share ceilings).
                    "transform": "log",
                    "tightness": constraint_tightness,
                },
                parameter_bindings={
                    "lower": ("income",),
                    "upper": ("income",),
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    # Second wave (test list section E): manifestation-based constraints. Both
    # operands descend from segment_shares (mean = sum_k pi_k * profile_k), so
    # the penalty gradient lands on the shares AND the profiles -- the v0
    # stand-in for profile priors. The mean side of each pair takes the whole
    # array (no spec); selection sums the segment axis away on the shares side,
    # so every violation lives on the gendered (country, year, gender) cells.
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="constraint_smartphone",
            kind="constraint_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="bernoulli",
                hyperparameters={
                    # No smartphone -> not AI-ready: pi(S3+) <= smartphone_mean.
                    "lower_spec": {"axis": "segment", "levels": ("S3", "S4")},
                    "transform": "absolute",
                    "tightness": constraint_tightness,
                },
                parameter_bindings={
                    "lower": ("segment_shares",),
                    "upper": ("smartphone_mean",),
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="constraint_mobinet_floor",
            kind="constraint_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="bernoulli",
                hyperparameters={
                    # A subscriber is not totally unconnected:
                    # mobinet_mean <= pi(S2+).
                    "upper_spec": {"axis": "segment", "levels": ("S2", "S3", "S4")},
                    "transform": "absolute",
                    "tightness": constraint_tightness,
                },
                parameter_bindings={
                    "lower": ("mobinet_mean",),
                    "upper": ("segment_shares",),
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="constraint_mobinet_ceiling",
            kind="constraint_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="bernoulli",
                hyperparameters={
                    # No subscription -> not AI-ready: pi(S3+) <= mobinet_mean.
                    "lower_spec": {"axis": "segment", "levels": ("S3", "S4")},
                    "transform": "absolute",
                    "tightness": constraint_tightness,
                },
                parameter_bindings={
                    "lower": ("segment_shares",),
                    "upper": ("mobinet_mean",),
                },
            ),
        )
    )

    # -- edges -------------------------------------------------------------------
    g.add_edge("income", "income_z")
    g.add_edge("cov_3g", "cov_3g_z")
    g.add_edge("cov_4g", "cov_4g_z")

    for parent in ("theta_bias", "theta_weight", "income_z", "cov_3g_z", "cov_4g_z"):
        g.add_edge(parent, "seg_logits")
    g.add_edge("seg_logits", "segment_shares")

    g.add_edge("segment_shares", "mobinet_mean")
    g.add_edge("profile_mobinet", "mobinet_mean")
    g.add_edge("segment_shares", "smartphone_mean")
    g.add_edge("profile_smartphone", "smartphone_mean")

    g.add_edge("income", "income_obs")
    g.add_edge("population", "pop_obs")
    g.add_edge("cov_3g", "cov_3g_obs")
    g.add_edge("cov_4g", "cov_4g_obs")
    g.add_edge("mobinet_mean", "mobinet_obs")
    g.add_edge("smartphone_mean", "smartphone_obs")

    g.add_edge("segment_shares", "constraint_3g")
    g.add_edge("cov_3g", "constraint_3g")
    g.add_edge("segment_shares", "constraint_4g")
    g.add_edge("cov_4g", "constraint_4g")
    # One edge only: the income parent fills both roles via parameter_bindings.
    g.add_edge("income", "constraint_income")

    g.add_edge("segment_shares", "constraint_smartphone")
    g.add_edge("smartphone_mean", "constraint_smartphone")
    g.add_edge("mobinet_mean", "constraint_mobinet_floor")
    g.add_edge("segment_shares", "constraint_mobinet_floor")
    g.add_edge("segment_shares", "constraint_mobinet_ceiling")
    g.add_edge("mobinet_mean", "constraint_mobinet_ceiling")

    return g

def cell(a: np.ndarray) -> jnp.ndarray:
    return jnp.asarray(a.reshape(panel.n_countries, 1))

def cell_g(a: np.ndarray) -> jnp.ndarray:
    return jnp.asarray(a.reshape(panel.n_countries, 1, panel.n_genders))

def national_segment_counts(result: InferenceResult) -> xr.DataArray:
    """``pi x pop`` per country and segment from a fitted ``InferenceResult``.

    Reads the single MAP draw of ``segment_shares`` (country, year, gender,
    segment) and the fitted latent ``population`` (country, year, gender), and
    multiplies. xarray aligns by dimension name, so the per-segment counts are
    driven by axis metadata, not hard-coded positions; summing over ``segment``
    returns the per-gender population (mass conserved).
    """
    shares = result.posterior["segment_shares"].isel(chain=0, draw=0)
    pop = result.posterior["population"].isel(chain=0, draw=0)
    return shares * pop

def fit_demo(
    panel: Panel | None = None, *, steps: int = 3000, lr: float = 0.05, seed: int = 0
) -> tuple[InferenceResult, Panel]:
    """Convenience: load (if needed), compile, and MAP-fit the demo graph."""
    panel = panel or load_panel()
    graph = demo_graph(panel)
    model = compile_model(graph)
    result = run_map(
        model, graph, demo_observations(panel), steps=steps, lr=lr, seed=seed
    )
    return result, panel

    # Every segment carries non-trivial mass in at least one country.

def test_latent_income_tracks_observed(fitted, panel: demo.Panel) -> None:
    """12. The latent's gender aggregate per country is close to observed T income.

    The latent is gendered; the genderless ``income_obs`` anchors its
    population-weighted mean over gender, so that aggregate -- not the
    individual F/M slices -- is what the tight likelihood (scale 0.1) pins.
    """
    income = fitted.posterior["income"].isel(chain=0, draw=0)
    countries = list(income.coords["country"].values)
    assert tuple(income.coords["gender"].values) == demo.GENDERS
    latent = income.values.reshape(len(countries), panel.n_genders)
    pop_by_country = dict(zip(panel.countries, panel.population))
    weights = np.array([pop_by_country[c] for c in countries])
    aggregate = (latent * weights).sum(axis=1) / weights.sum(axis=1)
    observed = dict(zip(panel.countries, panel.income))
    expected = np.array([observed[c] for c in countries])
    np.testing.assert_allclose(aggregate, expected, rtol=0.1)

def test_manifestation_means_track_observed(fitted, panel: demo.Panel) -> None:
    """13. Fitted mobinet/smartphone means sit near the observed F/M indicators."""
    for mean_id, obs_name in (
        ("mobinet_mean", "mobinet"),
        ("smartphone_mean", "smartphone"),
    ):
        mean = fitted.posterior[mean_id].isel(chain=0, draw=0)
        countries = list(mean.coords["country"].values)
        assert tuple(mean.coords["gender"].values) == demo.GENDERS
        fitted_vals = mean.values.reshape(len(countries), panel.n_genders)
        observed = dict(zip(panel.countries, _observed(panel, obs_name)))
        expected = np.stack([observed[c] for c in countries])
        # Conditioned result moved toward the data: positively correlated and
        # not far off in absolute terms (v0 tolerance).
        assert np.corrcoef(fitted_vals.reshape(-1), expected.reshape(-1))[0, 1] > 0.5
        assert np.abs(fitted_vals - expected).mean() < 0.2

def test_counts_are_coherent(fitted, panel: demo.Panel) -> None:
    """14. ``pi x pop`` counts are >= 0 and sum over segments to the population."""
    counts = demo.national_segment_counts(fitted)
    assert (counts.values >= -1e-3).all()
    pop = fitted.posterior["population"].isel(chain=0, draw=0)
    total = counts.sum("segment")
    np.testing.assert_allclose(total.values, pop.values, rtol=1e-4)

def test_income_monotonicity(fitted, panel: demo.Panel) -> None:
    """15. Log income correlates positively with high-segment mass across countries."""
    countries = _country_order(fitted, "segment_shares")
    log_income = dict(zip(panel.countries, np.log(panel.income)))
    shares = fitted.posterior["segment_shares"].isel(chain=0, draw=0).values
    shares = shares.reshape(len(countries), len(demo.GENDERS), len(demo.SEGMENTS))
    seg_index = np.arange(len(demo.SEGMENTS))
    # E[segment] per (country, gender), averaged over gender: the observed
    # income is the genderless T value, so compare against the national mean.
    expected_segment = (shares @ seg_index).mean(axis=1)
    x = np.array([log_income[c] for c in countries])
    assert np.corrcoef(x, expected_segment)[0, 1] > 0.0

def test_national_numbers_are_reasonable(fitted, panel: demo.Panel) -> None:
    """16. Implied manifestation means land within/around the observed spread."""
    for mean_id, obs_name in (
        ("mobinet_mean", "mobinet"),
        ("smartphone_mean", "smartphone"),
    ):
        countries = _country_order(fitted, mean_id)
        observed = _observed(panel, obs_name)
        lo, hi = observed.min(), observed.max()
        fitted_vals = fitted.posterior[mean_id].isel(chain=0, draw=0).values.reshape(-1)
        # Every fitted mean is a valid share and within a margin of the observed
        # cross-country range (no country implausibly far from its adoption).
        assert (fitted_vals > 0.0).all() and (fitted_vals < 1.0).all()
        margin = 0.15
        assert (fitted_vals >= lo - margin).all()
        assert (fitted_vals <= hi + margin).all()

def test_gendered_vs_genderless_axes(fitted) -> None:
    """G13. The gender axis lands exactly where the design puts it.

    Gendered: the income latent and its standardization, population, the logits
    / shares, and the manifestation means. Genderless: coverage and its

    post = fitted.posterior

def test_income_anchored_via_gender_aggregation(graph: BayesGraph, panel: demo.Panel) -> None:
    """G16. Gendered income latent, prior otherwise unchanged, anchored to T via per_capita.

    The latent gains only the gender axis (LogNormal(income_center, 1.0) as
    before), is declared family="rate" with the gendered population as weights,

    assert tuple(obs_hp["aggregate_over"]) == ("gender",)

def test_t_is_output_aggregation_never_a_cell(fitted, panel: demo.Panel) -> None:
    """G24. T = F count + M count, derived in the output layer; no T cell anywhere."""
    # No gender == "T" cell in the posterior...
    for name, da in fitted.posterior.data_vars.items():
        if "gender" in da.dims:
            assert "T" not in set(da.coords["gender"].values), name
    # ...or in the per-cell sheets.
    tables = output.result_tables(fitted)
    for sheet in (output.SHEET_SEGMENT_SHARES, output.SHEET_NATIONAL_SUMMARY):
        assert "T" not in set(tables[sheet]["gender"])

    total = counts.sum("gender")
    np.testing.assert_allclose(

def _share_violation(result, cov_name: str, levels: tuple[str, ...]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Per-cell ``pi(levels) - cov``: positive where the ceiling is breached."""
    shares = result.posterior["segment_shares"].isel(chain=0, draw=0)
    pi = shares.sel(segment=list(levels)).sum("segment")  # (country, year, gender)
    cov = result.posterior[cov_name].isel(chain=0, draw=0)  # broadcasts over gender
    return (pi - cov).values

def _mean_positive(violation: np.ndarray) -> float:
    return float(np.clip(violation, 0.0, None).mean())

def _manifestation_violation(
    result, mean_name: str, levels: tuple[str, ...], *, mean_is_lower: bool
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Per-cell violation between a manifestation mean and a share sum.

    ``mean_is_lower=True`` is the floor shape (``mean - pi(levels)``);
    ``False`` is the ceiling/smartphone shape (``pi(levels) - mean``).
    Positive where the constraint is breached.
    """
    shares = result.posterior["segment_shares"].isel(chain=0, draw=0)
    pi = shares.sel(segment=list(levels)).sum("segment")
    mean = result.posterior[mean_name].isel(chain=0, draw=0)
    gap = (mean - pi) if mean_is_lower else (pi - mean)
    return gap.values

def test_mobinet_floor_penalizes_violating_configuration(
    panel: demo.Panel, graph: BayesGraph
) -> None:
    """E27. The floor's penalty, pinned at the joint level by substitution.

    No observation surgery makes a *fit* breach this floor: the violation
    ``mobinet_mean - pi(S2+)`` needs pi(S1) large at the same time as a high
    mobinet mean, and with the shares unobserved the optimizer always escapes
    by moving mass up-segment (probed: pi(S1) -> 0.000 in every engineered
    scenario). The floor is insurance for configurations reached by other
    routes (scenario surgery, future priors), so this test substitutes such a
    configuration into the compiled model directly and checks the site's
    log-prob against the closed form -softplus(lambda * violation).
    """
    model = compile_model(graph)
    observations = demo.demo_observations(panel)

    def floor_log_prob(bias: float, profile: tuple[float, ...]) -> np.ndarray:
        # Zero driver weights make seg_logits = bias everywhere, so the bias
        # alone places the share mass; the profile sets mobinet_mean.
        substitutions = {
            "theta_bias": jnp.full(
                (panel.n_genders, len(demo.TRANSITIONS)), bias
            ),
            "theta_weight": jnp.zeros(
                (panel.n_genders, len(demo.TRANSITIONS), len(demo.DRIVERS))
            ),
            "profile_mobinet": jnp.asarray(profile),
        }
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
                with numpyro.handlers.substitute(data=substitutions):
                    model(observations=observations)
        site = tr["constraint_mobinet_floor"]
        assert site["is_observed"]
        log_prob = np.asarray(site["fn"].log_prob(site["value"]))
        # Closed form from the traced deterministics (trailing axis = segment).
        shares = np.asarray(tr["segment_shares"]["value"])
        mean = np.asarray(tr["mobinet_mean"]["value"])
        violation = mean - shares[..., 1:].sum(axis=-1)
        expected = -np.logaddexp(0.0, demo._CONSTRAINT_TIGHTNESS * violation)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(log_prob, expected, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)
        return log_prob

    # Bias -15 kills every transition (everyone unconnected) while the S1
    # mobinet profile sits near 1: mobinet_mean ~0.95 over pi(S2+) ~0, a
    # gross breach penalized ~ -softplus(50 * 0.95) ~ -47 per cell.
    violating = floor_log_prob(-15.0, (0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98))
    # Bias +15 sends everyone to S4: pi(S2+) ~1 over mean ~0.6, satisfied.
    satisfying = floor_log_prob(15.0, (0.05, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6))
    assert (violating < -40.0).all()
    assert (satisfying > -0.5).all()
    assert satisfying.min() > violating.max() + 40.0

def test_divergent_node_id_and_sheet_code_survive_desugar() -> None:
    """The property H1 exists for, asserted where it is cheap to assert.

    ``income`` declares sheet code ``dispinc_pc``. Two different consumers must
    read two different keys off that one node, and getting them crossed is the
    defect class this config was built to catch:

    - the *data* side asks for ``dispinc_pc`` -- that is the sheet the loader
      reads and the code the observation cells reference;
    - the *graph* side asks for ``income`` -- that is what claims a coefficient
      level on the child ``handset_smt``, because the runtime matches predictors
      on ``StructuredArray.node_id``.
    """
    cfg = desugar(_load())
    income = next(n for n in cfg.nodes if n.id == "income")
    assert income.indicator == "dispinc_pc"

    # The child's coefficient axis names the parent node, not its sheet code.
    levels = tuple(cfg.axes["handset_smt__coefficient"].levels)
    assert "income" in levels
    assert "dispinc_pc" not in levels

def _observed_indicators(res) -> set[str]:
    """Every indicator observed anywhere in the graph.

    One read per node, not per cell: E2's grid node covers a single
    ``(indicator, source, unit)`` triple and carries the code as a scalar
    hyperparameter. The set is still the right shape to ask for -- an indicator can
    be observed by more than one source (``cov_4g`` is, by GSMAINT and ITU) -- and
    reading only one node was what made the original version of this check look
    like an indicator gate when it was partly a family split.
    """
    return {
        str(node.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["indicator"])
        for node in res.graph.nodes()
        if node.role == "observation"
    }

def test_output_is_a_simplex_over_the_declared_segments() -> None:
    """K segments in the transition axis's place, summing to 1 in every cell."""
    model = compile_model(_graph())
    out = numpyro.handlers.seed(model, jax.random.PRNGKey(0))()

    seg = out["skill_seg"]
    # Segment leads, because `linear_predictor` builds the union grid with
    # mean_coeffs' own non-coefficient axes first and the predictors' axes after --
    # so the transition axis, which the segment axis replaces in place, comes out
    # in front.
    #
    # **This order is not load-bearing, and should not become so.** It is pinned
    # because it is worth knowing when it changes, not because anything depends on
    # it: the grid is addressed by axis *name* everywhere downstream (selection,
    # observation routing, labeling), and the only positional axis convention in
    # the library is the bundle axis at index 0, which is a different axis space.
    # So if this line fails because someone reordered the union grid, that is
    # information rather than a defect -- check that the axis *set* and the
    # per-axis metadata below are unchanged, then update the expectation. What
    # would be a real defect is a consumer that broke alongside it.
    assert tuple(a.name for a in seg.axes) == ("segment", "country", "year")
    assert seg.array.shape == (_N_SEGMENTS, _N_COUNTRIES, _N_YEARS)

    # The declared labels, and the role a downstream consumer asks for -- located
    # by name rather than by position, so this half of the test survives a
    # reordering even though the assertion above does not.
    (seg_axis,) = [a for a in seg.axes if a.name == "segment"]
    assert seg_axis.levels == _SEGMENTS
    assert seg_axis.axis_role == "segmentation"
    assert seg_axis.kind == "ordinal"

    # Structural, not enforced: the transform telescopes, and the recursion is a
    # convex combination of simplex points, so no year can drift off the simplex.
    seg_pos = seg.axis_names.index("segment")
    assert np.allclose(np.asarray(seg.array).sum(axis=seg_pos), 1.0)
    assert bool((seg.array >= 0.0).all())

def _logits_prior(
    resolved_bindings: Mapping[str, tuple[StructuredArray, ...]],
    *,
    sample_fn: Any,
    deterministic_fn: Any,
    hyperparameters: Mapping[str, Any],
    name: str,
) -> StructuredArray:
    """Latent logit field ~ Normal(0, 1) over (country, year, segment)."""
    value = sample_fn(name, dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0).expand(_SHAPE).to_event(3))
    return StructuredArray(
        array=value,
        axes=AXES,
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator=name, family="rate", unit="logit"),
        population=None,
    )

def _softmax_segments(
    resolved_bindings: Mapping[str, tuple[StructuredArray, ...]],
    *,
    sample_fn: Any,
    deterministic_fn: Any,
    hyperparameters: Mapping[str, Any],
    name: str,
) -> StructuredArray:
    """Deterministic softmax over the segment axis -> a per-unit K-simplex."""
    logits = resolved_bindings["logits"][0]
    shares = jax.nn.softmax(logits.array, axis=-1)
    value = deterministic_fn(name, shares)
    return StructuredArray(
        array=value,
        axes=AXES,
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator=name, family="rate", unit="share"),
        population=None,
    )

def register() -> None:
    """Install the synthetic CPDs (call after ``_clear_registry``)."""
    register_cpd(
        "axnormal",
        "prior",
        _logits_prior,
        kind="stochastic",
    )
    register_cpd(
        "axsoftmax",
        "segment",
        _softmax_segments,
        kind="deterministic",
        parameter_schema={
            "logits": ParamDecl(
                description="Logit field parent; exactly one.",
                min_count=1,
                max_count=1,
            ),
        },
        resolve_bindings=_resolve_logits,
    )

def test_map_runs_and_lands_near_prior_mode(
    single_node_graph: BayesGraph,
) -> None:
    """AutoDelta + SVI on the unobserved model should land near 0.5.

    AutoDelta is NumPyro's MAP guide: a Delta distribution at a learnable
    location, optimized by SVI (the entropy term vanishes for a Delta, so
    ELBO maximization reduces to log-joint maximization → MAP).

    NumPyro's AutoDelta places the Delta in *unconstrained* parameter
    space; the location is back-transformed through the bijector when
    queried. The two-node test discusses the Jacobian implications in
    detail; for the symmetric Beta(2,2) prior here, the unconstrained-
    space MAP back-transforms to the same point as the original-space
    MAP (0.5), so we don't need to worry about it.
    """
    model = compile_model(single_node_graph)
    guide = AutoDelta(model)
    svi = infer.SVI(model, guide, numpyro.optim.Adam(0.05), loss=infer.Trace_ELBO())
    svi_result = svi.run(jax.random.PRNGKey(0), num_steps=1000)
    map_estimate = float(guide.median(svi_result.params)["theta"])

    assert 0.0 <= map_estimate <= 1.0
    assert abs(map_estimate - 0.5) < 0.02

def test_svi_normal_runs_and_approximates_prior(
    single_node_graph: BayesGraph,
) -> None:
    """AutoNormal + SVI on the unobserved model should approximate the prior.

    AutoNormal is a mean-field guide: independent Gaussians in
    unconstrained space, mapped back through the bijector at sample
    time. For the symmetric Beta(2,2) prior, the back-transformed
    Gaussian's mean should be close to 0.5; the test confirms the
    inference path runs and the result is sensibly located.
    """
    model = compile_model(single_node_graph)
    guide = AutoNormal(model)
    svi = infer.SVI(model, guide, numpyro.optim.Adam(0.05), loss=infer.Trace_ELBO())
    svi_result = svi.run(jax.random.PRNGKey(0), num_steps=2000)
    samples = guide.sample_posterior(
        jax.random.PRNGKey(1), svi_result.params, sample_shape=(2000,)
    )
    theta = np.asarray(samples["theta"])

    assert theta.shape == (2000,)
    assert ((theta >= 0.0) & (theta <= 1.0)).all()
    # Mean-field Gaussian on logit(θ), pushed back through sigmoid, should
    # be near 0.5 for the symmetric prior; 0.05 is well above approximation
    # noise on 2000 samples after 2000 optimization steps.
    assert abs(theta.mean() - 0.5) < 0.05

def test_nuts_recovers_conjugate_posterior(two_node_graph: BayesGraph) -> None:
    """NUTS posterior over θ matches the analytic Beta(α+k, β+N-k) mean.

    With α=β=2, N=20, k=14, the posterior is Beta(16, 8) with mean 2/3.
    The single-node toy could only check the prior (no data); here the
    posterior is meaningfully shifted from the prior mean of 0.5, so a
    broken parent-value or observation path would visibly miss the target.
    """
    model = compile_model(two_node_graph)
    kernel = infer.NUTS(model)
    mcmc = infer.MCMC(
        kernel, num_warmup=500, num_samples=1000, progress_bar=False
    )
    mcmc.run(
        jax.random.PRNGKey(0),
        observations=Observations(by_site={"k": OBSERVED_K}),
    )
    theta = np.asarray(mcmc.get_samples()["theta"])

    # Analytic posterior: Beta(α + k, β + N − k).
    post_alpha = PRIOR_ALPHA + OBSERVED_K
    post_beta = PRIOR_BETA + (N_TRIALS - OBSERVED_K)
    expected_mean = post_alpha / (post_alpha + post_beta)
    expected_var = (
        post_alpha * post_beta
        / ((post_alpha + post_beta) ** 2 * (post_alpha + post_beta + 1))
    )

    assert theta.shape == (1000,)
    assert ((theta >= 0.0) & (theta <= 1.0)).all()
    # Posterior mean ~0.667; tolerance 0.03 is well above MCMC Monte Carlo
    # error on 1000 samples but well below the prior-vs-posterior shift
    # (~0.17), so a broken parent → child path would fail this.
    assert abs(theta.mean() - expected_mean) < 0.03
    assert abs(theta.var() - expected_var) < 0.01

def test_map_recovers_mode(two_node_graph: BayesGraph) -> None:
    """AutoDelta + SVI lands at the Beta(16, 8) posterior mode 15/22.

    With α=β=2, N=20, k=14, the posterior is Beta(16, 8) with mode
    (α−1)/(α+β−2) = 15/22 ≈ 0.682. Distinct from the posterior mean
    (16/24 ≈ 0.667), so getting the mode right is a real check.
    """
    model = compile_model(two_node_graph)
    guide = AutoDelta(model)
    svi = infer.SVI(model, guide, numpyro.optim.Adam(0.05), loss=infer.Trace_ELBO())
    svi_result = svi.run(
        jax.random.PRNGKey(0),
        num_steps=2000,
        observations=Observations(by_site={"k": OBSERVED_K}),
    )
    map_estimate = float(guide.median(svi_result.params)["theta"])

    # AutoDelta does MAP in the variable's original (constrained) space --
    # see its docstring: "This class does MAP inference in constrained
    # space." It uses an unconstrained-space *parameterization* for
    # unrestricted gradient steps, but the ELBO is evaluated at the
    # constrained value with no Jacobian correction, so the optimum sits
    # at d/dθ log p(x, θ) = 0 -- the original-space mode. Not a bug to
    # "fix."
    post_alpha = PRIOR_ALPHA + OBSERVED_K
    post_beta = PRIOR_BETA + (N_TRIALS - OBSERVED_K)
    expected_mode = (post_alpha - 1) / (post_alpha + post_beta - 2)

    assert 0.0 <= map_estimate <= 1.0
    assert abs(map_estimate - expected_mode) < 0.01

def test_svi_normal_approximates_conjugate_posterior(
    two_node_graph: BayesGraph,
) -> None:
    """AutoNormal SVI posterior mean matches the analytic Beta(16, 8) mean.

    AutoNormal is a mean-field Gaussian guide in unconstrained space.
    For the near-symmetric Beta(16, 8) posterior, the back-transformed
    Gaussian's mean is close to (but not exactly) the analytic posterior
    mean -- a small approximation bias that mean-field SVI carries on
    bounded-support variables. Tolerance 0.05 is well above approximation
    noise after 2000 steps and well below the prior-to-posterior shift,
    so a broken parent → child path or a broken obs path would fail.
    """
    model = compile_model(two_node_graph)

    svi = infer.SVI(model, guide, numpyro.optim.Adam(0.05), loss=infer.Trace_ELBO())
    svi_result = svi.run(
        jax.random.PRNGKey(0),
        num_steps=2000,
        observations=Observations(by_site={"k": OBSERVED_K}),
    )
    samples = guide.sample_posterior(
        jax.random.PRNGKey(1), svi_result.params, sample_shape=(2000,)
    )
    theta = np.asarray(samples["theta"])

    post_alpha = PRIOR_ALPHA + OBSERVED_K
    post_beta = PRIOR_BETA + (N_TRIALS - OBSERVED_K)
    expected_mean = post_alpha / (post_alpha + post_beta)

    assert theta.shape == (2000,)
    assert ((theta >= 0.0) & (theta <= 1.0)).all()
    assert abs(theta.mean() - expected_mean) < 0.05

def _graph(*, bundle: str | None = "obs_bundle", chain: bool = False) -> BayesGraph:
    """Two latents, each observed by a grid; the grids share ``bundle``.

    With ``chain``, the second grid also takes the first as a parent, which is
    the ancestry hazard ``_group_into_steps`` refuses.
    """
    g = BayesGraph()
    for tag, values in (("a", (0.1, 0.2, 0.3)), ("b", (1.0, 2.0, 3.0))):
        g.add_node(
            NodeMeta(
                node_id=f"lat_{tag}",
                kind="latent",
                indicator=f"ind_{tag}",
                cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                    family="testutil",
                    constructor="constant_latent",
                    hyperparameters={"values": values, "indicator": f"ind_{tag}"},
                ),
            )
        )
        g.add_node(
            NodeMeta(
                node_id=f"obs_{tag}",
                kind="observation",
                bundle_id=bundle,
                cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                    family="normal",
                    constructor="observation_grid",
                    parameter_bindings={"latent": (f"lat_{tag}",)},
                    hyperparameters={
                        "indicator": f"ind_{tag}",
                        "source": "src",
                        "unit": "1",
                        "axes": {"country": list(COUNTRY)},
                    },
                ),
            )
        )
        g.add_edge(f"lat_{tag}", f"obs_{tag}")
    if chain:
        g.add_edge("obs_a", "obs_b")
    return g

def test_an_unambiguous_axis_keeps_its_bare_name() -> None:

def test_suffix_is_a_deterministic_function_of_the_ordered_levels() -> None:
    """Pinned to golden values, deliberately.

    A test that only compared two calls in one process would pass under
    ``hash(frozenset(...))``, whose whole defect is that it changes *between*
    processes. Goldens are what make the process-salted implementation fail.

    Order is part of the input: the two orderings of one pair must differ,
    because they are two different coord lists.
    """
    assert level_set_suffix(("dispinc_pc",)) == SUFFIX_DISPINC
    assert level_set_suffix(("cov_4g",)) == SUFFIX_COV4G
    assert level_set_suffix(("KE", "NG")) == SUFFIX_KE_NG
    assert level_set_suffix(("NG", "KE")) == SUFFIX_NG_KE
    assert SUFFIX_KE_NG != SUFFIX_NG_KE

    # Type tags: same text, different coord dtype, so different dims.
    assert level_set_suffix((2019, 2020)) != level_set_suffix(("2019", "2020"))

    # ...but a numpy scalar is the same level as its Python equivalent.
    assert level_set_suffix((np.str_("KE"), np.str_("NG"))) == SUFFIX_KE_NG
    assert level_set_suffix((np.int64(2019),)) == level_set_suffix((2019,))

def test_suffix_ignores_surrounding_context() -> None:
    """The property that makes saved output comparable across runs: the suffix
    depends on the level set alone -- not on what else is in the graph, not on
    which node is visited first, not on dict iteration order.

    Without it, adding an unrelated node renames yesterday's dims and yesterday's
    netCDF file stops lining up with today's.
    """
    assert level_set_suffix(("KE", "NG")) == SUFFIX_KE_NG

    # Same levels reached by nodes declared in either order, in graphs of
    # different size, yield the same dim name.
    small = to_inference_data(
        {"a": _node(("KE", "NG"), axis="country"), "b": _node(("KE",), axis="country")}
    )
    large = to_inference_data(
        {
            "b": _node(("KE",), axis="country"),
            "z": _node(("dispinc_pc",)),
            "a": _node(("KE", "NG"), axis="country"),
        }
    )
    expected = f"country__{SUFFIX_KE_NG}"
    assert expected in small["posterior"].coords
    assert expected in large["posterior"].coords

def _register_guesser() -> None:
    """A parentless root that does what every real constructor does.

    It stamps the site name it was handed as the indicator code -- the only guess
    available to it -- along with a ``family``/``unit`` pair it does know.
    """

    def guesser(
        resolved_bindings: Mapping[str, tuple[StructuredArray, ...]],
        *,
        sample_fn: SampleFn,
        deterministic_fn: DeterministicFn,
        hyperparameters: Mapping[str, Any],
        name: str,
    ) -> StructuredArray:
        del resolved_bindings, sample_fn, hyperparameters
        return StructuredArray(
            array=deterministic_fn(name, jnp.array([0.25, 0.75])),
            axes=(GENDER,),
            indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator=name, family="rate", unit="fraction"),
            population=None,
        )

    register_cpd(
        "testutil",
        "guesser",
        guesser,
        kind="deterministic",
        parameter_schema={},
        hyperparameter_schema={},
        resolve_bindings=lambda *, child, parents, hyperparameters: {},
    )

def guesser(

    return StructuredArray(

def _run(node_id: str, indicator: str | None) -> StructuredArray:

            indicator=indicator,
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(family="testutil", constructor="guesser"),
        )
    )
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        return compile_model(g)()[node_id]

def test_only_the_code_is_restated() -> None:
    """``family`` and ``unit`` are the constructor's to state, and survive.

    ``family`` in particular is load-bearing -- it is what the reduction dispatch
    keys off -- so a stamp that rebuilt the whole ``IndicatorMeta`` from the config
    would quietly change how the value reduces.
    """
    out = _run("income", "dispinc_pc")
    assert (out.indicator.family, out.indicator.unit) == ("rate", "fraction")
    # And the rest of the value is untouched by either stamp.
    assert out.axes == (GENDER,)
    assert jnp.allclose(out.array, jnp.array([0.25, 0.75]))

def test_bundle_sum_consumer_produces_outer_sum() -> None:
    gender = AxisMeta(name="gender", levels=("F", "M"), kind="categorical")
    country = AxisMeta(name="country", levels=("A", "B", "C"), kind="categorical")
    g = jnp.array([1.0, 2.0])           # F, M
    c = jnp.array([10.0, 20.0, 30.0])   # A, B, C
    loc_flat = jnp.concatenate([g, c])  # bundle layout: gender atom, country atom

    g_ = BayesGraph()
    # The bundle labels its entries with the *sum node's* (id, "atoms") key —
    # exactly what the inline desugar interposition emits.
    g_.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="eff_bundle",
            kind="parameter",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="normal",
                constructor="bundled",
                hyperparameters={
                    "entries": (
                        {"consumer_id": "c1_sum", "role": "atoms", "axes": (gender,)},
                        {"consumer_id": "c1_sum", "role": "atoms", "axes": (country,)},
                    ),
                    "loc": loc_flat,
                    "scale": 1.0,
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    g_.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="c1_sum",
            kind="deterministic",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="effect_group",
                constructor="sum",
                parameter_bindings={"atoms": ("eff_bundle",)},
            ),
        )
    )
    g_.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="c1",
            kind="deterministic",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="testutil",
                constructor="passthrough",
                parameter_bindings={"param": ("c1_sum",)},
            ),
        )
    )
    g_.add_edge("eff_bundle", "c1_sum")
    g_.add_edge("c1_sum", "c1")

    model = compile_model(g_)
    # Fix the bundle draw to loc_flat so the downstream deterministic sum is exact.
    fixed = numpyro.handlers.substitute(model, data={"eff_bundle": loc_flat})
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        sampled = fixed()

    out = sampled["c1"]
    assert out.axes == (gender, country)
    expected = g[:, None] + c[None, :]  # result[i, j] = gender[i] + country[j]
    assert jnp.allclose(out.array, expected)

def test_compile_two_consumers_share_one_bundle_site() -> None:
    """Plan §M4.3: two consumers, one bundle sample site, shaped via unbundle."""
    country = AxisMeta(name="country", levels=("A", "B", "C"), kind="categorical")
    gender = AxisMeta(name="gender", levels=("F", "M"), kind="categorical")
    loc_flat = jnp.concatenate([jnp.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]), jnp.array([10.0, 20.0])])

    g = BayesGraph()
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="theta_bundle",
            kind="parameter",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="normal",
                constructor="bundled",
                hyperparameters={
                    "entries": (
                        {
                            "consumer_id": "node_a",
                            "role": "param",
                            "axes": (country,),
                        },
                        {
                            "consumer_id": "node_b",
                            "role": "param",
                            "axes": (gender,),
                        },
                    ),
                    "loc": loc_flat,
                    "scale": 1.0,
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    for nid in ("node_a", "node_b"):
        g.add_node(
            NodeMeta(
                node_id=nid,
                kind="passthrough",
                cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                    family="testutil",
                    constructor="passthrough",
                    # Plain binding to the shared bundle — design doc §E.
                    parameter_bindings={"param": ("theta_bundle",)},
                ),
            )
        )
        g.add_edge("theta_bundle", nid)

    model = compile_model(g)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        sampled = model()

    assert sampled["theta_bundle"].axes[0].name == BUNDLE_AXIS_NAME
    assert sampled["node_a"].axes == (country,)
    assert sampled["node_b"].axes == (gender,)
    # Mean of Normal(loc, 1) is loc — seed path uses free sampling; check shapes.
    assert sampled["node_a"].array.shape == (3,)
    assert sampled["node_b"].array.shape == (2,)
    # Single stochastic site for the bundle (consumers are deterministic).
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        tr = numpyro.handlers.trace(model).get_trace()
    sample_sites = [
        k for k, v in tr.items() if v["type"] == "sample" and not v.get("is_observed")
    ]
    assert sample_sites == ["theta_bundle"]
