def test_auto_buildable_param_classification(_pipeline_registry) -> None:
    buildable = {
        (family, ctor, role)
        for family in REGISTRY
        for ctor in REGISTRY[family]
        for role, decl in REGISTRY[family][ctor].parameter_schema.items()
        if is_auto_buildable_param(decl)
    }
    # The biases/weights of the two linear-structural constructors, plus the
    # mean_coeffs of every constructor built on `linear_predictor` (M3b step 3:
    # the Type-II latent's linear predictor is an auto-built effect-group bundle).
    # The two temporal entries appear here for exactly the same reason
    # normal.truncated does -- they share that parameter schema, which is the point
    # of the fused constructors; temporal.segment_v0's differs only in also
    # carrying the transition axis. segment_ordered_v0 reuses that same surface
    # (shared slopes + ordered thresholds from the bias row). The equality excludes
    # drivers/logits/shares/profile and every obs role.
    assert buildable == {
        ("transition_logits", "linear", "biases"),
        ("transition_logits", "linear", "weights"),
        ("dirichlet", "segment_v0", "biases"),
        ("dirichlet", "segment_v0", "weights"),
        ("normal", "truncated", "mean_coeffs"),
        ("temporal", "truncated_v0", "mean_coeffs"),
        ("temporal", "segment_v0", "mean_coeffs"),
        ("temporal", "segment_ordered_v0", "mean_coeffs"),
    }

def test_normalized_parent_contributes_its_indicator_not_the_z_node() -> None:
    """<=v3. A coefficient level is the indicator the channel arrives under.

    ``standardize`` propagates its parent's ``IndicatorMeta`` unchanged *below v4*,
    so the predictor reaching ``normal.truncated`` announces itself as ``income``,
    not ``income_z``. Naming the synthesized node here makes the runtime match fail.

    Still the correct answer for a v3 config, and quarantined as such -- see
    ``test_v4_normalized_parent_contributes_the_z_node_id`` for the inversion.
    """
    consumer = _truncated("mob")
    consumer["parents"] = [{"id": "income", "normalize": {"transform": "identity"}}]
    cfg = desugar(_cfg([consumer, _plain("income")]))
    assert tuple(cfg.axes["mob__coefficient"].levels) == ("bias", "income")

def test_v4_declared_indicator_does_not_reach_the_coefficient_levels() -> None:
    """The divergent case, stated the v4 way: the level is ``income``, not its code.

    This is H1's failure in miniature. The node declares sheet code ``dispinc_pc``
    and the stamp puts that on the value's ``IndicatorMeta`` -- but the value's
    ``node_id`` is ``income``, and that is what claims a coefficient level. Naming
    the code here is what produced "predictor 'income' has no matching coefficient
    level; coefficient levels: ['bias', 'dispinc_pc']".
    """
    parent = _plain("income") | {"indicator": "dispinc_pc"}
    cfg = desugar(_cfg4([_truncated("mob"), parent], edges=[["income", "mob"]]))
    assert tuple(cfg.axes["mob__coefficient"].levels) == ("bias", "income")

def test_v4_normalized_parent_contributes_the_z_node_id() -> None:
    """No hop. The standardizer is the parent, so the standardizer names the level.

    Below v4 hopping past the ``_z`` node was required, because the standardizer
    advertised its parent's code. From v4 it is not merely unnecessary but wrong:
    the ``_z`` node arrives announcing its own id, so a level named ``income``
    would be claimed by nobody.
    """
    consumer = _truncated("mob")
    consumer["parents"] = [{"id": "income", "normalize": {"transform": "identity"}}]
    cfg = desugar(_cfg4([consumer, _plain("income")]))
    assert tuple(cfg.axes["mob__coefficient"].levels) == ("bias", "income_z")

def test_role_omitted_comes_from_constructor(_pipeline_registry) -> None:
    """16. ``role`` omitted → retrieved from the node's CPD constructor.

    One case per default_role the pipeline ships, so the mapping is pinned end
    to end (schema node → registry entry → resolved role), not just spot-checked.
    """
    cases = {
        ("beta", "prior_v0"): "prior_v0",
        ("normal", "prior_v0"): "prior_v0",
        ("lognormal", "prior_v0"): "prior_v0",
        ("beta", "prior"): "prior_v0",
        ("normal", "bundled"): "prior_v0",
        ("standardize", "zscore"): "standardization",
        ("transition_logits", "linear"): "structural_prereq",
        ("continuation_ratio", "segment"): "segment",
        ("dirichlet", "segment_v0"): "segment",
        ("manifestation", "mixture_mean"): "indicator_latent",
        ("normal", "observation"): "observation",
        ("beta", "observation_v0"): "observation_v0",
        ("bernoulli", "constraint_v0"): "constraint_v0",
    }
    for (family, ctor), expected in cases.items():
        node = _node({"id": "n", "cpd": {"family": family, "constructor": ctor}})
        assert resolve_role(node) == expected, f"{family}.{ctor}"

def test_hand_assigned_role_overrides_default(_pipeline_registry) -> None:
    """17. ``role`` hand-assigned → overrides the constructor default.

    The v0 motivating case: cov_3g/cov_4g are *indicator latents* but are built
    by a ``beta.prior_v0`` constructor (default_role ``prior_v0``); the config
    must be able to say ``role: indicator_latent`` and have it stick.
    """
    node = _node(
        {
            "id": "cov_3g",
            "role": "indicator_latent",
            "cpd": {"family": "beta", "constructor": "prior_v0"},
        }
    )
    assert REGISTRY["beta"]["prior_v0"].default_role == "prior_v0"
    assert resolve_role(node) == "indicator_latent"

def test_role_never_derived_from_kind(_pipeline_registry) -> None:
    """18. Guard: nothing shape-relevant hangs off ``kind``.

    ``resolve_role`` must route through ``role``/``constructor`` only. Two arms:

    - a node whose ``kind`` names a role but whose constructor's default_role
      differs resolves to the *constructor's* role, never the ``kind`` string;
    - a node with only ``kind`` set (no cpd, no role) resolves to ``None`` --
      ``kind`` is not a role fallback.
    """
    misleading_kind = _node(
        {
            "id": "n",
            "kind": "indicator_latent",
            "cpd": {"family": "beta", "constructor": "prior_v0"},
        }
    )
    assert resolve_role(misleading_kind) == "prior_v0"

    kind_only = _node({"id": "n", "kind": "prior_v0"})
    assert resolve_role(kind_only) is None

def test_population_and_segment_pull_same_complement(_pipeline_registry) -> None:
    """2. ``population`` and ``segment`` roles pull the same demographic set.

    ``population`` (hand-assigned here; no shipped constructor defaults to it)
    demands nothing, so its shape is the bare complement. ``segment``
    (``dirichlet.segment_v0``) *demands* its anchor's output axis, which is
    prepended to the complement -- the demanded ∪ complement grid of §5.
    """
    nodes = [
        {
            "id": "pop",
            "role": "population",
            "cpd": {"family": "manifestation", "constructor": "mixture_mean"},
        },
        {"id": "seg", "cpd": {"family": "dirichlet", "constructor": "segment_v0"}},

    """11. ``prior_v0`` is demanded-only by default -- no demographic complement.

    Gender is present in the universe, but a plain ``prior_v0`` node makes no
    request, so the shape pass leaves it untouched (shape stays derived
    downstream). Contrast the complement roles, which pull gender automatically.
    """
    axes = _baked_axes(

    )
    assert axes is None

def test_prior_v0_gets_the_breakdown_on_request(_pipeline_registry) -> None:
    """12. The same ``prior_v0`` node with an explicit request gets the breakdown.

    ``include_axes`` is the universal request mechanism (§5): it augments the
    role's default free set, which for ``prior_v0`` is empty -- so the shape is
    exactly the requested axis. No role-specific machinery; the same
    ``include_axes`` that augments a complement role's shape supplies the
    "demographic-on-request" here.
    """
    axes = _baked_axes(
        "th",
        [
            {
                "id": "th",
                "cpd": {"family": "normal", "constructor": "prior_v0"},
                "include_axes": ["gender"],
            }
        ],
    )
    assert axes == ["gender"]

def test_version_2_segmentation_priors_come_from_desugar_not_build(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    # Post M1/M2: desugar owns segmentation-prior synthesis for v2, so
    # theta_bias/theta_weight *are* in the built graph -- but they come from
    # desugar, not build's (still v1-gated) step 4. Spy on the build helper to
    # confirm it stays dormant while the priors still land.
    called: list[str] = []
    orig = build_module._attach_segmentation_priors

    def _spy(*args, **kwargs):
        called.append("segmentation")
        return orig(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(build_module, "_attach_segmentation_priors", _spy)

    raw = _synth_raw({"income": ["country", "year"]})
    raw["version"] = 2
    built = build_graph(GraphConfig.model_validate(raw))
    # Priors present (desugar synthesized them)...
    assert "theta_bias" in built
    assert "theta_weight" in built
    # ...but build's v1-only step 4 did not fire.
    assert called == []
    # Declared nodes still land.
    assert "seg_logits" in built

def test_version_2_skips_attach_helpers(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    calls: list[str] = []

    def _spy(name: str, orig):
        def wrapped(*args, **kwargs):
            calls.append(name)
            return orig(*args, **kwargs)

        return wrapped

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        build_module,
        "_attach_upstream_driver_pairs",
        _spy(
            "upstream",
            build_module._attach_upstream_driver_pairs,
        ),
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        build_module,
        "_attach_segmentation_priors",
        _spy(
            "segmentation",
            build_module._attach_segmentation_priors,
        ),
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        build_module,
        "_attach_observations",
        _spy("observations", build_module._attach_observations),
    )

    raw = _synth_raw({"income": ["country", "year"]})
    raw["version"] = 2
    build_graph(GraphConfig.model_validate(raw))
    # Bridge-B: step 3 (upstream _z standardizers) is intentionally ungated so
    # it backfills for v2; steps 4-5 stay v1-only (desugar owns them for v2).
    assert calls == ["upstream"]

    calls.clear()
    raw["version"] = 1
    build_graph(GraphConfig.model_validate(raw))
    assert "upstream" in calls
    assert "segmentation" in calls

@pytest.mark.filterwarnings("ignore::UserWarning")
@needs("I1", AssertionError)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "name", ["h1_supply_constrained_v4.yaml", "segmentation_child_v4.yaml"]
)
def test_autoconstruct_priors_is_a_fixed_point_too(name: str) -> None:
    """The one exception, pinned to the phase that dissolves it.

    ``_autoconstruct_priors`` mints its ``{node}__coefficient`` axis with
    ``derived_for`` and no ``axis_role`` (``desugar.py:1401``); pass 11,
    ``_assign_axis_roles``, labels it ``bespoke`` afterwards and short-circuits when
    every axis already has a role (``desugar.py:2763``). So re-running pass 5 alone
    rebuilds the axis and strips the label. Nodes and edges are untouched -- it is
    the ``axes`` mapping that differs
    (``scratchpad/probe_autoconstruct_topkey.py``).

    **I1, not a phase named after this pass.** Ruling 5 says ``autoconstruct_priors``
    stays as it is and the new flag is ``autoconstruct_obs``, so no phase owns this
    pass by name. But I1 makes axis synthesis read a per-constructor declaration of
    *name, role, and level source* (rev. 9 lines 168-174). Once the role travels with
    the declaration, a rebuild carries it and there is nothing left to clobber --
    which is the fix worth having, rather than teaching this one pass to preserve a
    field it does not know it owns.

    Only the two v4 examples that synthesize a coefficient axis are listed; on
    everything else the general test above already covers this pass.
    """
    with open(_EXAMPLES / name) as f:
        flat = desugar(GraphConfig.model_validate(YAML().load(f)))
    pass_fn = dict(_passes_for(4))[_KNOWN_NOT_FIXED]
    assert pass_fn(flat) == flat

def test_has_explicit_observation_nodes() -> None:
    # Pinned to ``version: 1``, the tier current when this landed (2026-06-26,
    # three weeks before the version gate existed). Riding ``LATEST_VERSION`` it
    # had drifted to v4, where the Fork-A/Type-III split it asserts is on its way
    # out: v4 routes every observation through one mechanism regardless of the
    # ``sample`` site's shape (E's tuple addressing; B7's intention). So this pins
    # <=v3 wiring, which stays as pinned -- and B5, which is about the fork being
    # *misdetected* at v4, owns the v4 arm for as long as the fork survives there.
    #
    # Two independent detection axes after the M2/T4 merge:
    #   * obs-ness (build-time auto-attach gate) is read off the registry
    #     ``binds_data`` bit -- so a node needs a data-binding cpd, and the
    #     registry must be populated first (the M2 successor to the retired
    #     ``observation``-kind prefix rule);
    #   * Fork-A fit routing keys on the ``observation_v0`` kind marker, which
    #     ``binds_data`` cannot distinguish from Type-III on its own.
    # Real obs nodes (Fork-A and Type-III alike) always carry a cpd, so the two
    # axes agree on every example config; they only diverge on Fork-A vs
    # Type-III, which is exactly what ``has_observation_v0_nodes`` isolates.
    register_pipeline_cpds()
    fork_a = GraphConfig.model_validate(
        {
            "version": 1,
            "nodes": [
                {
                    "id": "cov_3g_obs",
                    "kind": "observation_v0",
                    "cpd": {"family": "beta", "hyperparameters": {"concentration": 50.0}},
                }
            ]
        }
    )
    type_iii = GraphConfig.model_validate(
        {
            "version": 1,
            "nodes": [
                {"id": "cov_3g_obs", "cpd": {"family": "normal", "constructor": "observation"}}
            ],
        }
    )
    latent_only = GraphConfig.model_validate(
        {"version": 1, "nodes": [{"id": "cov_3g", "kind": "prior"}]}
    )

    # Both obs shapes bind data -> the build-time gate suppresses auto-attach.
    assert has_declared_observation_nodes(fork_a) is True
    assert has_declared_observation_nodes(type_iii) is True
    assert has_explicit_observation_nodes(type_iii) is True  # backward-compat alias
    assert has_declared_observation_nodes(latent_only) is False

    # Fork-A fit routing keys on the observation_v0 marker, not on binds_data.
    # Asserted on the marker test itself rather than on the routing predicate,
    # which takes a graph: these three configs exist to isolate the *spellings*,
    # and building a graph from each would add axis scaffolding that says nothing
    # about the distinction. The routing predicate is pinned over real configs in
    # ``test_b5_fork_a_routing.py``.
    def _marks(cfg: GraphConfig) -> bool:
        return any(
            names_fork_a_site(n.kind, n.cpd.constructor if n.cpd else None)
            for n in cfg.nodes
        )

    assert _marks(fork_a) is True
    assert _marks(type_iii) is False
    assert _marks(latent_only) is False

@needs("H1", NotImplementedError)
def test_demo_pipeline_builds_and_fits(data_path: Path, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Both artifacts, asked for together -- the workbook is no longer a default.

    Pinned to H1 since 2026-08-27: the demo's ``income`` carries a ``from_data``
    population pointer (``demo_v0.yaml:108``) and the writer has no form for a
    weight array that is loaded data rather than a node, so ``save_result``
    refuses. Kept whole rather than run with serialization off, because the
    serialized directory is most of what this asserts. See
    ``docs/sketches/20260826_population_pointer_is_live_on_the_demo_path.md``.

    ``write_summary`` is off unless requested, so this names it; ``write_serialized``
    is on by default and is left implicit, which is what pins the default. Then the
    serialized directory is checked for the three things it has to be: a manifest, a
    ``run_info.yaml`` saying where the fit came from, and a faithful round trip that
    the second of those does not disturb.
    """
    result = run_pipeline_from_paths(
        DEMO_YAML,
        data_path=data_path,
        out_dir=tmp_path / "out",
        steps=25,
        seed=0,
        write_summary=True,
    )
    assert result.output_path is not None
    assert result.output_path.is_file()
    assert result.output_path.parent == tmp_path / "out"
    assert result.serialized_dir is not None
    assert (result.serialized_dir / "manifest.yaml").is_file()
    assert result.serialized_dir.parent == tmp_path / "out"

    # Provenance beside the manifest, and the same facts the workbook's `run_info`
    # sheet gets -- one `_run_info` dict feeds both.
    info = yaml.safe_load((result.serialized_dir / RUN_INFO_NAME).read_text())
    assert info["seed"] == 0
    assert info["steps"] == 25
    assert Path(info["config"]) == DEMO_YAML
    assert Path(info["data"]) == data_path
    assert info["generated_at"]

    # The unlisted file does not disturb the round trip: `load_result` reads only
    # what the manifest names, which is what makes it safe to write anything else
    # into the directory at all.
    reloaded = load_result(result.serialized_dir)
    for node, array in result.result.posterior.items():
        np.testing.assert_allclose(reloaded.posterior[node].values, array.values)
    losses = result.result.losses
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(losses))
    shares = result.result.posterior["segment_shares"].isel(chain=0, draw=0).values
    np.testing.assert_allclose(shares.sum(axis=-1), 1.0, atol=1e-5)

@needs("H1", AssertionError)
def test_cli_main_demo(data_path: Path, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """A bare terminal run: the serialized directory, and only that.

    ``AssertionError`` rather than ``NotImplementedError``: the refusal happens
    in a subprocess, so what reaches the pin is the return-code assertion below
    carrying that traceback as its message. Same H1 cause as
    ``test_demo_pipeline_builds_and_fits``.

    `main` prints one line per artifact written, serialized first. Nothing is
    passed but paths and steps, so what comes back is the default answer to "we
    rocked up and fit the model" -- a round-trip result, no workbook. The
    workbook variant is the next test.
    """
    proc = _run_cli(DEMO_YAML, data_path, tmp_path / "cli_out")
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr
    lines = proc.stdout.split()
    assert len(lines) == 1
    result_dir = Path(lines[0])
    assert (result_dir / "manifest.yaml").is_file()

@needs("H1", AssertionError)
def test_cli_main_demo_with_summary(data_path: Path, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """`--summary` adds the workbook without displacing the serialized directory.

    Pinned to H1 for the same reason as the two above.

    The two artifacts are independent options, so asking for one does not turn
    the other off. Order of the printed lines is serialized then summary.
    """
    proc = _run_cli(DEMO_YAML, data_path, tmp_path / "cli_out", "--summary")
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr
    result_dir, workbook = (Path(line) for line in proc.stdout.split())
    assert (result_dir / "manifest.yaml").is_file()
    assert workbook.is_file()
    assert workbook.suffix == ".xlsx"

def test_auto_attach_path_uses_gated_loader_values(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Auto-attach turns a bare ``beta`` prior into a fitted observation sink.

    Pinned to ``version: 1``, the tier current when this test was written
    (2026-06-26) -- which is to say, before config versioning existed at all
    (the gate landed with M0, ``a0d72d2``, 2026-07-17). Omitting ``version``
    therefore left it riding ``LATEST_VERSION``, and it was silently re-pointed
    at v2, then v3, then v4 as each tier landed, without anyone editing it. A
    test's pin should not move under our own version bumps.
    """
    path = tmp_path / "beta_only.xlsx"
    pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {
                "indicator_code": "cov_3g",
                "source_code": "GSMAINT",
                "country_iso3": "AAA",
                "year": 2020,
                "gender": "T",
                "urban_rural": "T",
                "age_group": "T",
                "unit": "pct",
                "value": 50.0,
                "obs_status": "A",
                "geo_level": "national",
            }
        ]
    ).to_excel(path, index=False)
    raw = {
        "version": 1,
        "axes": {
            "country": {"levels": ["AAA"], "kind": "categorical"},
            "year": {"levels": [2020], "kind": "ordinal"},
        },
        "nodes": [

def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):

        "iframe",

def test_inference_recovers_demo_gender_axis() -> None:
    """The theta-stripped demo synthesizes ``gender`` axes with no hard-code.

    ``demo_v0_stripped_nosign``'s shape: income carries ``gender``, the coverage
    drivers do not, so ``B = union − intersection = {gender}``. This is the
    load-bearing regression — the heuristic must reproduce the demo's
    ``(gender, transition, driver)`` / ``(gender, transition)`` theta axes that
    used to be spelled out in ``build.py``.
    """
    panel = _panel()
    resolver = make_observation_resolver(_loaded_from_panel(panel))
    raw = YAML().load(open(DEMO_YAML))
    theta_ids = {"theta_bias", "theta_weight"}
    raw["nodes"] = [n for n in raw["nodes"] if n["id"] not in theta_ids]
    raw["edges"] = [e for e in raw["edges"] if not (e[0] in theta_ids and e[1] == "seg_logits")]

    built = build_graph(GraphConfig.model_validate(raw), data_resolver=resolver)
    assert _axis_names(built, "theta_bias") == ("gender", "transition")
    assert _axis_names(built, "theta_weight") == ("gender", "transition", "driver")

def test_infer_empty_B_single_driver() -> None:

def test_signed_weight_loc_multi_axis() -> None:
    """Signed-driver loc is built over the full ``(*B, transition, driver)`` grid.

    With two disaggregation axes (``|B| = 2``) the loc is a dense 4-D array; a
    signed driver's slice must carry ``±m`` across every B/transition cell. This
    exercises the ``|B| != 1`` path the old hard-coded single-gender-axis builder
    could not reach.
    """
    raw = _synth_raw(
        {"d1": ["country", "year", "gender"], "d2": ["country", "year", "urban_rural"]}
    )
    for node in raw["nodes"]:
        if node["id"] == "d1":
            node["extra"] = {"sign": "positive"}
        elif node["id"] == "d2":
            node["extra"] = {"sign": "negative", "sign_loc": 2.0}
    built = build_graph(GraphConfig.model_validate(raw))

    tw = built.get("theta_weight")
    axes = tw.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["axes"]
    assert tuple(a.name for a in axes) == ("gender", "urban_rural", "transition", "driver")

    loc = np.asarray(tw.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["loc"])
    assert loc.shape == (2, 2, 2, 2)  # gender x urban_rural x transition(=K-1) x driver
    driver_pos = next(i for i, a in enumerate(axes) if a.name == "driver")
    driver_levels = axes[driver_pos].levels
    d1_slice = np.take(loc, driver_levels.index("d1"), axis=driver_pos)
    d2_slice = np.take(loc, driver_levels.index("d2"), axis=driver_pos)
    assert np.allclose(d1_slice, 1.0)  # positive, default magnitude
    assert np.allclose(d2_slice, -2.0)  # negative, sign_loc override

def test_anchor_found_by_descriptor_not_family_string() -> None:
    """A *renamed* segmentation family is still found, and drives synthesis.

    The registry entry for ``transition_logits`` is aliased under a new family
    name that build has never heard of. If anchor-finding still keyed on the
    literal ``"transition_logits"`` string this config would not be recognized as
    a segmentation anchor and *nothing* would be synthesized. Because detection is
    by the ``SegmentationAnchor`` descriptor, the structural axes are still
    inferred and the priors synthesized -- proving the family string is no longer
    load-bearing for anchor detection.

    The node ids stay ``theta_*``: the alias copies the transition entry's
    ``SegmentationAnchor``, which sets ``legacy_theta_prior_ids=True``, so its
    ``biases``/``weights`` still resolve through ``_BRIDGE_NODE_IDS`` to
    ``theta_bias``/``theta_weight``. (A paradigm without that opt-in gets the
    general ``{anchor_id}_{role}`` id -- see the §6 Dirichlet tests.)
    """
    from digital_readiness.core.cpd import REGISTRY

    REGISTRY["alt_seg"] = dict(REGISTRY["transition_logits"])

    raw = _synth_raw({"d1": ["country", "year"]})
    for node in raw["nodes"]:
        if node["id"] == "seg_logits":
            node["cpd"]["family"] = "alt_seg"

    built = build_graph(GraphConfig.model_validate(raw))

    assert "theta_bias" in built
    assert "theta_weight" in built
    assert _axis_names(built, "theta_bias") == ("transition",)
    assert _axis_names(built, "theta_weight") == ("transition", "driver")

def test_dirichlet_synthesized_shapes(_dirichlet_config) -> None:
    """Shapes come from the Dirichlet ``ParamDecl.axes`` with B (=∅ here) prepended.

    ``biases.axes == ("segment_axis",)`` -> ``(segment,)`` and
    ``weights.axes == ("segment_axis","driver_axis")`` -> ``(segment, driver)``.
    The config is genderless and both drivers share ``country``, so B is empty and
    ``weights`` stays 2-D (the gendered einsum path is untouched). The ``segment``
    axis has K=4 levels -- the Dirichlet ``output_length_from_k = k`` (K, not the
    logit paradigm's K-1).

    assert weights_levels["segment"] == biases_levels["segment"]
    assert weights_levels["driver"] == ("x1", "x2")

def _get(config: GraphConfig, node_id: str):
    return next((n for n in config.nodes if n.id == node_id), None)

def _eg(**block) -> dict:
    """A ``mean_coeffs`` priors block disaggregated over both demographic axes.

    v3 retired the old "B" inference in favour of declaring disaggregation with
    ``include_axes``, so a config that wants a *multi-atom* effect group has to
    say so — under both versions. Without it the role is one Cartesian atom and
    there is nothing to bundle.
    """
    return {"mean_coeffs": {"include_axes": ["gender", "country"], **block}}

def _eg_atoms(key: str = "*", **block) -> dict:
    """The same block, but with ``block`` describing the *atoms*.

    Under v4 ``priors.<role>`` describes the node the role binds to, which for an
    effect group is the combiner; every node in the graph is addressable, so an
    atom is addressed where it sits -- one hop down, under the combiner's own
    ``atoms`` role, keyed by additive axis (``"*"`` = all of them).
    """
    return _eg(cpd={"priors": {"atoms": {key: block}}})

def test_co_bundled_priors_come_out_as_separate_nodes_with_their_own_axes() -> None:
    """Item 4. One consumer's effect group is N atoms, not one merged node."""
    out = desugar(
        _cfg(
            [_truncated("mob", priors=_eg()), _latent("income")],
            edges=[["income", "mob"]],
        )
    )
    members = _members(out, _TYPE_I)
    # One atom per additive (demographic) axis, each carrying the Cartesian
    # coefficient axis plus its own additive axis -- not one flat vector.
    assert set(members) == set(_MOB_ATOMS)
    for node_id, axis in zip(_MOB_ATOMS, ["gender", "country"]):
        axes = members[node_id].cpd.hyperparameters["axes"]
        assert axes[-1] == axis
        # Its own axes, not the group's: no shared bundle axis anywhere.
        assert all("bundle" not in str(a) for a in axes)
    # No merged node, and nothing carries the v<=3 parallel-array surface.
    assert _get(out, "normal_bundled_type_i") is None
    assert all("entries" not in (n.cpd.hyperparameters if n.cpd else {})
               for n in out.nodes)

def test_each_consumers_declared_hyperparameters_survive_on_its_own_nodes() -> None:
    """Item 5. The old bug: the second consumer's ``scale`` silently discarded.

    v<=3 needed parallel per-entry arrays to keep both, because both consumers'
    atoms lived in one node. Here each consumer's atoms are its own nodes, so
    each simply carries its own scalar -- there is nothing to merge and no order
    to align.
    """
    out = desugar(
        _cfg(
            [
                _truncated("mob", priors=_eg_atoms(cpd={"hyperparameters": {"scale": 0.5}})),
                _truncated("smart", priors=_eg_atoms(cpd={"hyperparameters": {"scale": 9.0}})),
                _latent("income"),
            ],
            edges=[["income", "mob"], ["income", "smart"]],
        )
    )
    members = _members(out, _TYPE_I)
    scales = {node_id: n.cpd.hyperparameters["scale"] for node_id, n in members.items()}
    assert scales == {
        "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender": 0.5,
        "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_country": 0.5,
        "smart_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender": 9.0,
        "smart_mean_coeffs_atoms_country": 9.0,
    }
    # Scalars, not per-entry vectors: `scale: [a, b]` no longer means "one per
    # atom", it means a per-cell array on that one atom.
    assert all(not isinstance(v, list) for v in scales.values())

def test_nothing_is_bundled_unless_something_says_so() -> None:
    """Item 6. Absent ``bundle_id`` means solo; there is no implicit bundling.

    Two same-family roots that v<=3-style coalescing might have been tempted to
    merge stay separate, and so do the deterministic nodes the walk interposes.

    Nothing here is bundled at all -- not even the effect group, because with no
    ``include_axes`` it has no additive axes, so its fan-out resolves to an empty
    key set (Part 3a): one ordinary prior, no siblings to share a site with and no
    combiner to sum. A group of one is not a group; a bundle of one is not a
    bundle. (Contrast ``_eg()``, which declares the disaggregation.)
    """
    out = desugar(
        _cfg([_latent("income"), _latent("wealth"), _truncated("mob")],
             edges=[["income", "mob"], ["wealth", "mob"]])
    )

    coeffs = _get(out, "mob_mean_coeffs")
    assert coeffs.cpd.constructor == "prior_v0" and coeffs.cpd.family == "normal"
    # No combiner anywhere: the role's own prior *is* what the consumer binds.
    assert all((n.cpd.family if n.cpd else None) != "effect_group" for n in out.nodes)
    assert _get(out, "mob").cpd.parameter_bindings["mean_coeffs"] == ["mob_mean_coeffs"]

def test_auto_construction_groups_the_same_members_the_node_id_key_did() -> None:
    """Item 7. Same members *as a set* as the v3 shared-node key produced.

    v3 keyed the shared node by ``{family}_{constructor}_type_i``; v4 keys the
    shared *site* by the same formula. Order is deliberately not asserted: it is
    unobservable in the emitted config, and Part 3's one-site draw only requires
    that it be deterministic, not that it match v3's.
    """
    nodes = [
        _truncated("mob", priors=_eg()),
        _truncated("smart", priors=_eg()),
        _latent("income"),
    ]
    edges = [["income", "mob"], ["income", "smart"]]
    v4 = desugar(_cfg(nodes, edges=edges, version=4))
    v3 = desugar(_cfg(nodes, edges=edges, version=3))

    v3_entries = _get(v3, "normal_bundled_type_i").cpd.hyperparameters["entries"]
    # v3's members are (consumer, role, axis) entries inside one node; v4's are
    # nodes. Compare the (consumer, additive axis) identity they both carry.
    # v3 labelled entries by the interposed sum node's id (``{stem}_effect_sum``);
    # v4 derives ids uniformly, so the combiner is just ``{stem}``. Compare stems.
    v3_ids = {
        (e["consumer_id"].removesuffix("_effect_sum"), e["axes"][-1])
        for e in v3_entries
    }
    v4_ids = {
        (n.id.removesuffix(f"_atoms_{n.cpd.hyperparameters['axes'][-1]}"),
         n.cpd.hyperparameters["axes"][-1])
        for n in _members(v4, _TYPE_I).values()
    }
    assert v4_ids == v3_ids

def test_two_entries_for_one_bundle_are_refused_by_the_loader() -> None:
    """17n. Keying by bundle id is what makes this unrepresentable.

    And the refusal is better than unrepresentable-by-overwrite: ``ruamel.yaml``
    raises before the schema is reached, naming *both* conflicting values. That
    is the reason this section is a mapping and not a list -- a list would make
    the duplicate representable and the disagreement a rule to enforce.
    """
    from io import StringIO

    from ruamel.yaml import YAML
    from ruamel.yaml.constructor import DuplicateKeyError

    document = (
        "bundles:\n"
        "  b1:\n"

        "    distribution: numpyro.distributions.LogNormal\n"

def _register_scratch_families() -> None:
    """Two fan-out consumers with no demographic or effect-group content.

    Desugar-only: the constructor fns are never called (the walk consults
    schemas, not fns). The point of their existing is that ``fan_out`` is
    reusable -- ``f_lags`` is the AR(p) shape (n parents, one per lag index),
    ``f_split`` is the shape where the keys are axis names but nothing is summed.
    """

    def _fn(*args, **kwargs):
        raise AssertionError("scratch test CPD must never be constructed")

    def _resolve(**kwargs):
        return {}

    register_cpd(
        "f_lags",
        "v0",
        _fn,
        kind="stochastic",
        parameter_schema={
            # One coefficient per lag: the count is a hyperparameter of *this*
            # node, and the keys are indices rather than axis names.
            "coeffs": ParamDecl(
                min_count=1,
                max_count=None,
                fan_out=FanOut(over_count="order"),
                default_prior=DefaultPrior("normal", {"loc": 0.0, "scale": 1.0}),
            ),
        },
        hyperparameter_schema={"order": HyperDecl(default=1)},
        resolve_bindings=_resolve,
    )
    register_cpd(
        "f_split",
        "v0",
        _fn,
        kind="stochastic",
        parameter_schema={
            # Keys are axis names, and there is *no* combiner: the children bind
            # straight to the consumer as a tuple.
            "parts": ParamDecl(
                min_count=1,
                max_count=None,
                fan_out=FanOut(over_axes=("split_axes",)),
                default_prior=DefaultPrior("normal", {"loc": 0.0, "scale": 1.0}),
            ),
        },
        hyperparameter_schema={"split_axes": HyperDecl(default=())},
        resolve_bindings=_resolve,
    )

def _fn(*args, **kwargs):
    raise AssertionError("scratch test CPD must never be constructed")

def _resolve(**kwargs):
    return {}

def _get(config: GraphConfig, node_id: str):
    return next((n for n in config.nodes if n.id == node_id), None)

def _ids(config: GraphConfig) -> set[str]:
    return {n.id for n in config.nodes}

def _eg(*axes: str, **block) -> dict:
    return {"mean_coeffs": {"include_axes": list(axes), **block}}

def _eg_atoms(*axes: str, **by_key) -> dict:
    """``_eg``, but with the blocks describing the *atoms*.

    ``priors.<role>`` describes the node the role binds to -- for an effect group
    the combiner -- so an atom is addressed where it sits topologically: one hop
    down, under the combiner's own ``atoms`` role, keyed by additive axis. The
    reserved key ``"*"`` carries the block shared by every key.
    """
    return _eg(*axes, cpd={"priors": {"atoms": by_key}})

def test_the_number_of_children_is_a_per_node_fact() -> None:
    """Item 27. Two consumers of the same role fan out to different widths.

    The child count is not a property of the CPD family -- it is whatever *this*
    node's keys resolve to. Two consumers declaring different disaggregations get
    two and three atoms respectively, from one declaration.
    """
    out = desugar(
        _cfg(
            [
                _truncated("mob", priors=_eg("gender", "country")),
                _truncated("smart", priors=_eg("gender", "country", "region")),
                _latent("income"),
            ],
            edges=[["income", "mob"], ["income", "smart"]],
        )
    )
    ids = _ids(out)
    # Ids derive uniformly: the combiner is `{consumer}_{role}`, its atoms
    # `{combiner}_atoms_{key}`. No suffix is special-cased for being a sum.
    assert {"mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender", "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_country"} <= ids
    assert "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_region" not in ids
    assert {
        "smart_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender",
        "smart_mean_coeffs_atoms_country",
        "smart_mean_coeffs_atoms_region",
    } <= ids
    # Each child is bound to the combiner's role, in key order.
    assert _get(out, "smart_mean_coeffs").cpd.parameter_bindings["atoms"] == [
        "smart_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender",
        "smart_mean_coeffs_atoms_country",
        "smart_mean_coeffs_atoms_region",
    ]

def test_one_key_steers_one_child_and_the_shared_key_steers_the_rest() -> None:
    """Item 28. The reserved key ``"*"`` is the shared default; a named key wins.

    The layering is the whole reason the per-key blocks live *under* the role
    rather than in a wider key space on ``priors``: a role that does not fan out
    is addressed as one block, so the one-child case has exactly one spelling.
    """
    out = desugar(
        _cfg(
            [
                _truncated(
                    "mob",
                    priors=_eg_atoms(
                        "gender",
                        "country",
                        **{
                            "*": {"cpd": {"hyperparameters": {"scale": 0.5}}},
                            "country": {"cpd": {"hyperparameters": {"scale": 9.0}}},
                        },
                    ),
                ),
                _latent("income"),
            ],
            edges=[["income", "mob"]],
        )
    )
    assert _get(out, "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender").cpd.hyperparameters["scale"] == 0.5
    assert _get(out, "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_country").cpd.hyperparameters["scale"] == 9.0
    # Shared defaults that were not overridden still reach the steered child.
    assert _get(out, "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_country").cpd.hyperparameters["loc"] == 0.0

def test_a_key_this_node_does_not_have_is_loud() -> None:

        desugar(

                            "gender",

def test_an_empty_key_set_is_one_ordinary_prior() -> None:
    """Item 32. No keys means no fan-out, no children, and no combiner.

    Under the old subtraction-based computation this came out as "one Cartesian
    atom alone in a bundle", because the branch had already committed to the
    bundled path before discovering the complement was empty. Stated positively
    there is nothing to discover.
    """
    out = desugar(
        _cfg([_truncated("mob", priors=_eg()), _latent("income")], edges=[["income", "mob"]])
    )
    coeffs = _get(out, "mob_mean_coeffs")
    assert coeffs is not None and coeffs.bundle_id is None
    assert coeffs.cpd.family == "normal" and coeffs.cpd.constructor == "prior_v0"
    assert not any("effect_sum" in nid for nid in _ids(out))
    assert _get(out, "mob").cpd.parameter_bindings["mean_coeffs"] == ["mob_mean_coeffs"]

def test_fan_out_with_no_combiner_binds_the_children_directly() -> None:
    """Item 32a. A fanned-out role with no combiner is n parents, full stop.

    ``f_split`` has no ``effect_group``, no ``cartesian_axes`` and no sum node:
    the children bind straight to the consumer as a tuple. This is the evidence
    that fan-out carries no effect-group content -- the combiner is a separate
    decision, spelled as the role's ``default_prior``.
    """
    out = desugar(
        _cfg(
            [
                {
                    "id": "s",
                    "kind": "latent",
                    "cpd": {
                        "family": "f_split",
                        "constructor": "v0",
                        "hyperparameters": {"split_axes": ["gender", "country"]},
                    },
                }
            ]
        )
    )
    assert _get(out, "s").cpd.parameter_bindings["parts"] == ["s_parts_gender", "s_parts_country"]
    assert not any("effect_sum" in nid for nid in _ids(out))
    # Under `over_axes` the key is the child's own axis, beyond the shared shape.
    assert _get(out, "s_parts_gender").cpd.hyperparameters["axes"] == ["gender"]
    assert _get(out, "s_parts_country").cpd.hyperparameters["axes"] == ["country"]
    # `shared_site` defaults true: fan-out siblings are what a shared site is for.
    assert _get(out, "s_parts_gender").bundle_id == _get(out, "s_parts_country").bundle_id

def test_the_combiner_arrives_carrying_its_resolved_key_set() -> None:
    """Item 32c. The sum node's ``atoms`` role fans out from a hyperparameter.

    This is the one mechanism the general form genuinely requires: the emitted
    combiner carries its resolved additive axis list, so its ``atoms`` role can
    state its fan-out *positively* (``over_axes=("additive_axes",)``) instead of
    recomputing a complement it cannot see. Nothing asks "am I a sum node".
    """
    out = desugar(
        _cfg(
            [_truncated("mob", priors=_eg("gender", "country")), _latent("income")],
            edges=[["income", "mob"]],
        )
    )
    summed = _get(out, "mob_mean_coeffs")
    # Deterministic-ness is read off the constructor the node now names, not off
    # the `kind` marker the emission used to double as (v4 drops `kind`).
    assert (summed.cpd.family, summed.cpd.constructor) == ("effect_group", "sum")
    assert REGISTRY["effect_group"]["sum"].kind == "deterministic"
    assert summed.cpd.hyperparameters == {"additive_axes": ["gender", "country"]}
    # And no unexpanded sugar survives: the atoms are real nodes, not a `priors`
    # block waiting for a second pass.
    assert summed.cpd.priors == {}
    assert _get(out, "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender").cpd.hyperparameters["axes"] == [
        "mob__coefficient",
        "gender",
    ]

def test_everything_a_node_necessitates_is_unrolled_in_the_same_pass() -> None:
    """Item 34. A single ``desugar`` leaves no sugar for a second one to find.

    The contract is about the *walk*: when a node is expanded, the nodes whose
    existence it necessitates are enqueued and expanded later in the same pass --
    so a combiner emitted while expanding a consumer gets its own atoms before
    the walk ends. A no-op second call is how a violation would be *detected*,
    not the mechanism; asserting only idempotence would pass even if the second
    call were doing the real work.

    Deliberately more than minimal: two consumers, an authored atom-level
    override, and an authored ``bundle_id``.
    """
    cfg = _cfg(
        [
            _truncated(
                "mob",
                priors=_eg_atoms(
                    "gender",
                    "country",
                    **{
                        # The combiner is deterministic and joins no site, so the
                        # site is named on the atoms -- where the parameters are.
                        "*": {"bundle_id": "hand_rolled"},
                        "gender": {"cpd": {"hyperparameters": {"scale": 3.0}}},
                    },
                ),
            ),
            _truncated("smart", priors=_eg("gender", "country")),
            _latent("income"),
        ],
        edges=[["income", "mob"], ["income", "smart"]],
    )
    once = desugar(cfg)
    assert all(
        n.cpd is None or not n.cpd.priors for n in once.nodes
    ), "a second pass would have work to do"
    twice = desugar(once)
    assert _ids(twice) == _ids(once)
    assert [(e.parent, e.child) for e in twice.edges] == [
        (e.parent, e.child) for e in once.edges
    ]
    assert _get(twice, "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender").cpd.hyperparameters == _get(
        once, "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender"
    ).cpd.hyperparameters
    # The authored bundle_id steers the atoms (the combiner joins no site), and
    # the other consumer's atoms keep the derived default -- so the two consumers
    # are on separate sites.
    assert _get(twice, "mob_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender").bundle_id == "hand_rolled"
    assert (
        _get(twice, "smart_mean_coeffs_atoms_gender").bundle_id == "normal_prior_v0_type_i"
    )

def _entry(**kw) -> dict:

def _node_ids(cfg: GraphConfig) -> set[str]:

def _edge_pairs(cfg: GraphConfig) -> set[tuple[str, str]]:

def test_the_key_is_removed_from_the_desugared_node_not_emptied() -> None:
    """``obs`` has no counterpart in the graph, so it should not survive desugar.

    Principle 3 of ``docs/miscellaneous/20260805_desugar_overview.md``: a fully
    desugared v4 config mirrors the graph it produces. An ``obs: []`` left behind
    is a key with nothing under it, and a second spelling of "nothing" for every
    later reader to handle. Hence ``list | None`` rather than a list defaulting to
    empty -- which also means today's single-``obs:`` pin needs no restating.
    """
    flat = desugar(_cfg([_prior("cov_3g", obs=[_entry(source="itu", unit="pct")])]))
    assert next(n for n in flat.nodes if n.id == "cov_3g").obs is None

def test_an_author_writing_an_empty_list_gets_the_same_thing_as_omitting_it() -> None:
    """``obs: []`` is a statement that there are no observations, not an error.

    Normalized in the coercion so that "no observations" has one desugared
    spelling, and so the early-out in ``_expand_obs`` needs no second case.
    """
    flat = desugar(_cfg([_prior("cov_3g", obs=[])]))
    assert next(n for n in flat.nodes if n.id == "cov_3g").obs is None
    assert _edge_pairs(flat) == set()

def test_entries_are_named_from_their_source_and_unit_without_explicit_ids() -> None:
    """Identity from content, which is what makes autoconstruction possible.

    An earlier draft of this plan required an explicit ``id`` on every entry past
    the first, reasoning that an index is positional identity and ruling 12 keys
    addressing on tuples. The reasoning was right; the conclusion was not, because
    ``(source, unit)`` *is* the tuple. A generated entry has no author to name it,
    so if the pair could not name it, autoconstruction could not run at all.

    The spelling is ``{node}__{source}__{unit}__obs`` (Max, 2026-08-11). He first
    proposed leading with the *indicator* id; we tried moving indicator resolution
    ahead of ``expand_obs`` to make that possible and reverted it, because run 1
    then leaves every generated node with ``indicator=None`` and run 2 fills it in,
    breaking whole-pipeline idempotence
    (``scratchpad/probe_reorder_idempotence.py``). The node id is what pass 3 has,
    and for a latent whose id *is* its indicator code -- the common case -- the two
    spellings coincide.

    This is a **contract** pin: it names ``version: 4`` because a config author
    reads these ids, so moving it needs a ruling rather than a refactor.
    """
    flat = desugar(
        _cfg(
            [
                _prior(
                    "cov_3g",
                    obs=[
                        _entry(source="itu", unit="pct"),
                        _entry(source="gsma", unit="pct"),
                    ],
                )
            ]
        )
    )
    assert _obs_ids(flat, "cov_3g") == {
        "cov_3g__itu__pct__obs",
        "cov_3g__gsma__pct__obs",
    }

def test_a_lone_entry_with_no_source_keeps_todays_default_id() -> None:
    """The <=v3 spelling must emit the id it emits today, or configs break.

    ``{latent}_obs`` is a contract pin: it is the node id an author writes edges

    flat = desugar(_cfg([_prior("cov_3g", obs=[_entry()])]))

def test_an_entry_with_no_id_and_no_pair_alongside_another_is_refused() -> None:

    The courtesy warning says "you have wired this latent to data twice, and I

def test_every_emitted_node_inherits_the_latents_indicator() -> None:
    """The indicator is *not* assigned here, and that is the design.

    ``_expand_obs`` (pass 3) mints ids; ``_resolve_inherited_indicators`` assigns
    indicators, and an ``observation``-role node with exactly one parent inherits
    that parent's answer (``_INDICATOR_INHERITING_ROLES``, ``desugar.py:2508``).
    Each entry emits a node with exactly one parent -- the latent -- so the
    inheritance covers a list of entries with no change to pass 8 at all. That is
    the load-bearing reason B1 names ids from the node id rather than the
    indicator: the id is what pass 3 has, and the indicator arrives later by a
    route that already works.

    Asserted with an ``indicator:`` that differs from the node id, since a config
    whose latent id *is* its sheet code cannot tell inheritance from the fallback.
    """
    flat = desugar(
        _cfg(
            [
                _prior(
                    "income",
                    indicator="dispinc_pc",
                    obs=[
                        _entry(source="wb", unit="usd"),
                        _entry(source="oecd", unit="usd"),
                    ],
                )
            ]
        )
    )
    emitted = _obs_ids(flat, "income")
    assert len(emitted) == 2
    by_id = {n.id: n for n in flat.nodes}
    assert {by_id[obs_id].indicator for obs_id in emitted} == {"dispinc_pc"}

def test_a_familyless_entry_cpd_is_refused_at_validation_not_at_desugar() -> None:
    """``ObsEntryDef`` should not be a weaker copy of the ``NodeDef`` slice it lowers to.

    Before B1 the overlap was borrowed late and by accident. ``ObsEntryDef.cpd`` is
    a ``CpdSpecDef``, whose ``family`` is optional at the type level so the one
    model can also serve as a ``priors.<role>.cpd`` override fragment. The
    requirement that a *node's* cpd name its family lived only on ``NodeDef``, and
    the obs cpd met it only because ``_expand_obs`` happens to build a real
    ``NodeDef(...)``. Measured (``scratchpad/probe_obsdef_nodedef_overlap.py``):
    validation **accepted** a familyless obs cpd, and desugar then rejected it with
    a message naming ``cov_3g_obs`` -- a node the author never wrote -- and calling
    it "a node's cpd", which the author wrote as an obs block.

    Two costs, and they are the general shape of the duplication risk rather than
    this one field: the error arrives at the wrong surface, and any *future*
    ``NodeDef`` validator applies to obs entries silently, or fails to, depending
    only on whether ``_expand_obs``'s constructor call happens to route through it.
    B1's fix is ``_require_cpd_family``: one module-level helper called by both
    models, so the rule is borrowed deliberately from one source of truth rather
    than inherited by construction, and each call site reports the surface the
    author actually wrote.

    Written in the **single-mapping** form on purpose. When this test was pinned,
    the list form failed on the old ``obs`` type -- which was B1's other pin and
    said nothing about where the family check lives. The mapping form validated
    both before and after B1, so the only thing this test can fail on is the claim
    it is making.
    """
    familyless = {
        "cpd": {
            "constructor": "observation_v0",
            "hyperparameters": {"concentration": 50.0},
        }
    }
    try:
        _cfg([_prior("cov_3g", obs=familyless)])
    except ValidationError as exc:
        assert "family" in str(exc)
    else:
        raise AssertionError(
            "validation accepted a familyless obs cpd; the refusal arrives from "
            "desugar instead, naming the synthesized node 'cov_3g_obs'"
        )

@needs("D2", ValidationError)
def test_an_entry_with_a_unit_and_no_cpd_is_filled_from_the_units_preset() -> None:
    """The autofill B1 keeps ``cpd`` required *until*, pinned rather than prosed.

    Max's draft builds a global unit→CPD map -- user specs first, presets where a
    unit has none, an error where there is no preset either -- then fills every
    incomplete entry from it. None of that machinery exists: this is roadmap D2,
    along with the open question of who authors the missing presets and the
    wrinkle that ``UnitBundleDef`` is ``extra="forbid"`` with only
    ``family``/``site``.

    So the requirement stays, and this test is the record of what is meant to
    replace it. It fails today at exactly that requirement, and ``pytest -m needs
    -k D2`` is the answer to "what did we promise D2 would do".
    """
    flat = desugar(_cfg([_prior("cov_3g", obs=[{"source": "itu", "unit": "pct"}])]))
    obs_id = next(iter(_obs_ids(flat, "cov_3g")))
    emitted = next(n for n in flat.nodes if n.id == obs_id)
    assert emitted.cpd is not None
    assert emitted.cpd.family is not None

def _resolver():
    return make_observation_resolver(_loaded_from_panel(_panel()))

def _built(path: Path):
    return build_graph(_load(path), data_resolver=_resolver())

def _constructors(graph) -> dict[str, tuple[str | None, str | None]]:
    """node_id -> (family, constructor), reading the constructor wherever spelled.

    ``<=v3`` puts it in ``kind``, v4 in ``cpd.constructor``; build-synthesized
    nodes carry a structural ``kind`` and no constructor at either version.
    """
    out = {}
    for meta in graph.nodes():
        spec = meta.cpd_spec
        family = None if spec is None else spec.family
        constructor = None if spec is None else spec.constructor
        out[meta.node_id] = (family, constructor or meta.kind)
    return out

def test_declared_chain_builds_the_same_graph_as_the_tag() -> None:
    """The whole point of the gate: nothing is lost by not reading the tag."""
    tagged, declared = _built(TAGGED_V2), _built(DECLARED_V4)

    assert _constructors(tagged) == _constructors(declared)
    assert _edges(tagged) == _edges(declared)
    # Named explicitly, so a graph that matched by both twins losing the chain
    # could not pass.
    for z_id, driver in zip(_Z_IDS, _DRIVERS):
        assert z_id in declared
        assert declared.parents(z_id) == (driver,)
        assert "seg_logits" in declared.children(z_id)

def test_declared_chain_yields_the_same_driver_axis_levels() -> None:
    """The second, independent tag reader: the ``driver`` axis of ``theta_weight``.

    Order matters -- it indexes the weight coefficients. The tag left it to
    ``nodes`` declaration order; declaring the parents fixes it outright.
    """
    tagged = desugar(_load(TAGGED_V2))
    declared = desugar(_load(DECLARED_V4))
    assert infer_driver_levels(tagged, _anchor(tagged)) == _DRIVERS
    assert infer_driver_levels(declared, _anchor(declared)) == _DRIVERS

def test_declared_chain_reaches_the_same_map_optimum() -> None:
    """Same posterior mode, which is what proves the ``sign`` steering survived.

    ``sign: positive`` is *not* gated: ``signed_weight_loc_from_extra`` reads it
    off whichever roots the chain identifies as drivers, so once the chain is
    declared the steering follows. A prior that steered differently would move the
    mode.

    Asserted at the optimum rather than per step: MAP init is seed- *and*
    shape-dependent, and the twins' theta arrays are transposes of one another, so
    their loss *trajectories* legitimately differ (the same v2 config inits at
    468.4 on seed 0 and 673.4 on seed 1).
    """
    panel = _panel()
    obs = demo.demo_observations(panel)
    resolver = make_observation_resolver(_loaded_from_panel(panel))

    finals = []
    for path in (TAGGED_V2, DECLARED_V4):
        built = build_graph(_load(path), data_resolver=resolver)
        losses = run_map(compile_model(built), built, obs, steps=1500, seed=0).losses
        finals.append(float(losses[-1]))

    assert finals[0] == pytest.approx(finals[1], abs=1e-3)

def _tagged_upstream_raw(version: int) -> dict:
    raw = _drop_upstream_driver_pairs(_demo_raw())
    raw["version"] = version
    return raw

def _aliased_downstream_raw(version: int) -> dict:
    """The demo, with ``manifestation_role: profile`` swapped for the <=v3 alias.

    The demo itself carries the intended ``manifestation_role: profile``, which is
    *not* gated -- only the ``indicator_role: downstream`` alias is. The mean's
    edges to its obs/constraint children go too, so the v4 build (where no mean is
    synthesized) has no dangling edge and can be inspected directly.

    Cutting those edges orphans the mean's observation sinks, so they are dropped
    with it -- finishing what ``_drop_downstream_manifestation_pairs`` starts. B3
    (2026-08-12) is what surfaced them: an ``observation_v0`` node inherits its
    ``indicator`` from its parents, and with no parents there is nothing to
    inherit, which now raises. Before B3 the two fell back to their own node ids
    and asked the sheet for ``mobinet_obs`` rows, which do not exist -- so they
    were already meaningless here, just silently. Neither half of this pair reads
    them: the assertions are on whether the *means* appear.
    """
    raw = _drop_downstream_manifestation_pairs(_demo_raw())
    mean_ids = {"mobinet_mean", "smartphone_mean"}
    orphaned = {e[1] for e in raw["edges"] if e[0] in mean_ids} - {
        e[1] for e in raw["edges"] if e[0] not in mean_ids
    }
    raw["edges"] = [e for e in raw["edges"] if e[0] not in mean_ids]

def test_probability_is_the_penalty_hinge() -> None:
    """8. p = sigmoid(t·v); the site is a Bernoulli (logits-parameterized, so
    nothing saturates) whose log-prob at the observed 0 equals log(1 - p) =
    -softplus(t·v) -- finite for every finite violation."""
    violations = jnp.asarray([-10.0, -0.1, 0.0, 0.1, 10.0])
    site = dist.Bernoulli(logits=_penalty_logits(violations, _TIGHTNESS))
    log_prob = np.asarray(site.log_prob(jnp.zeros_like(violations)))
    # Never a zero-probability region: float32 sigmoid would saturate to
    # exactly 1.0 at t·v = 500 and make log(1 - p) = -inf; the logits path
    # keeps it finite (and exact: -softplus(500) = -500).
    assert np.isfinite(log_prob).all()
    # <= 0, not < 0: a deeply-satisfied cell's true penalty (-e^-500)
    # underflows to -0.0, which is the harmless side of the guarantee.
    assert (log_prob <= 0.0).all()
    assert log_prob[-1] == pytest.approx(-_TIGHTNESS * 10.0, rel=1e-6)

    capture = _CapturingSample()
    pi = np.array([[0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1], [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]])
    _call(
        _shares(pi),
        _cov(np.array([0.5, 0.5])),
        sample_fn=capture,
        lower_spec={"axis": "segment", "levels": ("S3", "S4")},
    )
    assert capture.name == "constraint"
    # dist.Bernoulli is a factory; logits parameterization -> BernoulliLogits.
    assert isinstance(capture.distribution, dist.BernoulliLogits)
    expected_logits = _TIGHTNESS * (pi[:, 2:].sum(axis=1) - 0.5)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        np.asarray(capture.distribution.logits), expected_logits, atol=1e-5
    )
    expected_p = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-expected_logits))
    log_prob = np.asarray(capture.distribution.log_prob(jnp.zeros(2)))
    np.testing.assert_allclose(log_prob, np.log1p(-expected_p), rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)

def test_penalty_shape() -> None:
    """9. log(1 - p) is ~0 when strongly satisfied, log(0.5) at equality,
    large-negative when strongly violated, monotone in the violation."""
    grid = jnp.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 21)
    site = dist.Bernoulli(logits=_penalty_logits(grid, _TIGHTNESS))
    log_prob = np.asarray(site.log_prob(jnp.zeros_like(grid)))
    assert log_prob[0] == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1e-6)  # violation -0.5: no penalty
    assert log_prob[10] == pytest.approx(np.log(0.5), abs=1e-6)  # equality
    assert log_prob[-1] == pytest.approx(-25.0, abs=1e-4)  # -softplus(50 * 0.5)
    assert np.isfinite(log_prob).all()
    assert (np.diff(log_prob) < 0).all()  # strictly decreasing

def __call__(self, name: str, distribution: dist.Distribution):
    self.name = name
    self.dist = distribution
    # Wrap in a jnp array: the real wrapper always returns a jnp array
    # (sampled or observed value), whereas a scalar ``Beta.mean`` is a bare
    # Python float, which StructuredArray rejects.
    return jnp.asarray(distribution.mean)

def _logits_sa(
    logits: np.ndarray,
    *,
    extra_axes: tuple[AxisMeta, ...] = (),
    transition_axis_pos: int = -1,
    n_transitions: int = 3,
) -> StructuredArray:
    """Build a logits ``StructuredArray`` with a length-``n_transitions`` axis.

    ``extra_axes`` are the non-transition axes (e.g. country); the transition
    axis is inserted at ``transition_axis_pos`` so tests can exercise the
    "find the axis by name, not by position" path.
    """
    transition_axis = AxisMeta(
        name="transition",
        levels=tuple(f"t{i + 1}" for i in range(n_transitions)),
        kind="ordinal",
    )
    axes = list(extra_axes)
    pos = transition_axis_pos if transition_axis_pos >= 0 else len(axes) + 1
    axes.insert(pos, transition_axis)
    return StructuredArray(
        array=jnp.asarray(logits, dtype=float),
        axes=tuple(axes),
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="logits", family="rate", unit="logit"),
        population=None,
    )

def _logit(p: float) -> float:
    return math.log(p / (1.0 - p))

def test_shares_sum_to_one() -> None:
    """Output is on the 4-simplex for ANY logit input (D12 simplex support).

    Spread the logits over several cells, including extreme values, so the
    sum-to-one property is exercised away from the symmetric r=0.5 point.
    """
    logits = np.array(
        [
            [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            [3.0, -2.0, 1.5],
            [-5.0, 4.0, -1.0],
            [10.0, 10.0, 10.0],
            [-10.0, -10.0, -10.0],
        ]
    )
    country = AxisMeta(
        name="country",
        levels=tuple(f"C{i}" for i in range(logits.shape[0])),
        kind="categorical",
    )
    out = _call(_logits_sa(logits, extra_axes=(country,)))
    sums = np.asarray(out.array).sum(axis=-1)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(sums, 1.0, atol=1e-6)
    # Every share is a genuine probability.
    assert np.all(np.asarray(out.array) >= 0.0)

def test_known_logits_hand_computed_pi() -> None:
    """For fixed (r1, r2, r3), pi matches the closed form exactly.

    Defends the exact continuation-ratio form:
        pi = (1-r1, r1(1-r2), r1 r2 (1-r3), r1 r2 r3).
    """
    r1, r2, r3 = 0.8, 0.6, 0.3
    logits = np.array([_logit(r1), _logit(r2), _logit(r3)])
    expected = np.array(
        [
            1 - r1,
            r1 * (1 - r2),
            r1 * r2 * (1 - r3),
            r1 * r2 * r3,
        ]
    )
    out = _call(_logits_sa(logits))
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.asarray(out.array), expected, atol=1e-6)

    # And the symmetric all-zero-logit case -> r=0.5 -> (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8).
    out0 = _call(_logits_sa(np.zeros(3)))
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        np.asarray(out0.array), [0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.125], atol=1e-6
    )

def test_monotone_positive_slope_shifts_mass_up() -> None:
    """Raising a transition logit moves mass toward higher segments.

    Defends the "ordinal + softly monotone for free" property. Raising r1's
    logit must (a) shrink pi_1 and (b) grow the mass above Seg 1.
    """
    base = _call(_logits_sa(np.zeros(3)))
    raised = _call(_logits_sa(np.array([2.0, 0.0, 0.0])))
    base_pi = np.asarray(base.array)
    raised_pi = np.asarray(raised.array)
    assert raised_pi[0] < base_pi[0]  # Seg 1 emptied
    assert raised_pi[1:].sum() > base_pi[1:].sum()  # mass moved up

def test_ceiling_r3_hard_negative_caps_seg4() -> None:
    """A hard-negative top-transition logit drives pi_4 -> 0.

    Defends upstream ceiling sense (a): r3 ~ 0 means mass cannot pass into
    Seg 4 ("necessary to reach 4").
    """
    out = _call(_logits_sa(np.array([0.0, 0.0, -20.0])))
    pi = np.asarray(out.array)
    assert pi[3] < 1e-6
    np.testing.assert_allclose(pi.sum(), 1.0, atol=1e-6)

def test_floor_r1_high_empties_seg1() -> None:
    """A high first-transition logit drives pi_1 -> 0.

    Defends upstream floor sense (a): r1 ~ 1 forces mass up out of Seg 1
    ("sufficient to reach 2").
    """
    out = _call(_logits_sa(np.array([20.0, 0.0, 0.0])))
    pi = np.asarray(out.array)
    assert pi[0] < 1e-6
    np.testing.assert_allclose(pi.sum(), 1.0, atol=1e-6)

    """Transform consumes the named axis even when it is not last.

def _prior_indicator() -> IndicatorMeta:
    return IndicatorMeta(indicator="__prior_bundle__", family="count", unit="1")

def _run(bundle: StructuredArray, *, consumer_id: str, role: str) -> StructuredArray:
    recorded: dict = {}

    def deterministic_fn(name: str, value):
        recorded["name"] = name
        return value

    def sample_fn(name, distribution):  # pragma: no cover - not called
        raise AssertionError("effect_group.sum is deterministic; no sample site")

    # The compile projection recovers the atoms (unbundle_all) before the CPD
    # runs; the CPD itself only sees the already-unbundled tuple.
    atoms = bundle.unbundle_all(consumer_id=consumer_id, role=role)
    out = effect_group.effect_group_sum(
        {"atoms": atoms},
        sample_fn=sample_fn,
        deterministic_fn=deterministic_fn,
        hyperparameters={},
        name="c1_effects",
    )
    assert recorded["name"] == "c1_effects"
    return out

def sample_fn(name, distribution):  # pragma: no cover - not called
    raise AssertionError("effect_group.sum is deterministic; no sample site")

def test_two_axis_effect_group_is_outer_sum() -> None:
    gender = AxisMeta(name="gender", levels=("F", "M"), kind="categorical")
    country = AxisMeta(name="country", levels=("A", "B", "C"), kind="categorical")
    g = jnp.array([1.0, 2.0])          # F, M
    c = jnp.array([10.0, 20.0, 30.0])  # A, B, C
    bundle = _bundle_from_entries(
        [
            ("c1", "effects", (gender,), g),
            ("c1", "effects", (country,), c),
        ]
    )
    out = _run(bundle, consumer_id="c1", role="effects")

    assert out.axes == (gender, country)
    # result[i, j] = gender[i] + country[j]
    expected = g[:, None] + c[None, :]
    assert jnp.allclose(out.array, expected)
    assert out.population is None

def _call(level_sa, capture=None, **hyper):
    capture = capture or _Capture()
    out = lognormal_observation_v0(
        {"level": (level_sa,)},
        sample_fn=capture,
        deterministic_fn=None,
        hyperparameters=hyper,
        name="dispinc_pc",
    )
    return out, capture

def test_positive_support() -> None:
    """1. Support is the positive reals; expected value strictly positive."""
    _, cap = _call(_level_sa(1000.0), scale=0.2)
    assert isinstance(cap.dist, dist.LogNormal)
    assert cap.dist.support is constraints.positive
    assert float(cap.dist.mean) > 0.0

def test_adds_correct_loglik_factor() -> None:
    """2. log_prob equals the analytic LogNormal(log(level), scale) log-pdf.

    Independent reference: scipy ``lognorm`` with shape s=scale, scale=exp(loc)
    = level. Mechanical wiring (right dist, right params), NOT peaks-at-observed.
    """
    level, scale, obs = 1000.0, 0.2, 1100.0
    _, cap = _call(_level_sa(level), scale=scale)
    got = float(cap.dist.log_prob(jnp.asarray(obs)))
    want = float(st.lognorm.logpdf(obs, s=scale, scale=level))
    assert got == pytest.approx(want, rel=1e-5)

    assert float(wide.dist.variance) > float(narrow.dist.variance)

def _call_prior(capture=None, **hyper):
    """Invoke ``lognormal_prior_v0`` directly with sensible hyperparameter defaults.

    The constructor reads ``loc`` / ``scale`` / ``axes`` straight from the
    hyperparameter mapping (the framework would fill schema defaults, but a
    direct body call must supply them).
    """
    capture = capture or _Capture()
    hyper.setdefault("loc", 0.0)
    hyper.setdefault("scale", 1.0)
    hyper.setdefault("axes", ())
    out = lognormal_prior_v0(
        {},
        sample_fn=capture,
        deterministic_fn=None,
        hyperparameters=hyper,
        name="dispinc_pc",
    )
    return out, capture

def test_prior_per_cell_loc_is_honored() -> None:
    """6. A per-cell ``loc`` array yields distinct per-cell medians/means."""
    country = AxisMeta(name="country", levels=("KE", "NG"), kind="categorical")
    loc, scale = [6.0, 8.0], 0.5
    out, _ = _call_prior(loc=jnp.asarray(loc), scale=scale, axes=(country,))
    # mean of LogNormal(loc, scale) = exp(loc + scale**2 / 2), elementwise.
    want = [math.exp(li + scale**2 / 2) for li in loc]
    assert out.array.shape == (2,)
    assert float(out.array[0]) == pytest.approx(want[0], rel=1e-5)
    assert float(out.array[1]) == pytest.approx(want[1], rel=1e-5)
    assert want[0] != want[1]

def test_observation_aggregates_over_declared_axes() -> None:
    """28. ``aggregate_over=("gender",)`` observes the population-weighted mean
    of the gender slices: a (country, gender) rate parent yields a (country,)
    site whose median is sum_g(level_g * pop_g) / sum_g(pop_g), per country."""
    levels = [[100.0, 200.0], [300.0, 500.0]]
    pops = [[10.0, 30.0], [20.0, 20.0]]
    parent = StructuredArray(
        array=jnp.asarray(levels),
        axes=(_COUNTRY, _GENDER),
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="dispinc_pc", family="rate", unit="level"),
        population=_pop_sa(pops, (_COUNTRY, _GENDER)),
    )
    out, cap = _call(parent, scale=0.1, aggregate_over=("gender",))
    # Hand computation: KE (100*10 + 200*30)/40 = 175; NG (300*20 + 500*20)/40 = 400.
    medians = jnp.exp(cap.dist.loc)
    assert medians.shape == (2,)
    assert float(medians[0]) == pytest.approx(175.0, rel=1e-5)
    assert float(medians[1]) == pytest.approx(400.0, rel=1e-5)
    # The observation site itself is genderless.
    assert out.axis_names == ("country",)
    assert out.array.shape == (2,)

def _shares_sa(
    array: np.ndarray,
    *,
    extra_axes: tuple[AxisMeta, ...] = (),
    segment_levels=_SEGMENTS,
    segment_pos: int = -1,
) -> StructuredArray:
    """Segment-simplex StructuredArray; segment axis inserted at ``segment_pos``."""
    seg = AxisMeta(name="segment", levels=tuple(segment_levels), kind="ordinal")
    axes = list(extra_axes)
    pos = segment_pos if segment_pos >= 0 else len(axes) + 1
    axes.insert(pos, seg)
    return StructuredArray(
        array=jnp.asarray(array, dtype=float),
        axes=tuple(axes),
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="segment_shares", family="rate", unit="share"),
        population=None,
    )

def test_mean_equals_mixture() -> None:
    """1. mean = sum_k pi_k * profile_k, hand-computed. Deterministic mean."""
    shares = np.array(
        [
            [0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.125],
            [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4],
        ]
    )
    profile = np.array([0.0, 0.2, 0.6, 0.9])
    country = AxisMeta(name="country", levels=("KE", "NG"), kind="categorical")
    out = _call(_shares_sa(shares, extra_axes=(country,)), _profile_sa(profile))
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.asarray(out.array), shares @ profile, atol=1e-6)

def test_near_zero_low_tail_gives_low_manifestation() -> None:
    """2. Profile ~0 on Seg 1-2 + mass low -> near-zero rate; mass high -> high.

    Defends downstream floor sense (b): ``#(manifestation) <= #(Seg 3-4)``.
    """
    profile = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.7, 0.95])  # near-zero low-segment tail

def _call_prior(capture=None, **hyper):
    """Invoke ``normal_prior_v0`` directly with sensible hyperparameter defaults.

    A direct body call must supply the hyperparameters the framework would
    otherwise fill from the schema defaults.
    """
    capture = capture or _Capture()
    hyper.setdefault("loc", 0.0)
    hyper.setdefault("scale", 1.0)
    hyper.setdefault("axes", ())
    out = normal_prior_v0(
        {},
        sample_fn=capture,
        deterministic_fn=None,
        hyperparameters=hyper,
        name="theta_normal",
    )
    return out, capture

def test_per_element_scale_honored_tight_vs_wide() -> None:
    """7. A tight entry and a wide entry in the same vector -> tight/wide marginals.

    The load-bearing "different prior strengths are different entries, not a
    shared prior" test: a near-zero-pinned ceiling slope ``N(0, small)`` beside a
    generic ``N(0, 1)`` income slope live in one node, with ordered variances.
    """
    param = AxisMeta(name="param", levels=("pinned", "generic"), kind="categorical")
    scale = jnp.asarray([0.01, 1.0])
    _, cap = _call_prior(loc=0.0, scale=scale, axes=(param,))
    var = cap.dist.variance
    assert var.shape == (2,)
    assert float(var[0]) < float(var[1])
    # the tight entry's sd is ~0.01, the wide entry's ~1.0 (sd**2 == variance).
    assert float(var[0]) == pytest.approx(0.01**2, rel=1e-5)
    assert float(var[1]) == pytest.approx(1.0, rel=1e-5)

def _loc(distribution):
    return _truncated(distribution).base_dist.loc

def _run(bindings, hyperparameters=None):
    captured: dict = {}

    def sample_fn(name, distribution):
        captured["name"] = name
        captured["dist"] = distribution
        return _loc(distribution)  # stand in for a draw; mean is what we test

    def deterministic_fn(name, value):  # pragma: no cover - truncated is stochastic
        raise AssertionError("normal.truncated is stochastic; no deterministic site")

    out = normal.normal_truncated(
        bindings,
        sample_fn=sample_fn,
        deterministic_fn=deterministic_fn,
        hyperparameters=hyperparameters or {},
        name="mobinet_pen",
    )
    assert captured["name"] == "mobinet_pen"
    return out, captured["dist"]

def sample_fn(name, distribution):
    captured["name"] = name
    captured["dist"] = distribution
    return _loc(distribution)  # stand in for a draw; mean is what we test

def deterministic_fn(name, value):  # pragma: no cover - truncated is stochastic
    raise AssertionError("normal.truncated is stochastic; no deterministic site")

def test_segmentation_predictor_unpacked_per_segment() -> None:
    """A predictor carrying a segment axis is unpacked: coefficient levels
    `seg_S#` each multiply the predictor's slice at segment S#, and the segment
    axis is contracted out (it does not reach the output grid)."""
    gender = AxisMeta(name="gender", levels=("F", "M"), kind="categorical")
    segment = AxisMeta(name="segment", levels=("S1", "S2"), kind="ordinal")
    # coefficient levels [bias, seg_S1, seg_S2], disaggregated by gender.
    coeffs = _coeffs(

        (gender,),
        [[0.1, 0.2],   # bias:   F, M
         [1.0, 2.0],   # seg_S1: F, M
         [3.0, 4.0]],  # seg_S2: F, M
    )

    out, d = _run({"mean_coeffs": (coeffs,), "predictors": (seg,)})

    expected = jnp.array([0.1 + 1.0 * 10.0 + 3.0 * 100.0,

    assert jnp.allclose(_loc(d), expected)

def test_segmentation_axis_is_identified_by_role_not_by_level_names() -> None:
    """A same-levels decoy axis must not be mistaken for the segment axis.

    The consumer's only evidence today is level strings, and here the two axes'
    level strings are *identical* -- so no level-naming discipline can disambiguate
    them, and nothing in B1 helps either. Declared axis order puts the decoy first,
    so the heuristic contracts `cohort` and lets `segment` ride into the output grid:
    silently, and exactly backwards.

    This is the test that shows the declaration replaced the inference rather than
    merely shadowing it.
    """
    segment = AxisMeta(
        name="segment", levels=("S1", "S2"), kind="ordinal", axis_role="segmentation"
    )
    cohort = AxisMeta(name="cohort", levels=("S1", "S2"), kind="categorical")
    coeffs = _coeffs(("bias", "seg_S1", "seg_S2"), (), [0.1, 1.0, 2.0])
    # Predictor grid is (cohort, segment) -- the decoy comes first.
    seg = _predictor("seg", (cohort, segment), [[10.0, 20.0], [30.0, 40.0]])
    out, d = _run({"mean_coeffs": (coeffs,), "predictors": (seg,)})

    # The segment axis is contracted; the decoy survives.
    assert out.axes == (cohort,)
    # mu[c] = bias + seg_S1 * P[c, S1] + seg_S2 * P[c, S2]
    expected = jnp.array([0.1 + 1.0 * 10.0 + 2.0 * 20.0,
                          0.1 + 1.0 * 30.0 + 2.0 * 40.0])
    assert jnp.allclose(_loc(d), expected)

        array=jnp.array(value),

    """Each bundled site names its cell axis ``f"{name}_cell"``, not ``"cell"``.

def test_two_bundled_sites_of_differing_arity_label_without_collision() -> None:
    """Regression: two family-bundled obs sites of different cardinality survive
    ``to_inference_data`` together.

    The bug: both bundled constructors once named their internal axis ``"cell"``,
    so a 4-cell and a 6-cell site declared the same axis with mismatched
    coordinate labels and ``inference/labeling.py`` raised
    ``ValueError: axis 'cell' appears with inconsistent coordinate labels``.
    """
    sampled = {"obs_a": _beta_obs_array("obs_a", 4), "obs_b": _beta_obs_array("obs_b", 6)}
    idata = to_inference_data(sampled)  # must not raise
    post = idata["posterior"]
    assert "obs_a_cell" in post.coords and len(post.coords["obs_a_cell"]) == 4
    assert "obs_b_cell" in post.coords and len(post.coords["obs_b_cell"]) == 6

def test_the_labeler_splits_genuinely_inconsistent_axes_by_level_set() -> None:
    """Node-scoping is a readability choice, not the only thing standing between
    two level sets and a mislabeled array.

    This once asserted a ``ValueError`` from the labeler's global consistency
    check. Phase I replaced that check: an axis name carrying two level sets is
    split into one suffixed dim per set (see
    ``tests/inference/test_i_axis_level_set_suffixes.py``), so two sites that do
    share a name survive with their own labels rather than colliding. Node
    scoping still applies first, which is why ``obs_a_cell`` reads better than a
    digest; this is the net underneath it.
    """
    shared = lambda n: StructuredArray(  # noqa: E731
        array=jnp.zeros((n,)),
        axes=(AxisMeta(name="cell", levels=tuple(range(n)), kind="ordinal"),),
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="x", family="rate", unit="fraction_observed"),
        population=None,
    )
    post = to_inference_data({"a": shared(4), "b": shared(6)})["posterior"]

    cell_dims = [name for name in post.coords if str(name).startswith("cell__")]
    assert len(cell_dims) == 2
    assert "cell" not in post.coords
    assert sorted(len(post.coords[dim]) for dim in cell_dims) == [4, 6]

def _meta(name: str) -> IndicatorMeta:
    return IndicatorMeta(indicator=name, family="count", unit="parameter")

def _normal_build(**params):
